News.title: Huge 5.7-mag earthquake hits Japan with at least 25 injured & windows shattered as locals warned of more violent tremors
News.content:
QUAKE SHOCK Huge 5.7-mag earthquake hits Japan with at least 25 injured & windows shattered as locals warned of more violent tremors







Next

AT least 25 people are injured after a powerful earthquake struck Japan this morning.

People were forced to flee buildings as the 5.7 magnitude quake shook central Japan, shattering windows and scattering glass across the street.



The Aichi Prefecture, including the city of Hamamatsu and the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara were affected.

Nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu were also hit by tremors.



The 25 injured included people who plummeted from stairs while they were trying to flee.

News.title: One dead & 20 injured after ‘impaired’ elderly driver, 76, crashes into cyclists with luxury car before ‘fleeing scene’
News.content:
FATAL RIDE One dead & 20 injured after ‘impaired’ elderly driver, 76, crashes into cyclists with luxury car before ‘fleeing scene’







Next

ONE person has died and at least 20 others are injured after an elderly man ploughed his luxury car into a group of cyclists.

Donald Robert Morris-Jones, 76, was driving a black Infiniti when he veered across the road and smashed into the group on Saturday Morning.



The bikers, from the Capital Cyclist Club were riding in the opposite direction on Optimist Farm Road, Wake County, North Carlonlina.

Morris-Jones then swerved back into his own lane and continued driving before he crashed into a ditch about half a mile away and stumbling out.



Cyclist Patrick Turner, 63, of Cary, died at the scene, and seven other people were taken to the hospital, WRAL reports.

At least 13 others sustained minor injures from the crash.



Injuries included wounds to the cyclists legs and ribs. One victim suffered a cut to the arm, according to Holly Springs Fire Department.

Morris-Jones was arrested by cops and now faces a slew of charges including driving while impaired.

The elderly man has also been charged with felony death by vehicle, seven counts of felony serious injury by vehicle, eight counts of felony hit-and-run, reckless driving and driving left of the centre.

Morris-Jones was jailed at the Wake County Detention Centre and held on a $1million bail.



According to court documents, he has no criminal record but is considered an overwhelming danger to society, WRAL reports.

The cause of the elderly man’s impairment remains unknown at this stage.

A spokesperson from the State Highway Patrol said it “cannot speculate” but “many questions” will be answered in the final crash report.

One of the cyclists told WRAL the road that the crash occurred on is a frequent route used by the cycling group.

It comes after a man allegedly ploughed into a bike race in Arizona, critically injuring six cyclists.



Shawn Michael Chock, 35, was shot by police during a confrontation after the carnage in Show Low in June 2021.

Chock was accused of driving his Ford pickup into a throng of cyclists setting off on the 55-and-over group of the annual Bike the Bluff road race.

Racer Jim Volkenant told ABC 15 that he had locked eyes with the driver.

“It was a look I will never forget,” Volenant said. “Staring like there was nothing there.”

Police caught up with Chock after he sped away and they opened fire.



Six of the injured racers were rushed to hospital by ambulance while several other victims were treated as walk-ins.

Australian cyclist Jeremy Barrett, 58, later died from his injuries.

In August Chock was charged with Barrett’s death, aggravated assault of nine other people, leaving the scene of an accident and fleeing from law enforcement.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

At sentence he received 26 years in prison.

He received 16 years for one count of second-degree murder and 10 years for felony aggravated assault. His sentences for eight other counts of aggravated assault will be served concurrently.

News.title: What time is the two minutes’ silence for Remembrance Sunday 2026 today?
News.content:
Next

THE annual observation of two minutes’ silence to remember British troops who lost their lives in conflict will take place on Remembrance Sunday.

It sees many people across the UK and the Commonwealth observe a period of silence to pay their respects to those who lost their lives.

So, what time is the period of silence and why does it take place at the same time on Remembrance Sunday each year?



Read on below for everything you need to know about Sunday’s timings.



What time is the two minute’s silence for Remembrance Sunday 2026 today?

Sunday’s two-minute silence will take place at 11am as part of Remembrance Sunday.

It is held at 11am as a nod to the armistice that marked the end of World War I.

This took effect at the “eleventh hour [French time] of the eleventh day of the eleventh month” in 1918 (on November 11 of that year).



The tradition of observing a period of silence to honour those who died in conflict began the following year, in 1919, when King George V requested Brits to do so as a mark of remembrance.

Remembrance Sunday is held annually on the second Sunday of November to allow the nation to come together as mark to pay their respects to those who died at war.

This year, it precedes Remembrance Day, which falls on Wednesday 11 November.



An additional two-minute silence will also be on that date, also taking place across the nation at 11am.

News.title: Italian foreign minister ‘targeted by pro-Putin hackers who leaked his personal info on dark web’ after Ukraine support
News.content:
HACK PROBE Italian foreign minister ‘targeted by pro-Putin hackers who leaked his personal info on dark web’ after Ukraine support







Next

A SENIOR politician has been targeted in a series of sick cyber attacks which he says have been launched over his support for Ukraine.

The personal data of Italy’s foreign minister has been plastered all over the dark web in a suspected Russian hacking spree.



Twisted fiends have also targeted the politicians’ families in a seriesof continuouss attacks over several days.

Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said: “For days now, cyber-criminals have been publishing my personal data on the dark web and seeking further information, effectively exposing me to new threats and intimidation.”



The stricken politician did not share what type of information had been maliciously disseminated.

Tajani claimed: “Our position on Ukraine is the political reason I have been targeted.

“Defending the freedom of a sovereign state, taking a clear stand in support of a nation’s democracy and independence, is dangerous in the eyes of these criminal entities.”

Italian prime minister Georgia Meloni blamed the leaks on pro-Russia hackers and swore her “full solidarity”.

She added that the sale of private information “must be tackled with the utmost determination”.

The Kremlin has not responded to the allegations.



It comes as Vladimir Putin is ramping up his shadow warfare against Europe – with fears mounting that Moscow was behind a wave of chaos at supermarkets and on passenger flights this week.

Devastating cyber attacks wiped out fridges across Europe and cost companies millions of pounds worth of damage.

And at least 24 flights were hit by bomb threats across three days of mid-air chaos – with several forced to make emergency landings.



A Russian hate group claimed responsibility for at least two incidents, allegedly threatening to “turn the skies red” in one chilling email.

Blood banks in France were also struck by cyber attacks which sent the temperatures of their life-saving stock soaring from -30 degrees celsius to over 100 degrees celsius.

The barrage of cyber crime has seen eyes swivel to the Kremlin with fears mounting that the attacks are part of Vladimir Putin‘s increasingly brazen hybrid campaign.

Experts have warned that the hacks could spark war if they continue to go unchecked.

One MP also warned that NHS blood banks and vaccine reserves are at high risk of hacks.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Graeme Downie, chair of the Coalition on Secure Technology, warned that “hostile actors” could target the UK next and urged hospitals to check the security measures on kit storing crucial medical supplies.

He added that NHS fridges were “vulnerable” to an attack like France faced “or worse”.

News.title: Three in ten kids want parents to put their phones away while a third wish mums & dads would play more, study finds
News.content:
SWIPE OUT Three in ten kids want parents to put their phones away while a third wish mums & dads would play more, study finds







Next

AROUND three in ten kids want their parents to put their phones away.

A survey by toy maker Playmobil also found 38% youngsters aged four to nine wished their mums and dads would play with them more often.



It was also revealed 15% of parents realise their child wants them to spend less time on their phones.

The findings come after five kids were appointed by Playmobil to create its Christmas advert – and they decided they wanted it to be about children calling on adults to put their phones down and play with them.



Every scene in the advert has been imagined and filmed by the children.

Delilah, aged 8, who worked on the advert, said: “We wanted to show in our advert that Christmas is much more fun when everyone plays.



“My mum does really funny voices when we play, and sometimes they’re so silly that we can’t stop laughing.

“This Christmas, I think grown-ups should put their phones away and come play with us.

“After all, a phone can’t be a princess, an astronaut or a dinosaur… well, not a very good one anyway.”

What kids want adults to do when they play with them Play with me more – 38%

Help me come up with ideas – 33%

Pretend to be a character – 31%

Put their phone away – 28%

Play with me rather than watching TV – 23%

Be more silly – 22%

Let me be messy – 22%

Start the story in a funny way – 21%

Let me play on my own – 12%

The study also found 70% of parents say using devices with screens during playtime is often the easiest option when they’re busy and their child needs entertainment.



Despite this 54% feel guilty handing a device over to their children.

Meanwhile, six in ten parents don’t think children experience boredom, thanks to devices and constant entertainment.

News.title: Lisa Nandy sparks fury from veterans and MPs after bungling Remembrance Sunday announcement
News.content:
Next

CULTURE Secretary Lisa Nandy sparked fury from veterans and MPs after bungling a Remembrance Sunday announcement.

The Tories said her tribute to the Armed Forces suggested no one in our country had fought a war since 1945.



In a press release, Ms Nandy said: “This Remembrance Sunday, we come together to reflect and honour the sacrifices our Armed Forces made in the First and Second World Wars, and continue to make today.

“We are about to raise the first generation for whom fighting a war really is part of history.



“Future generations must know the significance of those who served in our national story, that they forged a path for friendship and cooperation that meant no one in our country has had to fight a war since.”

Tory chairman Kevin Hollinrake blasted: “She seems to be saying that no one in our country has had to fight a war since 1945. Tell that to veterans of Korea, the Falklands, Northern Ireland, Iraq and Afghanistan, and to families of the hundreds who never came home. Many will be at the Cenotaph.”

Reform UK’s Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said: “This shows shameful disregard for the 7,193 British soldiers who have sacrificed their lives in conflicts since World War Two.”

Veteran Simon Weston, 65, who suffered severe burns in the Falklands War, said: “It’s tragic that somebody could be so obtuse. I am stunned.”

Sean Williams 52, who served in the Royal Logistic Corps, told The Sun: “My family fought in the Falklands. We’ve lost people. I’m speechless to be honest.”

Ex-Royal Navy seaman Maurice Quinlan, 47, who served on HMS Liverpool from 1998-2000, added: “She’s swept us all under the carpet.



“I’ve lost mates who gave their lives for our country.”

Ms Nandy’s claims about the diminishing prospect of war also appeared to contradict Government messaging on stockpiling. The Be Ready Campaign told the public to prepare for disruption caused by “hostile state actors”.

News.title: Veterans and military personnel will have rail discounts protected in law
News.content:
HEROES' DISCOUNT LAW Veterans and military personnel will have rail discounts protected in law

Source: Getty







Next

VETERANS and military personnel will have rail discounts protected in law.

Our heroes are entitled to a third off fares through a railcard, and children travelling with them get 60 per cent off.

But ministers hope that enshrining it in law will give veterans and serving members of the Armed Forces reassurance discounts will continue for generations to come.

The announcement comes after free rail travel was extended to bereaved military family members attending Remembrance events.





Rail Minister Lord Hendy told The Sun on Sunday: “They deserve our support, this Remembrance weekend and always.”

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said: “We have a moral duty to stand by our veterans and the military families who sacrifice so much.”

The King will lead the nation in two minutes’ silence at The Cenotaph today for those who have served in the Armed Forces and died in conflicts.

PM Andy Burnham said: “I want to offer my personal thanks to those who served and continue to serve.”



And Nigel Farage teared up while filming a documentary on World War One battlefields and asked cameras to stop.

The Reform UK leader said: “The process was very brutal so if you died in the war your family got one of those called the dead man’s penny.

“Very often if you see them today, they’ve got solder on the back. They were stuck above mantelpieces.

“That was what the dead soldier got…and you can stop recording now, please.”

News.title: Tory MPs launch bid to close loophole that lets sanctioned firms from Russia and Iran sponsor workers’ visas
News.content:
Next

TORY MPs are launching a bid to close a loophole that allows sanctioned firms from Russia and Iran to sponsor worker visas.

They warn that the current situation could threaten our national security and allow immigration backed by our “enemies.”



MPs have tabled an amendment to Labour’s immigration legislation to force the Home Office to remove visa sponsor licences from any individual or company under UK sanctions.

It comes after investigations earlier this year found companies under sanctions for links to the Russian and Iranian regimes were approved to sponsor worker visas.



Alicia Kearns, Shadow Security Minister, warned that Labour was leaving Britain’s backdoor “open to immigration sponsored by our enemies”.

She added: “Sanctions are supposed to punish those who threaten our national security and undermine our interests. It is therefore utterly absurd that a company can be sanctioned by Britain and still bring in workers to our country.



“The Conservatives would close this loophole. We will not allow sanctioned firms from Russia or any country to import people to our country and put our safety at risk.”

Chris Philp, Shadow Home Secretary, added: “It is ridiculous that we are handing out the right to bring foreign workers into Britain to companies that have been blacklisted by our Government.”

Russian airline Aeroflot, cryptocurrency platform Exmo Exchange and Iranian banks Melli and Persia International, were listed as holding licences to bring employees to the UK earlier this year.

The two Russian companies are no longer on the sponsor list.



Another probe also found UK subsidiaries of sanctioned Russian companies could still sponsor Russian nationals to enter the UK via the loophole.

Technically, while a company may be sanctioned for a particular activity, it does not mean that having a sponsor licence contravenes the sanction.

But the Government insisted the powers already exist to revoke a sponsor licence where an organisation is subject to sanctions.

A Home Office spokesperson said: “The power to revoke sponsorship from sanctioned companies already exists.

“We will not hesitate to act to protect the integrity of the system. More broadly, we have taken robust action against Russia and Iran.



“The UK has now sanctioned over 3,500 individuals, businesses, and ships under the Russia sanctions regime, as well as sanctioning more than 550 individuals and entities under the Iran sanctions regimes, including the IRGC in its entirety.”

News.title: Major UK suncream brand, travel agent and sports store collapse into administration
News.content:
Major UK suncream brand, travel agent and sports store collapse into administration

Popular businesses have fallen into administration

View 2 Images A number of popular businesses have entered administration (Image: Getty)

This week has seen another blow to businesses across the UK as a number of well-known names have entered administration. It has been a challenging time for businesses, with many making the tough decision to call in administrators.

‌



‌



Businesses can enter administration when they are unable to settle their debts, a situation known as insolvency. Plans to restructure the firm are developed, and an administrator from a qualified accountancy practice takes control until a new owner can be found.

‌



Administration is a lengthy procedure and can take several months. A company can be put into liquidation and shut down if there is no way to make more cash. Here are the latest businesses that have begun the process across the UK.

‌



Malibu Health Products Limited

View 2 Images A rescue deal has been secured (Image: Daily Record)

The manufacturer of the iconic Malibu suncream has entered administration. Its products, which included sun lotion and tanning oils, were stocked by major UK retailers, including Morrisons, Boots, The Range, Home Bargains, TK Maxx, Savers and Poundstretcher.

It had traded successfully for 27 years but the company entered administration on October 15, with Marco Piacquadio and Rachel Ennis of FTS Recovery Limited appointed as administrators. The administrators said a fire hit the company's trading and manufacturing warehouse on August 11, reducing vital stock, raw materials, and specialised machinery.

‌



Thankfully, a vital rescue deal has been secured. The FTS Recovery spokesperson said: "On the date of the administrators' appointment, a sale of the goodwill of the business was transferred to a new business operated by the director."

All nine head office staff are transferring to the new company with their contracts, pay, and legal workplace protections remaining intact. It added: "All manufacturing jobs (numbering around 30) that are employed by a separate company within the group have been unaffected by the administration and the transfer."

‌



Ensure our latest business headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

Wroxham Travel

Norfolk-based independent travel agency has closed after entering administration. The firm, which opened in 1987, sold customers European holidays to countries like Greece, Portugal, Italy and Spain, but also to more exotic destinations like Bali, Barbados, Thailand and Mauritius.

‌



The firm had two offices, one in Hoveton and Ayslsham, both in Norfolk. Customer advice from the Association of British Travel Agents (ABTA) has described the development as a "financial failure".

A statement from ABTA said: "We are sorry to inform you that Wroxham Travel has ceased trading with effect from 30 October 2026. We are now treating this as a financial failure. If you had booked travel arrangements with Wroxham Travel, you should follow the advice set out below.

‌



"If you booked a holiday through Wroxham Travel, the tour operator or principal business with whom Wroxham Travel booked your holiday will be named on your paperwork (or ATOL certificate if it was a flight inclusive holiday; this would be stated on your ATOL certificate under “Who is protecting your trip”).

"To ensure your holiday can continue as planned, you will need to contact the credit control department of your tour operator or other principal travel business with whom you have a contract. Your booking should continue as normal, and they will be your direct point of contact.

‌



"Please ensure that you have all your documentation with you, as they may require information from it to assist you."

J's Cycle Shack

The sports store has collapsed into administration after 12 years in business. J's Cycle Shack, which had locations in Wakefield and Epworth as well as an online store, has appointed administrators according to a notice in the Gazette.

Article continues below

The stores specialise in bikes, repairs, cycling gear and other helpful services, whilst the online store also stocked running gear, nutrition supplements, trainers and much more. The business was founded by James Wagner back in 2014, and what started as a small local bike shop turned into four stores and showrooms dotted around the country.

Currently, the stores in Wakefield, Leeds and Epworth are showing as 'temporarily closed' on Google, and the website features a message saying: "We are sorry that we're currently unavailable but, fear not, we'll be back soon."

News.title: Japan rocked by 5.7 magnitude earthquake as windows shatter and mudslide warning issued
News.content:
Japan rocked by 5.7 magnitude earthquake as windows shatter and mudslide warning issued

The 5.7 magnitude tremor struck a wide area including the cities of Kyoto and Nara, sending terrified residents fleeing from buildings and leaving at least 22 injured

View 2 Images Shattered windows are seen at a car dealer following a strong earthquake in Toyohashi, central Japan (Image: /Kyodo News via AP)

A powerful earthquake has rocked central Japan this morning, shattering shop windows and sending terrified residents fleeing from buildings, with at least 22 people injured.

‌



‌



The tremor struck across a wide area including the historic cities of Kyoto and Nara, as well as Hamamatsu and neighbouring areas. Yamanashi and Gifu were also among the locations affected.

‌



Footage broadcast on Japanese TV showed shards of glass scattered across streets and a bookstore strewn with piles of books knocked from their shelves.

‌



Some of those injured had fallen down stairs while trying to flee as the tremor struck at 1:04am on Sunday.

View 2 Images An employee crouches amid books fallen from shelves following a strong earthquake in Toyota, central Japan (Image: /Kyodo News via AP)

‌



Japan's Meteorological Agency put the quake's magnitude at 5.7, while the US Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.

The earthquake was centred around 40km (25 miles) beneath the surface in Shizuoka Prefecture, neighbouring Aichi, where officials recorded the strongest shaking. The tremors were not felt as far away as Tokyo.

‌



Officials are now urging residents to remain on alert for further powerful tremors and possible mudslides over the coming week, especially in the next two to three days.

"Please be on the lookout for mudslides, falling rocks and the possible effects from rainfall," Ayataka Ebita, an agency official, told reporters.

Article continues below

He said no apparent change was detected so far to the Nankai Trough plate, where scientists say a megaquake can possibly hit.
