Sports.title: Man City's slump cannot be excused by guilty verdict: Too many blunders, too much arm waving and football problems are piling up after 3-1 defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
This run will not be about the verdicts. This cannot be about the verdicts. Footballers do not care about these things, the stuff out of their control. Besides, all of them are earning cut-price transfers elsewhere were Manchester City to suffer relegation anyway. And cut-price fees mean bulkier salaries. So to them the current climate, the circumstances around City – their recent history and their immediate future – does not overly matter. Sure, there might be the odd one who is slightly more philosophical and inquisitive about appeals and appendices but the majority won't be giving it much or any thought. City insist on their innocence publicly and privately; until that changes, their players and Enzo Maresca carry on regardless. There were the usual jeers here, there were ditties about cheating, but that surely cannot affect them. Instead, the performances over the past few weeks, this a third consecutive Premier League defeat and now sinking six points adrift of Arsenal, cannot be excused by the findings of an independent commission. The problems are football problems. This is a squad who appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game. Namely how to build from the back – and that is prompting individual mistakes. It happened against Ipswich Town and at Aston Villa. On the river Trent, it was no different. The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story. Man City are a squad who now appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story Three defeats in a row have seen Enzo Maresca's side slip six points behind leaders Arsenal Too many errors. Too much arm waving. Too much feeling sorry for themselves when decisions go elsewhere. Oliver Glasner is not stupid, he will have seen examples of this play out in parts of City's victories as well as reverses. As Liam Delap raced into the corner to celebrate his second with 17 minutes left – a huge day in his career against the club which moulded him – Glasner was dashing down the touchline with unbridled joy. MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Nottingham Forest (5-2-2-1): Sels 6; Munoz 6 (Netz 65, 6), Cunha 8, Milenkovic 8, Murillo 7, Williams 8; Yates 8 (Sangare 79), Schlager 8; McAtee 7 (Ndoye 65, 6), Gibbs-White 7; Delap 9 (Jesus 87) Manager: Oliver Glasner 8 Man City (4-1-4-1): Donnarumma 5; Khusanov 5, Dias 5, Guehi 4 (Nunes 46, 7), Gvardiol 4 (O'Reilly 46, 6); Anderson 5; Ndiaye 6, Cherki 6, Fernandez 4 (Foden 78), Doku 6; Haaland 5 Manager: Enzo Maresca 5 Referee: Sam Barrott 6 Att: 30,762 Forest displays have deserved more than their points total so far and this was vindication for their fifth manager in 14 months, who suggested he fancied sampling Nottingham’s nightlife afterwards. Delap was exceptional, some personal redemption after criticism. The way in which Glasner nudged James McAtee further forward, stationed higher from the off in order to pressurise the visitors, spoke to an idea that City arrived here ready to be ruffled and have been wearing a look of fragility. By the time this was eight minutes shy of half time and McAtee was nicking possession from Elliot Anderson, drawing a foul that sparked another onslaught on Gianluigi Donnarumma's box, Forest were already two clear – and had been for some time. Phil Foden warmed up on the touchline, laughing and hugging with Callum Hudson-Odoi. Forest preyed on City insecurities. A midfield structure that is simply not working at the moment, easily railroaded. A defence allergic to the basics and an epidemic of individual mistakes – either as a result of nervousness or blase attitude on the ball. Straight to the mistakes. A real collection, these: the first in the fifth minute and the others 13 minutes afterwards. Jair Cunha wheeled away after picking Josko Gvardiol's pocket, meandering forward into the box and side-footing into the far corner largely unchallenged. Gvardiol seemed to have the air of a man who felt invincible when gathering possession before being eased off it. Later, as Delap thundered forward 45 yards unchecked to hammer past Donnarumma, you wondered about the communication between these City players. Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye left things to each other near halfway, Xaver Schlager gave his thanks – finding Delap – and the City academy graduate bulldozed clear. Marc Guehi waved him through, Ruben Dias dithered and Maresca bowed his head. Liam Delap was exceptional for Nottingham Forest, some personal redemption after criticism Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes. Dias looked aghast at Guehi, who was then hooked at the break alongside Gvardiol. Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki both stood in the centre circle, hands on hips. It later emerged via replays that Anderson had been arguing with Abdukodir Khusanov in the build-up to Forest's opener as well, proof that City were nowhere near close to producing what was expected when on the ball in their own half. Glasner had the weapons at his disposal to make this work but even the Austrian must have been surprised at the way in which they tickled City's soft underbelly. They had not scored at the City Ground all season. All change when owner Evangelos Marinakis made his first trip to see a game since Glasner's appointment, which felt particularly handy, with Yates having delivered a spinetingling dressing room speech pre-match. Anger permeated the eyes of some City players as the whistle went. Cherki stormed down the tunnel, animatedly discussing how to play through Forest with Fernandez when they re-emerged. Their lifeline came after 52 minutes, a Ryan Yates deflection from Jeremy Doku's cross sitting up for Cherki to hammer home a half-volley off the bar. Doku soon almost squeezed another effort past Matz Sels and the mood shifted, City briefly creeping menacingly like the monsters they are portrayed as. Maresca had introduced Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly, with both affecting the upturn. An admission of selection errors, perhaps, although O'Reilly is managing an ongoing back issue and is set for therapy on it over the international break. City will need some of that as a collective. Delap won the ball inside his own third, gliding past Anderson, and Forest's explosive counter ended with Delap spearing a shot in off the post after Morgan Gibbs-White carried possession unopposed for 60 yards. Delirium, Glasner darting to the corner flag. The quirk of this is that City's failings mean Manchester United drop into the bottom three. MARESCA'S VERDICT: Maresca criticised Manchester City’s lack of fight but insisted that City created enough chances to leave with something despite admitting his players were physically second best. ‘In the first half we were not good enough - we didn't match the intensity that these kind of games require,’ Maresca said. ‘If you are not able to win the second balls then you struggle. You have to match the desire to win second balls and duels, otherwise it is not good. When you lost balls the way we did and cannot recover immediately, it’s a matter of winning duels.’ Maresca has a two-week international break to rake over the issues affecting his side and believes time away could do the squad good. The Italian added: ‘When you lose a game you always want to go again immediately to try to win games but I think that this international break, the last one until March, is also good for the players. ‘We didn't match the intensity. We need to understand the reason why and try to avoid the next games. There is no panic. We need to understand but no panic.’ Maresca revealed that defenders Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol asked to come off at half time with injuries, while Forest out-ran his team by 6km on the night. ‘If you want to win against City, you need to do this,’ Oliver Glasner said after recording his first home win. ‘Credit to Liam, these strikes are something you have or you don't have. ‘It can be a turning point but we have to prove it. The way we performed today should give us confidence.’ City winger Jeremy Doku could not explain why they could not deal with Forest before half time. ‘We are used to playing every two days - that's not a reason,’ Doku said. ‘If you ask me for the reason for our first half I don't know. ‘We reacted too late. We need to be fresh minds, start again and analyse what we can do better and move forward. The international break comes at the right moment for us to analyse and come back refreshed.’ JACK GAUGHAN

Sports.title: Non-league footballer in stable condition after collapsing in warm-up and being rushed to hospital, leading to match being abandoned
Sports.content:
Truro City's match against Folkestone Invicta was abandoned due to a medical emergency on Saturday after a footballer collapsed during the warm-up.

Yassine En-Neyah, 26, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after collapsing while preparing with his team-mates on the pitch. It was later confirmed he was in a stable condition.

The former Nottingham Forest academy youngster had been named among the substitutes to face Folkestone in the National League South game in Kent.

A club statement on Saturday read: 'Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed.

'Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.'

The club added a welcome on Saturday night, saying: 'He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation.

Truro City's clash with Folkestone Invicta has been abandoned due to a medical emergency

Yassine En-Neyah - pictured before the game - was named on the bench to face Folkestone

Club Statement:



Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed.



Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.



We will… pic.twitter.com/IyiF2VIFMz — Truro City FC (@TCFC_Official) November 7, 2026

'The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City's medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club.

'Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too.'

Truro City's players had earlier gathered around the rear of the ambulance where En-Neyah was being treated to shield him from view.

The Moroccan-born former Republic of Ireland youth international began his career at Nottingham Forest, making his professional debut in January 2020 as a substitute during an FA Cup third-round clash against Chelsea.

After being released by Forest in 2021, the winger has played for multiple non-league sides including Shelbourne, Waterford and Maldon & Tipree.

Having briefly represented Truro in 2023, En-Neyah returned to the Tinners for a second spell in 2024, where he has remained since.

When he signed his new Truro contract last season, En-Neyah admitted he didn't think twice about the decision to stay.

'Truro's been my home for the last couple of seasons and it was a very easy decision,' he told BBC Radio Cornwall.

'I feel home so I just want to continue working hard and help the club achieve greater things.

'It wasn't a case of having to think about it, it was just a matter of getting it done and continuing to work hard and do well for the club and for myself.'

Sports.title: Nightmare in Brazil for Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari as penalty leaves him at the back of the grid after chaotic, rain-swept day of qualifying in Sao Paulo
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s chance of making up for recent frustrations with a strong run in the Sao Paulo GP took a major blow after power unit penalties sent him to the back of the grid for Sunday’s race.

It also meant that he made only a token effort in the sort of soaking wet qualifying session in which he normally thrives.

The man who benefited most from the conditions was Lando Norris, who couldn't have anticipated that he would secure pole in Brazil. The McLaren driver put in a superb performance to be fastest.

'Today was a good day, we're on pole,' said the outgoing World Champion. 'A nice surprise in some ways. A good reward for the team, a good reward for myself.'

Hamilton is one of four star drivers from the leading teams to take a penalty hit at Interlagos, a legacy of reaching the last few races of a long season amid mounting mileage on tired and fragile engines.

In Hamilton’s case the drop is more serious than had been anticipated by his team.

Hamilton is one four star drivers from the leading teams to take a penalty hit at Interlagos

Ferrari decided to change the internal combustion engine on the cars of Hamilton and Leclerc

Ferrari decided to change the internal combustion engine on the cars of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, knowing that they would have to take the plunge at some point.

That saddled both men with an initial 10-place drop – costly, but not disastrous given that Interlagos is a track where overtaking is at least possible.

However, in Friday’s final FP3 practice session Hamilton’s fresh V6 failed after just a few laps, obliging the former World Champion to take another complete new power unit.

That move accrued more penalties and consigned him to the back, where he joins Max Verstappen, whose Red Bull has undergone a similar wholesale change.

George Russell also drops five places after the Mercedes man took a new V6, having been second fastest in the wet qualifying session. His front row spot thus goes to team mate Kimi Antonelli.

It is far from over for Hamilton or Verstappen, but making it to the top three will require some good fortune. The Dutch driver pointed out that overtaking will be more difficult without the DRS tool that is no longer on the cars in 2026, and Hamilton agreed.

'I think overtaking will be very, very, very hard,' said the Ferrari ace. 'I'm not sure you're going to see the same sort of races that you've seen in the past.'

The penalties for so many top runners open up the possibility for better than anticipated results for those not affected and who made the most of the wet qualifying session – notably Kiwi Liam Lawson, who starts a surprise third for Racing Bulls.

Sports.title: 'I was happy to escape the Man Utd negativity – it was common sense to join Aston Villa'
Sports.content:
'I was happy to escape the Man Utd negativity – it was common sense to join Aston Villa'

The former Manchester United star felt it was necessary to depart Old Trafford and join Aston Villa to escape the negativity

View 3 Images Tom Cleverley was happy to leave Manchester United when he did (Image: Getty)

Tom Cleverley once admitted he was happy to escape the "negativity" that surrounded him at Manchester United during a tough period in his career. The former midfielder moved to Aston Villa on loan after a troubling stint at Old Trafford and claimed the move was "common sense" for all involved.

‌



‌



Cleverley joined United's academy at the age of 12 and worked his way up the ranks. He embarked on several loans with the likes of Watford and Wigan Athletic before a stint at Villa earned him a permanent switch to Everton.

‌



Through 79 United appearances, Cleverley scored five goals and assisted strikes seven times. However, negative attention surrounding the club at the time of his loan exit in 2014 meant he was glad to see the back of Manchester.

‌



Speaking after his deadline-day move to Villa 12 years ago, Cleverley said: "I am happy to get away from some of the negativity that surrounded me at Man United and I am genuinely excited about this season at Aston Villa. If all the players last season said they were high in confidence, they would be lying. It wasn't just me.

Man Utd prepare for Real Madrid conflict as JJ Gabriel nears Old Trafford exit READ MORE :

"It was the rest of the squad and that rubs on to players and the fans, too. It was a tough season for us but I've got away from the negativity of that and this is a brand-new challenge and I can't wait to get stuck into it.

View 3 Images Cleverley says he left United due to negativity (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"If any footballer gets a bit of stick off their own fans, they are going to be hurt but it has made me strong as a character. You don't turn into a bad player just because someone says it on Twitter."

‌



Despite enduring a rocky time at United, Cleverley was quick to praise his then-manager Louis van Gaal. He added: "He was always straight with me. Any footballer wants the best opportunity to play every week so it was common sense for me to try and get this move."

Cleverley's contract ran out at the end of the 2014/15 season and he made it clear he didn't think he would be back at Old Trafford. He said: "With me being out of contract at the end of the year, if I'm honest, I don't think I would play for the club again."

‌



View 3 Images Cleverley jumped ship for Villa on loan (Image: Getty)

He joined the Toffees after the successful loan at Villa where he made 37 appearances and scored three goals. His stint at Villa Park ended with an FA Cup runners-up medal after suffering final defeat to Arsenal.

‌



Two seasons at Everton followed, where he starred in 42 games and made eight goal contributions. Cleverley would end his career at Watford, where he was arguably at his best, scoring 19 goals and assisting 15 times.

He has since entered management, overseeing Watford from 2024 to 2025 before becoming the current head coach at Plymouth Argyle.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher's row with Aston Villa exposed a painful truth about Man Utd's new reality
Sports.content:
It was the sort of innocuous, run-of-the-mill opinion football fans hear all the time.

The dismal form of Manchester United this season has seen all sort of names bandied around as possible replacements for Michael Carrick and Jamie Carragher, in his role as a Sky Sports pundit, suggested Unai Emery.

Cue a gigantic - and understandable - backlash from Villa fans and a ridiculous and over-the-top response from the club and Villa chairman Nassef Sawiris, who threatened Carragher with legal action for his "unacceptable insults".

The row is still bubbling away in the background, via Emery's firm suggestion that Villa can challenge for the Champions League after Carragher revisited the topic in his weekly newspaper column.

‌



Unai Emery sends Jamie Carragher firm message over Aston Villa plans after legal threat READ MORE :

JJ Gabriel breaks silence on Man Utd exit with eight-word explanation for Real Madrid move READ MORE :

Carragher said it was "beyond doubt" that United eclipse Villa on every conceivable metric. "It did not strike me as controversial to suggest that when a club of United’s size wants Aston Villa’s managers or players, traditionally they get them," he wrote.

That, of course, is true. The financial power of the Premier League's traditional elite, their history and offers of playing in European competitions and winning trophies do usually tempt prospective targets.

But what Carragher perhaps fails to gauge is that his viewpoint is now out of date. Like a jar that has been forgotten about at the back of the fridge, it needs chucking out and replacing with something fresher.

United are no longer the powerhouse of their Sir Alex Ferguson glory days. And they don't have their pick of the best players and managers from the Premier League and beyond.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 4 Images Michael Carrick's side are far from what they once were (Image: Getty Images)

This summer, they spent £155million to sign Youri Tielemans from Villa, Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Carlos Baleba from Brighton. They didn't exactly have to fight off rival clubs for their signatures - and we've seen why in the last few months.

These are middle-shelf players at best. Premium, top-shelf ones are heading elsewhere. With the Glazers piling up debts and Sir Jim Ratcliffe slashing costs wherever he can, United are unwilling or unable to shop at the same stores as their rivals.

‌



It's a similar picture when it comes to managers. Since Ferguson retired in 2013, they have had 11 permanent or interim bosses. Five, including Carrick, have been former United players. Just two, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho, could be described as proven, elite managers.

View 4 Images Unai Emery has big ambitions at Aston Villa and is not interested in joining Manchester United (Image: Javier Borrego/Getty Images)

The last two permanent bosses before Carrick show United's current level: Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim were hired after encouraging form with Ajax and Sporting Lisbon respectively. As the connection with Emery - who is about to sign a new contract with Villa - shows, United are simply unable to cherry-pick the best in the business.

In 2024, United chiefs spoke with Thomas Tuchel and Gareth Southgate as they pondered replacements for Ten Hag. Neither wanted the job.

‌



The list of prospective replacements for Carrick showed the situation clearly. Emery and Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler are unattainable. Julian Nagelsmann is at a career lull after a World Cup exit with Germany. Antonio Conte is a nuclear option not many other clubs are willing to take.

View 4 Images Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada have been unable to hire a top-tier replacement for Michael Carrick (Image: Getty Images)

In the Goldilocks analogy, Eddie Howe - a former Bournemouth and Newcastle boss - is just right. If they had managed to woo an elite manager then the truth is that Carrick would be long gone.

This harsh reality will be visible to all on Sunday at Old Trafford when Emery takes his Villa side to play United. Villa may arrive on the back of a 3-0 mauling by Barcelona, while United are buoyed by a 3-2 comeback win over Roma.

‌



But as the odds show, nobody would be surprised to see Villa follow in the footsteps of Bournemouth by leaving with all three points. Emery is perfectly happy where he is with good reason.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney set to break I'm A Celebrity rule before ITV show even starts
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney set to break I'm A Celebrity rule before ITV show even starts

Wayne Rooney possesses unique inside knowledge of I'm A Celebrity camp

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney watched his wife, Coleen, in the jungle back in 2024 (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock)

Wayne Rooney is set to inadvertently break an I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! rule due to his marriage to wife Coleen. The Manchester United icon has been rumoured to be one of 12 new campmates for the 2026 edition of the ITV show, which premieres on Monday, November 16.

‌



‌



The 41-year-old would follow in the footsteps of his wife, who finished runner-up in the jungle in 2024. Rooney will need to undergo a psychological evaluation before officially taking part in the competition, and he will also need to inform the show's bosses of any physical ailments that could prevent him from participating in certain trials.

‌



However, Rooney may find it difficult to adhere to one of the several key rules of I'm A Celeb. Campmates are not allowed to tell anyone, including friends who've been on the show before, that they are entering the Australian jungle until the broadcaster officially confirms the news.

‌



Cast members are also not allowed to ask previous contestants for tips, but how ITV can realistically enforce it remains to be seen. That obviously makes it a tricky situation for the England icon to manage, given Coleen's prior involvement and the fact that they live together.

Wayne Rooney calls out Jamie Carragher to fight in Man Utd vs Liverpool boxing bout READ MORE :

Rooney never visited the camp during Coleen's tenure, with the pair's youngest children, Kit and Cass, making the trip Down Under with Coleen's mother, Colette, when family were allowed to visit the cast members.

Breaking of this specific rule emerged in 2022 when actor Danny Miller revealed that after winning the 2022 edition of the show, he sought jungle advice from his former Emmerdale co-star and ex-I'm A Celeb participant Adam Thomas.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 2 Images Coleen Rooney finished runner-up in I'm A Celebrity 2024 (Image: ITV)

‌



Miller said: "I confided in Adam about me taking part as he is one of my best friends in the world. I feel like I am a step ahead as I've asked him questions about what it will be like." One thing that Rooney won't be able to get around is the strict prohibition of mobile phones when setting foot in the jungle.

Finding out the latest United scores during his time on the show can only come through winning a Dingo Dollar Challenge. Rooney will reportedly join a long list of former footballers to star on the show, including the likes of Ian Wright, Wayne Bridge, Dennis Wise, 2018 winner Harry Redknapp and 2022 queen of the jungle Jill Scott.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho's first act as Man Utd boss offers JJ Gabriel hope after transfer wish granted
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho's first act as Man Utd boss offers JJ Gabriel hope after transfer wish granted

JJ Gabriel has had a glimpse of what his future might look like away from Manchester United should he sign for Real Madrid

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel appears set to join Real Madrid (Image: Anthony Devlin/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Jose Mourinho's defence of his youth policy could see JJ Gabriel fast-tracked into senior football. The wantaway Manchester United wonderkid stunned the Premier League giants in September when requesting to leave the club and have his registration cancelled.

‌



The likes of Real Madrid, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich all had interest in the 16-year-old, but it's the 15-time European champions who seem to have won the race for the promising youngster.

Gabriel is expected to sign for Mourinho's side in January on a long-term contract at the Santiago Bernabeu. The Athletic reports that the deal to acquire the forward - who is expected to play for Madrid's Castilla team - is subject to FIFA regulations and is reportedly advanced.

The teenager's desire to leave United is said to stem from his camp's belief that the club are not at the level of the European giants that have registered interest in his services. Gabriel's exclusion from the club's Champions League squad reportedly left his family disappointed and was a major factor in his decision to leave.

A speedy ascent to first-team football this season was a clear motivator for Gabriel, whose representatives requested that he feature for at least 20 minutes across United's matches against Sabah, Brighton and Bournemouth, according to the Manchester Evening News.

JJ Gabriel rejects PSG transfer offer as wantaway Man Utd wonderkid picks next club READ MORE :

The request was snubbed and eventually contributed to Gabriel's desire to seek pastures new. While Madrid is known for platforming world-class players rather than promising young talent, Gabriel could find hope under Mourinho, who once outlined his promotion of academy stars in his first press conference as United boss in 2016.

The Portuguese boss had been criticised for the lack of youth players that featured across his tenures at Chelsea, Inter Milan and his first stint at Madrid between 2010 and 2013.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho previously backed his record of promoting youth players (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

In true Mourinho fashion, he came prepared to challenge his critics as he claimed: "I have promoted 49 youth players from academies. If you want, I can give you that list." He then showed a list to the room and continued: "Two factors that are very important on these records, because sometimes you promote because you don’t have another chance or so many injuries, you have to bring them in.

"The second factor is when you are not playing for big targets, then it is easier to bring them up. My record with injuries is very low – even from the UEFA studies, there were many times the team with the least injuries in the whole of Europe was mine."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Mourinho then discussed the quality of the players he's promoted and the accolades they've earned at the highest level of the game. He added: "Last year, the only season of my career that I was not fighting for the title – every other season I was winning or finishing second, or finish third once but still fighting for the title.

"I still did 49 and some of them we are speaking about big names – players that today are Champions League winners, playing for national teams. Forty-nine is a lot. Once more – it’s one lie repeated many times. Sometimes it looks like it might be true but it is always true. Many of you… the names. If you want them, I’ll give them to you."

While JJ Gabriel is leaving United because of a lack of opportunities, Mourinho's words suggest he will be willing to give anyone a chance to prove themselves if they have the talent.

Sports.title: Cheavon Clarke stuns Chris Billam-Smith with brutal KO to settle rivalry
Sports.content:
Cheavon Clarke stuns Chris Billam-Smith with brutal KO to settle rivalry

Chev Clarke upset the odds by stopping former world champion Chris Billam-Smith to breathe new life into his cruiserweight career

View 3 Images Chris Billam-Smith is knocked down by Cheavon Clarke

Cheavon Clarke punched himself into world title contention after stopping long-time rival Chris Billam-Smith in a stunning upset.

‌



‌



The 35-year-old was heading into their Copper Box clash with all the bragging rights having beaten Billam-Smith on the amateur scene 10 years ago. After back-to-back defeats to Leonardo Mosquea and Viddal Riley, Clarke was forced to work his way up - put has put the division on notice with a stunning upset win.

‌



With the cruiserweight division starting to heat up following the news that two-time undisputed heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk was to move back down, Clarke was itching to prove why he should be considered as one of the top players in the division and throw his name into contention for a crack at gold.

‌



It was a rather quiet opening three minutes as both men were merely trying to get a read of each other. But Billam-Smith put his foot on the gas in the dying moments, and tagged his long-time foe coming in. Clarke seemed mildly happy making it a grappling match, but a locked-in Billam-Smith found a way to get out of bother, and pile on the pressure. As the crowd roared on the 'Gentleman,' the Bournemouth scrapper answered their prayers and ended the second on the front foot.

View 3 Images Cheavon Clarke punches Chris Billiam-Smith

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Former champion boxer Josh Frederiksen dead at 36 after tragic skydiving accident READ MORE :

Tyson Fury issues response to Oleksandr Usyk trilogy snub READ MORE :

A sneaky right hand from Billam-Smith in the opening moments of the third just send Clarke backpedalling a tad, before firing a sharp uppercut counter - his best shot in the first three rounds. While the eye-cacthing shot should have sprung Clarke into life, it proved to be anything but as he went back to grappling. It was Billam-Smith who found himself ending the third strongest as he landed a tidy combination upstairs.

The fourth saw the round dominated by more grappling and holding as the referee was forced to step in yet again. But Clarke detonated a right hand to end the strongest. As the fifth threatened to be yet another grappling battle, Clarke appeared to stun Billam-Smith with a clubbing right hand, forcing the Bournemouth native to hold on. Clarke's bizarre attacks seemed to pay dividends heading into the midway point.

‌



Both men, visibly donning damage, began trading right hands. Billam-Smith found some brief success with the jab, but momentum quickly shift after Clarke came in on the offence. Billam-Smith was soon sent crashing to the canvas, but was quick to get back to his feet.

That said, Clarke was smelling blood as he saw his long-time adversary on wobbly legs. Clarke dropped his rival twice more with several piercing combinations before the referee stepped in and waved off the clash - much to the frustration of 'CBS' who thought it was harsh.

‌



Meanwhile, in the co-main event Denzel Bentley secured a points win on his Zuffa Boxing debut just weeks after being stripped of his WBO middleweight title. The London brawler came out with a real point to prove as he looks to establish himself as one of the faces of the Zuffa banner.

Shane Mosley Jr, son of boxing great Shane Mosley, was quite simply unable to build on his jaw-dropping win over Serhii Bohachuk earlier this year. The 35-year-old American boxing veteran had it all to do, and his first fight on British shores could not have gone any worse.

‌



View 3 Images But the British scrapper powered through to win on points (Image: Getty Images)

Bentley was quick off the blocks early doors - eager to stamp his authority. Mosley Jr, though, was happy to turn it into a scrappy affair. British brawler Bentley kept his composure and attacked on the backfoot. But it was very much a tactical chess match in the opening three minutes. Bentley and Mosley Jr were very much happy to work each other out and not get caught with anything major.

‌



The second stanza saw Mosley Jr resort to hunting his foe yet again, circling him, and refusing to let Bentley breathe. Unfazed by the pressure, Bentley fired off a clubbing right hand which seemed to wobble his foe, before another onslaught sent Mosley Jr crashing to the canvas. But the durable American quickly rose to his feet. Rather than taking a backfoot, the American ended the round on top, and even snuck in a couple of shots of his own.

A firefight quickly ensued in the third as both fighters began trading in the pocket. Bentley, on his bike, caught Mosley Jr coming in with a sneaky left hand. Bentley decided to up the tempo in the final exchanges of the third, picking his shots nicely and managed to clip his foe - who eventually survived the round.

‌



In the fourth, a rather wild exchange against the ropes saw Bentley make Mosley Jr pay for his sloppy approach. Just moments later, and the Brit connected with a stinging one-two followed by a right hand over the top. Mosley Jr's chin was required to work overtime as the American was absorbing attack after attack.

Despite appearing to sport some damage on the right eye, Mosley Jr began the fifth on the ascendancy, marching forward and piling on the pressure on Bentley. It felt like a real turning of the tide moment, as the London crowd began to get a bit restless. As Mosley Jr threatened to control proceedings in the sixth, Bentley bit down on his gumshield and resorted to jabbing away on the backfoot.

Article continues below

The seventh opened up towards the midway point when Bentley fired off a stinging left over the top, but it was Mosley Jr who ended strong and appeared to do some damage, forcing his foe to retreat. Both men were evidently tiring as the pair fired hard leather, but neither seemed to lad. A gun-shy Bentley just could not find a home for anything.

In the penultimate round, and Mosley Jr was very much in control. But at the midway point of the ninth, Bentley got to work behind the jab and managed to connect with some of his attacks - which set up an intriguing final three minutes. In the final round, while Mosley Jr was stilling pushing forward, it was Bentley who picked his shots well and managed to do some damage whilst back-pedalling. Despite Mosley Jr's late second half flurry, it was Bentley who got the nod on points as the official scorecards read: (96-94,96-93,95-94).

Sports.title: Crowd erupts into violence at Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson boxing clash
Sports.content:
Crowd erupts into violence at Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson boxing clash

The Joshua Buatsi-Willy Hutchinson rematch card was overshadowed after fans began clashing with one another in the crowd

View Image A brawl broke out in the crowd during Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson (Image: DAZN)

A massive ringside brawl broke out at the AO Arena during the undercard of Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson. Security rushed to intervene early on in Jack Rafferty's clash against Hovhannes Martirosyan.

‌



‌



Having first faced off in September 2024 for the vacant WBO Interim Light-Heavyweight World Championship, Buatsi and Hutchinson meet again on Saturday evening in a hotly anticipated rematch.

‌



Buatsi was the victor by split decision in the first bout and Hutchinson had campaigned for some time to secure the rematch. The vacant WBC Light-Heavyweight World Championship is the prize.

‌



However, whilst sparks fly in the ring, as the undercard got underway in Manchester, they flew in the stands. Rowdy spectators threw punches at each other.

Sports.title: Bleak Man City reality hits home as Liam Delap fires Nottingham Forest to statement win
Sports.content:
Bleak Man City reality hits home as Liam Delap fires Nottingham Forest to statement win

NOTTINGHAM FOREST 3-1 MANCHESTER CITY: Liam Delap scored two wondergoals to give Oliver Glasner's side a morale-boosting victory over their downbeat visitors

View 3 Images Liam Delap scored twice to sink Manchester City at the City Ground

He gave it the full Cristiano Ronaldo celebration. And had every right to. No-one is ever going to confuse Liam Delap with the five-times Ballon d’Or winner but this was something special.

‌



‌



With around a quarter of the contest remaining, Nottingham Forest’s chances of holding on to a one-goal lead seemed slim to none. And slim was packing his bags. But Delap, a product of City, then started and finished a counter-attack with the bravado of a world-beater.

‌



It was some moment. Left foot, bullet-quick, arrow-straight, postage-stamp territory, City Ground in glorious uproar as the mist really did roll in.

‌



Delap’s sensational hit - his second of the match - gave Forest a thoroughly deserved win but this was another uninspiring City performance. Three Premier League defeats on the spin suggest a side waiting for their fate to be decided elsewhere.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources .

‌



The initial reaction of the players to the independent commission’s guilty verdicts appeared to be one of defiance. It is hard not to think that defiance has dissipated somewhat.

Ex-professionals and pundits queue up to tell us the spectre of extreme sanctions will not affect the mentality of the squad but this is unprecedented. No-one really knows how it will impact their psyche. This is a group of footballers who strongly suspect whatever they produce on the pitch is likely to be rendered irrelevant by heavy punishment should the club’s appeal be unsuccessful. How can that not have the slightest impact?

‌



Whether it is a factor or not, one thing was for sure based on much of the evidence from this match. City’s aggression has disappeared, City’s snap has gone, City’s desire has diminished.

They lost every even contest in the early stages. They were outmuscled. They showed no great appetite for a fight. First things first. Forest were outstanding in those early stages. Yes, Josko Gvardiol was culpable ahead of the opening goal but the determination and drive of scorer Jair Cunha was magnificent. And yes, another unacceptable surrender of possession preceded Forest’s second but Delap’s buccaneering run and finish was something to behold.

‌



View 3 Images Manchester City were beaten again by Nottingham Forest (Image: Gareth Copley)

Oliver Glasner’s game-plan was brutally effective in its simplicity. Every time a City player had the ball in the opposition half, he was confronted by a ferociously committed Forest man.

‌



They did not give the talented trio of Jeremy Doku, Rayan Cherki and Iliman Ndiaye a moment’s peace. And upfront, Delap comprehensively unsettled Marc Guehi and Ruben Dias.

Guehi’s form for City has been alarmingly poor - it was no shock he was hooked at half-time - and, of course, it does not help that Gianluigi Donnarumma is in one of those spells that is particularly unfortunate for a goalkeeper. Any decently-struck shot that comes his way goes past him. Not ideal.

‌



They were very good hits from Cunha and Delap but Donnarumma’s efforts to keep them out looked to be little more than token.

View 3 Images Delap fires home his first goal against Manchester City (Image: Alfie Cosgrove/NurPhoto)

‌



Inevitably, City improved but Forest were relatively untroubled throughout the first half and Enzo Maresca inevitably made a couple of changes at the interval.

To begin with, they had minimal effect, though. Sloppiness ran through City’s ranks. They needed a moment of inspiration, an instance of genius. And it came from the left boot of Cherki, fizzing the sweetest of shots into the top corner. He does not deal in the mundane, Rayan.

‌



With well over half an hour left on the clock, a full City comeback looked inevitable. But this was an evening when Forest dug fantastically deep, the example being set by captain Ryan Yates.

His work-rate set the standard but no-one was taking the man of the match honours away from Delap and Glasner afforded him the great ovation he deserved by substituting him late in proceedings.

Article continues below

It was just the performance Delap needed. For City, it was the performance of a team that knows the most costly defeats are likely to come off the pitch.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
