A small plane has made an emergency landing on a busy Florida road, much to the shock of drivers. The Cessna, which suffered mechanical failure, clipped a pickup truck, but no injuries were reported.

World.title: Drone attack on Colombian army base kills three soldiers and wounds 16
World.content:
Colombian President de la Espriella says those behind the attack in Santa Rosa del Sur will have ‘nowhere to hide’.

Share Drone attack on Colombian army base kills three soldiers and wounds 16 on social media

A drone attack on a military base in northern Colombia has killed three soldiers and wounded at least 16, the country’s armed forces said.

The Colombian military said in a statement on Saturday that the attack hit a base in Santa Rosa del Sur, a small town in the foothills of the San Lucas mountain range. Authorities have not said who carried out the strike, the latest in a series of attacks on security forces as violence rises across rural parts of the country.

The area is rich in gold mines and has long been disputed by rebel armed groups including the Gulf Clan, the National Liberation Army (ELN) and smaller groups led by former members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).

Footage shared on social media showed clouds of smoke rising from the base after three explosions, and soldiers taking cover in shelters made of sandbags.

“Those who were behind this attack… will have nowhere to hide,” President Abelardo de la Espriella wrote on X. “Every attack against our soldiers strengthens our resolve to defend Colombia.”

Rising violence

Violence has intensified in several rural areas since de la Espriella, a conservative, took office in August.

The president cancelled peace talks with rebel groups and has taken a confrontational approach, including more air strikes, deploying more troops in some cities and creating joint task forces to defend strategic assets such as a pipeline that runs from the Caribbean coast to central Colombia.

De la Espriella’s government argues that armed groups used ceasefires granted by the previous government to consolidate their grip on rural areas, where they tax local businesses and profit from the drug trade.



Some groups have responded by stepping up attacks on the country’s armed forces.

Last week, a military base in Tolima province was targeted with missiles made from gas canisters. The attack killed four civilians, including a two-month-old baby.

Police in the border city of Cucuta have been attacked several times with remotely activated bombs.

State forces and illegal armed groups carried out 34 attacks with bombs or explosives in Colombia in the four weeks to October 16, a 9 percent increase on last year’s four-week average, according to ACLED, a group that monitors armed conflicts.

A 2016 peace deal with FARC led to the demobilisation of more than 14,000 fighters, but smaller groups have since fought over the rebels’ former territory.

World.title: Earthquake hits central Japan, injuring more than 20 people
World.content:
The magnitude 5.7 quake hit Shizuoka prefecture, and authorities warn of possible strong aftershocks in coming days.

More than 20 people have been injured after a strong earthquake shook central Japan, shattering store windows and sending people fleeing buildings, according to local media and authorities.

The magnitude 5.7 quake struck at 1:04am local time on Sunday (16:00 GMT Saturday) at a depth of about 40km (25 miles) in western Shizuoka Prefecture, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.

More than 20 people were injured in the Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures, the Kyodo news agency cited authorities as saying.

A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara, and the prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, and Gifu.

No tsunami warning was issued, Kyodo reported.

The quake was not felt in Tokyo, which is far from the epicentre.

Japanese television showed shattered shop windows and shards of glass scattered across streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had fallen from the shelves.

Some of the injured had fallen on the stairs as they tried to flee, the Associated Press news agency reported.

Aftershock warnings

The meteorological agency warned people to be ready for possible strong quakes in the coming week, especially the next two to three days.

“Please be on the lookout for mudslides, falling rocks and the possible effects from rainfall,” agency official Ayataka Ebita told reporters.

He said no apparent change had been detected so far in the Nankai Trough, an underwater ocean trench where two major tectonic plates meet under parts of Japan, where scientists say a megaquake could occur.



Some local train services were suspended, while the Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in affected areas as a precautionary measure.

Trains on the Tokaido Shinkansen line, which connects Tokyo and Osaka, were delayed between Shizuoka and Gifu-Hashima stations after safety checks, rail operator JR Central said.

World.title: Trump asks UFC chief Dana White to be White House press secretary
World.content:
Ultimate Fighting Championship CEO says he will meet with the US president on Monday to discuss the offer.

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White has said he will meet with Donald Trump after the US president offered him the job of White House press secretary.

Speaking at a new conference after a boxing event in London on Saturday, White said he would meet with Trump at the White House on Monday to discuss the president’s offer.

“Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other,” Trump wrote on Truth Social earlier on Saturday. “Dana, please take the job!”

Trump also requested that White “bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country”.

Trump listed and posted pictures of six current and former UFC title holders to join White: Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov from Russia’s Dagestan region; Americans Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier and “Kayla Harris”, likely a reference to Kayla Harrison; and Amanda Nunes, a Brazilian who became a US citizen last year.

“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote.

The White House press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia’s tenure ended ‌last ⁠month after just five days.

Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down from the role at the end of August.

White and Trump first worked together in the early 2000s, but they grew closer since ⁠the UFC chief publicly backed Trump’s presidential campaign in 2016.

In recent years, Trump has attended several UFC events, and in June, the White House hosted a night of UFC fights as ⁠part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of US independence.



The White House press office already has a former UFC spokesperson among its ranks: Director of Communications ⁠Steven Cheung, who worked for White’s organisation from 2013 to 2016.

Cheung shared the president’s message on X and said, “Hell yeah! Do it, @DanaWhite! It’ll just be like old times!”

World.title: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
World.content:
Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed, including a British national. Three victims are Polish and two have not been identified.

Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia.

Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk later named the injured officers as Senior Constable Jakub Kulik and Senior Constable Artur MoraÅski.

One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added.

Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims.

Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack.

On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's parents and his sister, who was 21-years-old.

World.title: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
World.content:
Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say at least 33 people, including women and children, have been killed in air strikes by Saudi Arabia.

There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.

Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.

The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.

The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.

Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Saturday. It added that 39 people had been injured.

The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.

The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.

A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plane landing there.

The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.

Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.

On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.

The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.

The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.

Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.

A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

World.title: 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years
World.content:
New Zealand voted in a new government as fog choked the capital, Wellington, on Saturday - and the mood was as palpable as the grey weather.

"It's pretty flat," 21-year-old Imogen Vlutger says. "There's this kind of apathy and a bit of dread."

"Tired. I think we're all tired," Symone, 28, admits.

"I didn't even vote," one man in his 40s sheepishly confesses. He couldn't bring himself to tick any of the boxes, he explains, declining to chat further.

"Wellington's a bit of a bubble," another voter says, expressing a caveat I heard often, before describing feeling disillusioned.

But polling shows this is a pervasive sentiment across the country: the national mood is low and faith in politics is even lower.

More than half the country no longer sees it as a land of opportunity, a recent study found, while a similar portion fears that the future looks even worse.

Many Kiwis feel the economy is in ruins, there are no jobs, the cost of living has become sky high, the sense of community that used to be a source of national pride is breaking down and there's no sense of genuine progress on policy solutions.

A record number of them are abandoning ship in search of brighter futures elsewhere.

Saturday's election also saw a record number of voters desert the two major parties, giving neither a clear mandate.

But it brought new highs for parties across the spectrum: the left-leaning Greens, the right-wing libertarian Act Party and the centrist Opportunity Party â the latter of which had never won a seat in parliament before but could now hold the balance of power with seven.

World.title: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
World.content:
Israel's president says he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government.

Isaac Herzog has been holding talks with political parties after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a majority in Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset, following last week's election.

Eisenkot will now have 28 days to try to form a new administration, with a potential 14-day extension.

"Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," the former military chief wrote on X.

No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, meaning all governments have been coalitions.

Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.

Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.

Herzog said that, after consulting all parties during the week, he would give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government.

A statement from the president's office said he had informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of the decision.

Following consultations with delegations from the incoming Knesset members, Eisenkot received 67 recommendations for the premiership and Netanyahu 46, the statement said.

The president has broad discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition and does not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.

World.title: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
World.content:
A US State Department statement about its multi-million dollar reward said it was offering the money for information about the Iranian programme, including "facilities, equipment and associated personnel".

It said Iran's "lack of compliance with the IAEA [the International Atomic Energy Agency] on safeguards obligations has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like [nuclear] centrifuges".

Centrifuges are needed to produce enriched uranium, which can be used to make reactor fuel for civilian use but also for nuclear weapons if enriched to around 90% purity or higher.

There had been mounting speculation that the US might resume significant strikes in Iran after the midterm elections, though Trump told reporters, prior to the polls, that he was in "no rush" to do so.

In an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterms, the president also said the US "might need to go after Pickaxe [Mountain]", an underground site linked to Iran's nuclear programme.

This was "not a big deal" and could be done in "one hour", Trump said.

The president has repeatedly threatened to bomb the suspected underground site on previous occasions.

However, both Trump and Vice-President JD Vance have said public opposition to the war on Iran fuelled heavy losses for their Republican Party in this week's midterm elections, which has led to speculation the White House may no longer seek an escalation in the conflict.

On Friday, Trump insisted that Iran was keen to end the eight-month conflict with the US, stressing the damage to Tehran's economy and military.

"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he said.

Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman said on Tuesday that both sides were "reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented" and that it remained hopeful of a deal being agreed.

Iranian negotiators had discussed with mediators a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days once the US met its seven conditions.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

World.title: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
World.content:
The EU's former Brexit negotiator has warned that the UK cannot "cherry pick" which elements of the single market to which it subscribes, after Andy Burnham said he wanted to explore closer economic ties with Europe.

The prime minister has said rejoining the bloc's internal market was among options he could pursue as part of a reshaping of ties since the UK's exit from the EU nearly six years ago.

But Michel Barnier told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that EU members would insist on the UK readopting certain conditions, such as the free movement of people, to gain access.

He said there was not a "single market Ã la carte" menu from which the UK could pick and choose what elements it wanted to adopt.

Barnier - who led the EU delegation during Brexit talks between 2016 and 2021, and had a three-month spell as French prime minister in 2024 - said the "door is open" within Europe to the UK rejoining as an EU member.

But he insisted that any move to rejoin the single market - which allows for goods to be freely traded without border controls - would require the UK to follow the same terms as other members.

He added that this included compliance with regulations designed to promote the circulation of goods, services, capital and people, referred to collectively within EU institutions as the "four freedoms".

"There will be no possibility to have one freedom and not the other. The four freedoms are clearly the four conditions to be inside a single market."

Since becoming prime minister in July, Burnham has suggested he could commit Labour to pursuing a much closer future relationship with Europe, including asking to rejoin the organisation as a full member, though he has ruled out major changes before the next election.

His predecessors have struck a series of deals with the EU on different aspects of how the UK and EU interact post-Brexit.

Both sides are hoping to use a meeting in Brussels in 10 days' time to unveil deals on food standards, youth visas and re-linking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime.

World.title: With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle
World.content:
In the aftermath of the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, Donald Trump said he would be willing to work with the newly ascendent Democrats in Congress.

On Friday, however, he elevated Stephen Miller, his bare-knuckled political operative and longtime adviser, to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.

Far from an olive branch to Congress, Miller's promotion could be a sign that the president is girding for political battle by installing a partisan firebrand in the top White House job.

"The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our president and defend this magnificent republic," Miller posted on X, adding that he was "honored beyond words" to be Trump's pick for the job.

One of the most powerful positions in Washington, the chief of staff is gatekeeper to the president, agenda-setter in the White House and chief negotiator with Congress and other outside political interests.

"Stephen Miller's been with me since the beginning," Trump said in comments to reporters after announcing the move on his Truth Social website. "He gets it."

World.title: Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse
World.content:
Prosecutors in Paraguay have charged former president Santiago PeÃ±a over his alleged role in a banking scandal that led to his impeachment.

He has been accused of breach of trust and administration for personal gain.

PeÃ±a, who denies any wrongdoing, was forced from office after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.

He was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests.

He had offered to step down but rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached PeÃ±a and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents.

PeÃ±a, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing.

The impeachment charges that led to PeÃ±a's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.

PeÃ±a's deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as the new interim president and promised not to "abandon" the millions of people affected by the scandal.

"Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028.

The demise of the digital bank left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank.

Long lines of people trying to withdraw money from Ueno branches snaked down the streets of the capital Asuncion on Tuesday and Wednesday.

An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions, prompting public outrage particularly in the capital, AsunciÃ³n.

Protests erupted across the country in response, with thousands taking to the streets on Thursday to demand their money.

Earlier demonstrations featured clashes with the police, who used tear gas and water cannons on the crowd.

PeÃ±a's impeachment passed with 44 out of 45 senators voting in favour of it. One lawmaker was absent.

"It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me," PeÃ±a said in a video posted on X announcing his resignation, adding his priority was "the peace of mind of Paraguayans who entrusted their savings to our financial system".

Afterwards, senate president Basilio NÃºÃ±ez said PeÃ±a was found guilty of "dereliction of duty".

World.title: First Lady celebrates Flamingos after historic U-17 World Cup title win
World.content:
The First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, has congratulated the Flamingos following their historic victory at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, describing their achievement as a triumph of resilience and commitment.

The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition after defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat.

In a congratulatory message, Mrs Tinubu said she was pleased to join Nigerians in celebrating the team’s achievement, which she said had placed the country and Africa at the top of women’s football.

“Your path to victory was not an easy one. You shrugged off your shaky start and took on the world, winning six matches in a row on your way to the golden trophy, confirming what others already know – that Nigerians are world beaters,” she said.

The First Lady also praised the players, head coach Akeem Busari and the technical crew for their teamwork, dedication and hard work.

“Through your team spirit, dedication and hard work, Nigeria is again the toast of the world,” she added.

The Flamingos made history after recovering from a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match to win six consecutive games and claim their first title in the tournament.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

They subsequently defeated Puerto Rico 2-0 and defending champions Korea DPR 3-1 before progressing to the knockout rounds.

Nigeria beat Mexico 2-1 in the round of 16 and edged Venezuela in the quarter-finals, with Azeezat Oduntan scoring the decisive penalty in the 89th minute.

The team then produced one of their best performances of the competition, defeating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-finals to reach the final for the first time.

Against Japan, Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring in the 39th minute before Oluebube Umejiaku doubled Nigeria’s lead shortly after the restart.

Japan pulled one back through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Nigerian girls held on through the closing stages to secure the title.

The victory marked a significant improvement on Nigeria’s previous best performance at the competition, a bronze-medal finish in 2022.

It also ended Japan’s hopes of winning a second title. The Asian side had previously won the competition in 2014 and finished runners-up in 2010 and 2016.

Nigeria’s triumph is the first time an African country has won the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, giving the continent a landmark achievement in women’s football.

World.title: U-17 Women’s World Cup: Flamingos Coach reveals philosophy behind Nigeria’s historic win
World.content:
For Nigeria U-17 women’s team head coach Akeem Busari, winning the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco was not simply about having the most talented players in the squad; It was about character, mindset, attitude and merit, values he insisted every member of his team had to demonstrate before earning a place in the starting line-up.

That philosophy became increasingly evident as the Flamingos moved from an opening-day disappointment against Poland to a historic triumph over Japan in the final. Coach Busari was willing to make changes, trust players who had initially been on the fringes and reward those who continued to show commitment, regardless of their status in the squad.

Those decisions were especially evident in the emergence of Oluebube Umejiaku and Awawu Bashiru, two players who did not begin the tournament as regular starters but ended it among Nigeria’s most influential performers.

Umejiaku started the competition on the bench, playing second fiddle to captain Harmony Chidi in the attacking setup. However, she finished as the tournament’s arguably standout player, winning the golden ball, scoring the decisive goal in the final against Japan and playing a major role in Nigeria’s historic success.

Her journey mirrored the Flamingos’ remarkable campaign. She came off the bench to score in Nigeria’s opening match against Poland, although her effort could not prevent a 2-1 defeat. Further goals against Korea DPR and Mexico, followed by her decisive contribution in the final, helped Nigeria secure the title.

The Flamingos became the first team in the competition’s history to lose their opening match and still lift the trophy.

Speaking to FIFA after the final, Busari’s faith in giving players their opportunities was reflected in Umejiaku’s account of how she remained patient while waiting for her moment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Every time I went to training and every time I slept, I told God that I was praying for all the people who are starting. But when I wanted to start, I just told God that it is my time,” an ecstatic Umejiaku said.

The forward also recalled the squad’s reaction after the defeat to Poland, explaining how the players challenged themselves to approach every subsequent fixture with the intensity of a final.

“When we lost the first game against Poland, everybody said we needed to wake up because we didn’t come here to look at anybody’s face, and we have to take every game as a final. We don’t downgrade anything; we play, and we put all our best into every game.”

Awawu Bashiru provided another example of Busari’s selection philosophy paying off. The Confluence Queens forward had played just 77 minutes between Nigeria’s opening defeat to Poland and the quarter-final against Venezuela. Still, her opportunity eventually arrived when the coach handed her a starting role against Brazil in the semi-final.

She responded with a brilliant brace in the 3-1 victory, before scoring Nigeria’s opening goal in the final against Japan as the Flamingos completed their historic run to the title.

Bashiru credited the team’s collective discipline, teamwork and willingness to follow the coaches’ instructions for their success, while describing the triumph as a moment of pride for the country.

“I’m so happy, I’m so excited, and I’m so grateful,” she said. “The teamwork, instruction and listening to our coaches are why we got the goals and why we won the final. We are history-makers. We made Nigeria, and the millions of people there, proud.”

Busari: Character, attitude and merit come first

For Busari, the decisions to introduce fresh faces and adjust his starting line-up were not coaching masterstrokes but reflected the standards he expected from every player.

The coach explained that talent alone was never enough to guarantee playing time. His selections were influenced by the players’ mentality, attitude, character and what they demonstrated in their efforts to earn a place in the team.

“No matter how good you are, I’m a coach that plays on character,” Busari said when discussing the changes that proved crucial to Nigeria’s campaign.

“It’s all about mindset, attitude and merit; if they’re there, you get your playing time. If they’re not there, you’re waiting to come in. As a coach, we want everyone to wire up and play together.”

That approach allowed different players to take responsibility at important moments, ensuring Nigeria were not overly dependent on a handful of individuals. Umejiaku and Bashiru’s contributions were among the clearest examples. Still, their rise also reflected a wider team culture in which every player understood that an opportunity could come at any stage.

Busari’s emphasis on collective responsibility and competition for places helped the Flamingos find solutions throughout the tournament, particularly after the setback against Poland. Rather than letting the defeat derail their campaign, the team regrouped, made the necessary adjustments, and won their next five matches to become world champions.

Busari: ‘This is a turnaround for Africa’

Nigeria’s victory means more than the trophy. The Flamingos became the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first country from the continent to triumph at a FIFA women’s tournament.

The achievement also continued Nigeria’s remarkable record at the U-17 global finals, ensuring that a Nigerian team, male or female, has won the competition in each of the previous five decades.

For Busari, the triumph represents an important breakthrough for African football and a powerful source of motivation for the next generation. He believes Nigeria’s success has demonstrated that African teams can compete at the highest level of youth football and challenge the traditional powerhouses.

His players share that ambition. Umejiaku was particularly emphatic that the victory should mark the beginning of more success for African teams on the global stage.

“I’m very happy because now we have broken the chain,” she added. “In Africa we always win – that’s a promise. We’ve won, and now we’ll be winning and winning, that’s just it. We thank God for everything.”

Bashiru also promised that Nigeria would return to future editions of the competition with the same energy and determination, insisting that the historic achievement should be a platform for even greater success.

“We can expect more from Nigeria,” she said. “We are winning, and we’ll bring the same energy, the same zing, at the next U-17 Women’s World Cup.”

Busari, meanwhile, believes the title will have a lasting impact on youth football development across Africa, showing the continent is making progress and can compete for the biggest honours.

“This is a turnaround for Africa,” he concluded. “In terms of youth-age football, it’s improving, and here we could really come and compete. Being a champion is going to go a long way to really motivate us, and we are sending a signal, a message to the world that Africa is really coming.”

For the Flamingos coach, the triumph was the reward for a team that embraced competition, responded to setbacks and understood that nobody was guaranteed a place without earning it.

His insistence on character, attitude and merit helped create an environment where players who began on the bench could become match-winners when their opportunity arrived.

Nigeria’s historic victory in Morocco was therefore not just a story of goals and individual brilliance. It was also a story of a coach who trusted his philosophy, a squad that bought into his demands and a group of young players who delivered when their country needed them the most.

World.title: FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup Triumph: Dikko, Olopade, Ahmadu reward Flamingos
World.content:
The Flamingos of Nigeria, champions of the world, were given a special treat in Rabat, Morocco, on Saturday night after their historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, where they defeated Japan to become the first African team to win the competition.

The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, and the Director General, Bukola Olopade, hosted the team to celebrate their remarkable achievement.

The reception was also attended by the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, and Saleh Ahmadu, a sponsor of the National Sports Commission.

It was an opportunity to celebrate a group of young players who have made the country proud and delivered a historic moment for Nigerian women’s football. In a further show of appreciation, Mr Ahmadu rewarded the team with a cash gift of $50,000.

It was a welcome gesture for the players and officials, whose hard work, commitment and determination throughout the tournament ultimately brought the trophy home.

There was also good news concerning the outstanding bonuses owed to the team. The Presidency, through the National Sports Commission, facilitated the payment of the Flamingos’ bonuses covering their journey from the preliminary qualifying rounds through to the final match, which they won spectacularly with a 2-1 victory over 2014 champions Japan.

Ikpeme dedicates Flamingos’ World Cup triumph to President Tinubu

Meanwhile, the Acting General Secretary of the Nigeria Football Federation, Emmanuel Ikpeme, has dedicated Saturday night’s FIFA World Cup win by the Flamingos to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This victory has been made possible by the support and special love shown to all the National Teams at every point in time by His Excellency, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR. The Father of the Nation has continued to be a father for all, and we are grateful for his love and encouragement all the time.”

Mr Tinubu directed the National Sports Commission to offset the outstanding bonuses and allowances of the players and officials following Saturday night’s historic win, which made Nigeria the only African country to have won the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup trophy.

The feat also sets Nigeria apart as the only African country to have won the FIFA U17 World Cup in both the men’s and women’s categories. The male team, Golden Eaglets, remains a five-time world champion: 1985, 1993, 2007, 2013 and 2015.

World.title: Kogi announced N7bn upgrade of PHCs, won’t provide details while clinics remain uncompleted, understaffed
World.content:
From a distance, the OAU Primary Health Centre in Ojoku, Ankpa Local Government Area of Kogi State, appeared newly built when PREMIUM TIMES returned to the facility on 6 May 2026.

Its blue-and-white exterior had been painted, the roof was in place, and doors and windows had been fitted.

But a closer inspection revealed signs of unfinished work. The clinic was locked, with no health workers or patients in sight. No clinical services were being provided.

PREMIUM TIMES had first visited the facility in December 2025 and found that it was not providing clinical services.

Aminu Nuhu, head of the Department of Health Services, Ankpa Local Government Council, identified OAU PHC Ojoku as one of six facilities selected for revitalisation in the council area.

He said the council was still searching for health workers to deploy to some of the revitalised facilities.

“Those that have been revitalised, we are looking for staff to put in those facilities,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, the absence of personnel was not the only problem.

Mr Nuhu said a borehole had been drilled at the facility but could not supply water because there was no electricity or solar installation to power the pump.

“They have completed it, but we are expecting them to put it into operation,” he said.

Nearly five months after the first visit, PREMIUM TIMES returned to the facility and found that clinical services had still not commenced.

A security guard at the facility said there was no medical equipment inside.

“There is nothing inside,” he said. “It’s just the building.”

The situation at OAU PHC Ojoku was among the problems uncovered during a months-long PREMIUM TIMES investigation into the Kogi State government’s multibillion-naira primary healthcare revitalisation programme.

The investigation examined whether the government’s investment had translated into functional health facilities capable of delivering essential services to residents.

It found unfinished rehabilitation work, inadequate staffing, lack of basic infrastructure and health workers operating from temporary accommodation, despite the government’s announcement that dozens of facilities had been revitalised and commissioned.

The N7 billion promise

In January 2025, the Kogi State government announced that it had committed over N7 billion, with support from the World Bank, to upgrade 88 PHCs across the state’s 21 LGAs.

The announcement was made during the formal handover of project sites to contractors at the Model PHC in Felele, Lokoja.

Governor Ahmed Ododo, represented by the Commissioner for Health, Abdulazeez Adams, said the intervention would contribute to the upgrading of more than 150 PHCs into functional Level 2 facilities.

The contractors were directed to complete the projects within four months.

On 7 November 2025, the state government announced the commissioning of 80 revitalised PHCs.

Muazu Musa, executive director of the Kogi State Primary Health Care Development Agency, said the facilities had been transformed from Level 1 to Level 2.

Under the federal government’s 2025 HOPE-PHC Programme Operations Manual, functional Level 2 PHCs are expected to provide 24-hour health services, including basic emergency obstetric and neonatal care.

The programme’s verification framework also covers the availability of skilled birth attendants, reliable electricity or backup solar power, functional toilets with water and access to clean water.

These requirements are intended to ensure that upgraded facilities can provide essential healthcare services beyond improvements to their physical structures.

However, the Kogi State Government did not provide PREMIUM TIMES with the complete list of the 80 facilities it announced as commissioned.

As a result, the newspaper could not independently establish whether the facilities inspected during the investigation were among those officially commissioned.

Following the money: N6.09 billion in four contracts

A review of Kogi State procurement disclosures revealed four infrastructure contracts covering 88 PHCs.

The contracts had a combined value of N6.1 billion and were awarded to Multi Purpose Errand Mens Services Ltd, QSA Nigeria Ltd, Inknuel Ltd and Base-SAN Ventures Nigeria Ltd.

The records showed that N5.5 billion, representing approximately 90.6 per cent of the combined contract value, had been recorded as paid to the four contractors.

PREMIUM TIMES could not independently verify the payments against bank statements or government treasury records. The figures are therefore described as amounts recorded ‘as paid’ in the procurement disclosure.

The procurement records also revealed a discrepancy in the geographical coverage of the contracts.

Although the state government said the intervention covered all 21 LGAs, the descriptions of the four contract lots identified only 20 distinct LGAs.

Kogi LGA, whose headquarters is Koton-Karfe, was not listed in any of the four lots.

This does not necessarily mean the LGA was excluded from the intervention. However, without the complete list of the 88 beneficiary facilities, PREMIUM TIMES could not determine whether the omission occurred in the procurement summary or reflected the actual distribution of the projects.

The combined contract value of N6.1 billion was also lower than the government’s announced commitment of over N7 billion.

The available records did not explain what additional activities or expenditures accounted for the difference.

Separately, the state’s 2025 fourth-quarter Budget Implementation Report recorded a final budget of N8.205 billion for the broader Immunisation Plus and Malaria Progress by Accelerating Coverage and Transforming Services (IMPACT) programme.

The report showed year-to-date expenditure of approximately N7.818 billion.

However, the IMPACT programme covers activities beyond the four infrastructure contracts. Its expenditure cannot therefore be treated as the amount spent specifically on the 88 PHC rehabilitation projects.

The records available to PREMIUM TIMES did not reconcile these figures.

Questions over Lot D contractor

One of the contracts, identified as Lot D, was awarded to Base-SAN Ventures Nigeria Ltd for work covering 23 PHCs across Ankpa, Olamaboro, Omala, Ofu, Dekina, Ibaji and Bassa LGAs.

The procurement disclosure recorded approximately N1.069 billion as paid under the contract.

During a follow-up visit to PHC Ankpa, PREMIUM TIMES found a project signboard identifying “BASESAN VENTURE NIG LTD” as the contractor responsible for upgrading the facility.

The variation between the company name on the signboard and the name in the procurement disclosure raised questions about the contractor’s precise legal identity.

Separately, publicly available corporate information reviewed by PREMIUM TIMES identified BASESAN Ventures Limited, with registration number RC 822294, and listed a person named “Sanni Eggidi A” as a person with significant control.

The newspaper could not independently establish whether BASESAN Ventures Limited, Base-SAN Ventures Nigeria Ltd and the company named on the project signboard were the same legal entity or related companies.

PREMIUM TIMES subsequently contacted Sanni Abdulraheem, the member representing Ajaokuta Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, seeking clarification on whether he had any connection to BASESAN Ventures Limited.

The similarity between the name in the corporate information and that of the lawmaker does not establish that they refer to the same individual.

The newspaper also sought clarification on the relationship between the companies and requested records relating to the 23 PHCs covered by Lot D, including their approved scopes of work, completion status and inspection and certification documents.

The lawmaker’s response has not been received as of publication.

Missing records, unanswered questions

Beyond the discrepancies in contract values and geographical coverage, the procurement disclosure did not identify all 88 PHCs individually.

It also did not specify the approved scope of work, contract value or payment status for each facility.

The state government did not provide PREMIUM TIMES with the complete list of the 80 PHCs announced as commissioned in November 2025.

Without these documents, it was impossible to match the facilities covered by the contracts with those announced as completed and commissioned.

The absence of facility-level inspection reports and completion certificates also prevented independent verification of what was approved, delivered, and certified at individual project sites.

These gaps do not, on their own, establish diversion of funds or failure to execute the contracts. They do, however, limit public scrutiny of the government’s claims about the intervention.

Between December 2025 and September 2026, PREMIUM TIMES inspected and revisited health facilities across Ankpa, Lokoja and Ajaokuta LGAs.

The newspaper interviewed health workers, residents, and government officials; examined project signboards; and reviewed procurement and budget documents.

The findings concern facilities that local officials or site-level evidence linked to the state intervention.

PHCC Ankpa: services running, problems persist

At the Primary Health Care Centre in Ankpa (PHCC Ankpa), clinical services were ongoing when PREMIUM TIMES first visited.

The facility provided antenatal care, routine immunisation, family planning, outpatient consultations and delivery services.

Momo Oneshona, the officer-in-charge, said the centre could receive as many as 70 patients on Mondays for immunisation, antenatal care and general consultations.

However, the facility faced significant operational challenges.

Health workers said there was no running water, grid electricity or solar power for general operations.

The available solar installation served the vaccine refrigerators.

“We don’t have solar, we don’t have water here, we don’t have light,” Mrs Oneshona said.

She explained that workers sterilised reusable instruments by boiling them over gas or ordinary stoves.

During the initial inspection, the laboratory was padlocked and appeared dusty.

The facility also faced staff shortages.

“We have a shortage of staff,” Mrs Oneshona said. “They retire; no replacement.”

She estimated that about seven workers were actively providing services, including three Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs) and two Junior CHEWS.

According to Mrs Oneshona, the shortage of personnel and absence of a security guard meant the facility could not operate overnight.

This fell short of the 24-hour service expectations for functional Level 2 PHCs.

Contractors left unfinished work

Beyond the operational challenges, PREMIUM TIMES observed an unfinished building undergoing rehabilitation within the facility’s compound.

Doors and window frames had been removed and piled inside, while openings in the walls and roof remained exposed.

“They scattered our place and went away,” Mrs Oneshona said. “We only saw them working, then they departed.”

Mr Nuhu, the Ankpa LGA health official, confirmed that PHCC Ankpa was among six facilities selected for revitalisation.

He said construction workers left the project between December 2025 and January 2026 and had not returned by the time of the newspaper’s initial inspection.

Of the six facilities, he identified PHC Emekutu as the only one he considered fully completed at the time of his interview.

Mr Nuhu also described broader staffing challenges across Ankpa LGA.

He estimated that the council had 68 functioning PHCs but only about 50 to 55 per cent of the personnel required to operate them effectively.

According to him, 12 facilities relied entirely on volunteers, while six or seven retired health workers had been retained to keep services running.

Laboratory affected by rainwater

When PREMIUM TIMES returned to PHCC Ankpa on 28 September 2026, the laboratory was accessible.

Rain had fallen shortly before the visit.

Water was visible on sections of the laboratory floor, while damp and discoloured patches appeared on parts of the walls.

A project signboard at the facility identified the work as the “Upgrading of Primary Health Care Centre Ankpa – Ankpa LGA”.

It named Kogi State IMPACT Project 2024 as the client and listed “BASESAN VENTURE NIG LTD” as the contractor.

The procurement disclosure separately identified Base-SAN Ventures Nigeria Ltd as the contractor for Lot D, covering 23 PHCs across seven LGAs.

Although the signboard linked PHCC Ankpa to the IMPACT project, PREMIUM TIMES could not obtain the facility’s approved scope of work, valuation, payment records or completion certificate.

Lokongoma PHC: Renovation followed by more construction

At PHC Lokongoma, in Lokoja, local health officials linked the facility to the state’s revitalisation programme.

When PREMIUM TIMES visited on 13 May 2026, the centre had a new perimeter fence, a paved compound, freshly painted walls and red roofing.

However, the gate was locked when the reporter arrived at approximately 5:45 p.m.

A nearby shop owner said health workers generally left between 2 p.m. and 3 p.m.

According to the resident, the clinic provided antenatal care, deliveries, routine immunisation and treatment for minor illnesses when open.

PREMIUM TIMES did not obtain the facility’s duty roster to independently verify its operating hours.

The resident also said the clinic had been renovated less than a year earlier.

Subsequent images showed that construction activities continued after the May inspection.

Images dated 9 July 2026 showed work on sections of the red roof, additional structures and paving.

By 20 July, further images showed blue roofing, more structures and additional paving.

The images establish that further work took place after the May visit.

However, PREMIUM TIMES could not determine whether services continued during construction or whether the successive works formed part of the same project.

The available records also did not establish what each round of construction covered, who financed it or whether the work had been inspected and certified.

Ganaja PHC: Eight years in school classrooms

At Ganaja, in Ajaokuta LGA, health workers were still providing healthcare services from two borrowed classrooms inside UBE Standard College when PREMIUM TIMES visited.

Local health officials linked the facility to the state’s revitalisation programme.

Health workers said flooding had forced them to abandon their original building nearly eight years earlier.

Since then, they had been operating from the temporary accommodation.

“We were on the other side before, but flood covered that place,” the Officer-in-Charge, identified as Ms Aminu, said. “We are just managing this place as a temporary site.”

Across the road from the school, the former PHC showed signs of prolonged abandonment.

Vegetation had overtaken parts of the compound, while refuse had accumulated around the deteriorating building.

Inside the school, one classroom served as an office and consultation room.

Medical supplies, vaccine carriers, desks, chairs and patient records occupied the limited space.

The arrangement constrained the services health workers could provide.

Ms Aminu said the classrooms could not accommodate patient admissions or maternity services.

She estimated that approximately 10 workers were attached to the facility but said there was no midwife.

As a result, pregnant women requiring delivery services were referred elsewhere.

Ms Aminu said a replacement PHC was being constructed elsewhere in Ganaja.

She estimated that the project was about 70 per cent complete.

However, PREMIUM TIMES could not independently verify the estimate because the reporter could not locate and inspect the construction site.

Ms Aminu could not provide sufficiently precise directions, and no one was available to accompany the reporter.

She also could not provide a completion date or indicate when health workers would relocate.

When PREMIUM TIMES returned in September 2026, the clinic was still operating from the school classrooms.

Nearly eight years after flooding displaced the original facility, health workers and patients were still waiting for a permanent building.

The situation also raised questions about whether the replacement project had adequately considered the flooding that forced the relocation.

PREMIUM TIMES did not establish the cause of the original flooding or attribute it specifically to climate change.

The documents reviewed did not include a flood-risk, environmental or climate-vulnerability assessment showing what safeguards had been incorporated into the replacement project.

Commissioned, but were the facilities ready?

The Kogi State government’s November 2025 announcement that 80 PHCs had been commissioned suggested substantial progress in its healthcare revitalisation programme.

However, findings from facilities inspected by PREMIUM TIMES revealed gaps between infrastructure development and the delivery of functional healthcare services.

At OAU PHC Ojoku, a newly painted building remained without clinical services during follow-up visits.

At PHCC Ankpa, patients continued receiving care despite unfinished rehabilitation work, staffing shortages and inadequate water and electricity supply.

At Lokongoma, additional construction was documented months after an earlier renovation.

At Ganaja, health workers continued operating from school classrooms while awaiting a permanent facility.

Local officials or site-level evidence linked these facilities to the state’s intervention.

However, because the complete commissioning list was unavailable, PREMIUM TIMES could not establish whether any of the four facilities was among the 80 announced as commissioned.

The newspaper also could not obtain facility-level inspection reports or completion certificates showing what had been assessed and certified before commissioning.

These gaps leave important questions unanswered about the criteria used to declare facilities ready, the work completed at individual sites and whether the upgrades translated into the services expected of Level 2 PHCs.

Government fails to provide project records

PREMIUM TIMES sought explanations and supporting documents from the Kogi State government before completing the investigation.

On 15 May 2026, the newspaper submitted written requests under Nigeria’s Freedom of Information Act 2011 to the Kogi State Ministry of Health and the Kogi State Primary Health Care Development Agency.

The requests sought an inventory of PHCs; details of revitalisation and infrastructure projects; the identities of beneficiary facilities and contractors; contract sums; project status; Basic Health Care Provision Fund disbursements; staffing information; and facility operational records.

The newspaper followed up through telephone calls and WhatsApp messages with the Commissioner for Health and Aisha Mohammed, who identified herself as secretary and personal assistant to the executive director of the State’s primary healthcare agency.

When the requests did not produce substantive responses, PREMIUM TIMES contacted the Commissioner for Information and Communications, Kingsley Fanwo.

The newspaper informed him of the outstanding requests and asked him to respond on behalf of the government or help obtain answers from the relevant agencies.

Calls, WhatsApp messages and a text message were sent to Mr Fanwo, including a reminder that the report was being finalised and that the government’s response could still be included.

By publication time, the state government had not provided the complete schedule of the 88 facilities, the list of 80 commissioned PHCs, facility-level scopes of work, inspection reports or completion certificates.

World.title: Tinubu condoles with Niger junta leader over father’s death
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to Niger Republic’s military leader, Abdourahamane Tiani, over the death of his father, Elhadji Hassane.

Mr Hassane died on Thursday, 5 November, at the age of 110.

In a condolence message issued by presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, Mr Tinubu said the Nigerian government and people stood in solidarity with Niger during the period of mourning.

“The passing of a father brings a profound and deeply personal grief,” the president said, urging General Tiani to take solace in his father’s impact on the lives of others and his remarkable longevity.

Mr Tinubu said the deceased left behind a legacy of faith, honour and integrity.

“In this moment of mourning, I pray that you will find solace in the enduring legacy of faith, honour, and integrity that your father leaves behind, and in the knowledge that his long and fulfilled life was a blessing to all who knew him,” he said.

The president added that Nigeria stood with Mr Tiani and the government and people of Niger Republic during the period of grief.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

READ ALSO: Jigawa resettles returnee farmers from Niger Republic after 47 years of dispute

He prayed that Almighty Allah would grant the deceased “Al-Jannah Firdaus” and comfort his bereaved family and loved ones.

The condolence message comes amid strained diplomatic relations between Nigeria and Niger following the July 2023 military coup that ousted the country’s civilian government and the subsequent withdrawal of Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in January 2025.

Niger’s military leader has repeatedly accused Nigeria of conspiring with France to destabilise his country, including allegations that Abuja was facilitating the establishment of terrorist bases in its north-western and north-eastern regions. Nigeria has consistently described the accusations as baseless, insisting that it remains committed to regional peace and security.

World.title: 2027: Collect politicians’ money but vote your conscience, Makinde tells Nigerians
World.content:
The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has urged Nigerians to collect money offered by politicians during election campaigns but vote according to their conscience in the 2027 general election.

Mr Makinde gave the advice on Saturday in Bauchi State during the flag-off of the APM presidential campaign, where he urged voters not to allow financial inducements to influence their electoral choices.

“Don’t bother at all when they bring money, it is your money. Collect it, spend it, but vote your heart. And I know your heart is with us and with APM,” he told supporters.

The Oyo State Governor said Nigerians dissatisfied with the country’s current direction must support his proposed Reset Agenda, which he said would address hunger, insecurity and exclusion from governance.

He identified hunger as the biggest problem confronting the country and argued that the situation required a fundamental change in economic policies and governance.

“Our people are hungry. Because we’re hungry, should we reset the economy? Because there is insecurity, should we reset the security architecture? Because the majority of our people are not allowed to participate, should we reset the socio-political environment in Nigeria?” he asked.

Mr Makinde said Nigerians who were unhappy with the lack of inclusion, transparency and sincerity in government had only one option: to reset the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“If you are not happy with the way things are in our country today, if you’re not happy that there’s not enough inclusivity, if you’re not happy that your government cannot tell you the truth, they cannot handle our issues with sincerity, then there’s only one path for us. And the path is to reset Nigeria,” he said.

Bala Mohammed demands inclusion

The campaign flag-off was attended by the APM National Leader and Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed, who urged Nigerians to support Mr Makinde’s presidential ambition.

Mr Mohammed said he and the presidential candidate left the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) after experiencing what he described as injustice within the party.

He described the APM as a new political platform through which they could pursue their ambitions and promote a more inclusive political system.

The governor said Mr Makinde had the experience and capacity to lead Nigeria, citing his performance as governor of Oyo State.

He also said the presidential candidate’s proposed government of national unity would address tribalism, religious intolerance and political exclusion.

Mr Mohammed, however, urged Mr Makinde to ensure that Bauchi State and the North-east would not be marginalised if he won the presidency.

He called for fairness in federal appointments, insisting that government positions should reflect the country’s diversity and adhere to the federal character principle.

“There are over 100,000 positions to be filled, but they must not be occupied by one ethnic group alone or skewed in favour of one tribe,” he said.

The governor said appointments should balance merit with equitable representation, adding that leadership recruitment must reflect the interests of different sections of the country.

He also lamented the financial challenges facing Bauchi State, saying he did not want the state to remain disadvantaged after supporting the APM presidential candidate.

“We are even tired of being in the opposition. We have lost a lot. I know how much I suffered as the leader of the opposition. I do not want to come into government only to be marginalised and pushed aside again,” he said.

He added that Bauchi needed greater support to meet its financial obligations, including the payment of workers’ salaries.

APM promises inclusive government

Also speaking, the APM National Chairman, Yusuf Dantalle said the party’s Reset Agenda was designed to address what he described as deceit and hypocrisy in Nigerian politics.

He said the party intended to establish a government in which public office holders would be accountable and committed to the welfare of Nigerians, irrespective of their ethnic, religious or social backgrounds.

Mr Dantalle said the proposed administration would promote broader participation in governance and develop an agreed national programme to address the country’s challenges.

He also called for greater representation of women in political leadership, lamenting the limited number of women in the National Assembly and other decision-making institutions.

The chairman disclosed that the party had established a directorate dedicated to women’s affairs and engaged the National Assembly Joint Committee on the proposed special seats for women.

He commended the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, for initiating the proposal, although it did not receive the necessary legislative support.

The chairman urged Nigerians to scrutinise the party’s proposals, saying its leadership was prepared to answer difficult questions about its policies and commitments.

The APM campaign flag-off marks the beginning of the party’s mobilisation for the 2027 general election, with Mr Makinde seeking to sell his Reset Agenda as an alternative to the country’s current political and economic direction.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu campaigns in Rivers, commends Wike, Fubara reconciliation, slams Atiku
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday acknowledged the pivotal role of Rivers State voters in the 2023 presidential election that brought him into office, and sought their renewed backing in the 16 January 2027 election to consolidate his administration’s gains.

Speaking at a campaign rally at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, the president commended the large turnout and praised the reconciliation between Governor Siminalayi Fubara and his predecessor, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike.

The Rainbow Coalition, led by Wike, organised the rally, which brought together political leaders and supporters from across Rivers State and beyond.

President Tinubu said Governor Fubara demonstrated maturity, understanding and respect for the intervention of political elders in resolving the disagreement with his predecessor.

“During the political crisis caused by a misunderstanding in the family, I intervened on your behalf. I thank Governor Fubara, in particular, for his maturity, understanding, and respect for the wisdom of elders when we intervened. Fubara, you will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” the president said.

Turning to the economy, President Tinubu assured Nigerians that his administration’s reforms were putting the country on the path to prosperity.

He said the federal government was addressing inherited liabilities, including unpaid pensions and gratuities, to ensure that more families benefited from economic recovery.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The people who governed before us left unpaid pensions and gratuities running into billions and trillions of Naira. We are clearing that backlog so that every family is included and we can share in the prosperity,” he stated.

He said outstanding liabilities, like pensions and salaries owed in 27 of the 36 states, had been cleared, and beneficiaries were more certain of monthly payments.

“When those people talk about hunger, remember that I am cleaning up the mess they created. Atiku was one of them. Ask him how he built a private university while in office as Vice President in charge of our economy. Who funded the university for him? It was your money, your effort!” Mr Tinubu noted.

The president questioned the former vice president’s moral standing for seeking another opportunity to serve in public office.

“A man without moral integrity, latitude, and ethics has no business holding public office,” he added.

President Tinubu also used the occasion to present his manifesto for the 2027 election.

In his remarks, Vice President Kashim Shettima urged political leaders and supporters in Rivers State and across the South-South to support President Tinubu’s re-election, citing the administration’s performance and commitment to the region.

Mr Shettima said the economic indicators were encouraging, with the country’s reserves rising from about $3.9 billion to $60 billion in about three years.

He said Atiku’s economic recommendations should be ignored as he is “intellectually malnourished “, while the NDC candidate, Peter Obi, struggles with “political irrelevance ” and “mediocrity.”

Governor Fubara promised to deliver three million votes for Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

The governor assured the president of his full participation in the Rainbow Coalition and his recognition of the FCT Minister’s leadership.

“Under the guidance and leadership of FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, we will deliver not less than three million votes for you,” Mr Fubara declared.

The governor said political supporters from the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) were working together in harmony under the Rainbow Coalition.

“Thank you, Mr President, for standing by us at a most difficult time. A good gesture deserves reciprocity. As you have stood by us, we will stand by you,’’ he assured.

Earlier, in his welcome address, Mr Wike described the turnout as evidence of Rivers State’s support for the President’s re-election.

“Your Excellency, this is Rivers State’s rally. We did not mobilise anybody from any other state. You can see with your eyes that the people of Rivers State have already concluded and agreed that on January 16, they will vote for you,” he stated.

The FCT minister thanked President Tinubu for appointing Rivers State indigenes to his administration and cited federal projects in the state, including the Bonny–Bodo Road and the Federal University of Environment in Ogoniland.

“Since the inception of democracy in 1999, Rivers people have never had it this way. We have no less than 47 political appointments from Mr President. So, who is our brother? Our brother is Bola Ahmed Tinubu because he has identified with the people of Rivers State,” he said.

Mr Wike said the former Rivers State Governor and ADC Vice Presidential Candidate Rotimi Amaechi could not account for $39 million designated for the Karibi Whyte Specialist Hospital project and the budget for fumigating the state.

The grand rally at the 40,000-capacity Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium was packed, with the crowd spilling into the surrounding precincts.

Dignitaries at the rally included the First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu; the wife of the Vice President, Nana Shettima; Senate President Godswill Akpabio; Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas; APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda; and the Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari.

Also present were state governors, Senators Magnus Abe, Adams Oshiomhole and ex-Governor Ifeanyi Okowa, other members of the National Assembly, and the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila.

President Tinubu arrived in Port Harcourt after official engagements and a political rally in Akwa Ibom State, where he commissioned projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration.

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information & Strategy)

November 7, 2026

World.title: Tinubu congratulates Flamingos for winning FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos for making history as the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco.

The president, who received the cheering news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States, hailed Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the nation and a landmark achievement for African women’s football.

“What wonderful news to return home to! Our young girls have conquered the world and given Nigerians everywhere another reason to celebrate our great country.

“To our gallant Flamingos, I say congratulations. You have shown courage, discipline, determination and the Nigerian spirit of never giving up.

“I followed your journey throughout this tournament, and after your semi-final victory, you promised to bring the trophy home. Today, you have kept that promise. You believed in yourselves, fought for one another and carried our nation’s flag to the very top of the world.

“Your victory is an inspiration to millions of young Nigerian girls who dream of achieving greatness. You have shown them that with hard work, opportunity and determination, they too can reach the highest levels of achievement.

“Today, Nigeria celebrates you. You have written your names in gold, and your country is immensely proud of you.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The president particularly applauds Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku, whose goals secured the historic victory, while commending the entire squad for their exceptional teamwork throughout the tournament.

He also congratulates the coaching crew, the Nigeria Football Federation and the National Sports Commission for their contributions to the team’s success.

President Tinubu reaffirms his administration’s commitment to investing in grassroots sports development and expanding opportunities for young Nigerians, particularly girls, to discover, nurture and fulfil their potential.

“Congratulations once again, Flamingos. Thank you for making Nigeria proud.”

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information & Strategy)

November 7, 2026

World.title: Woman arrested over poisoning of co-wife’s children in Niger
World.content:
police badge

By Clare Nnabuike, Niger

The Niger State Police Command has arrested a woman, Mariya Abdullahi, over the alleged poisoning of her co-wife’s two children in Takuti community, Lapai Local Government Area, leaving one dead and the other receiving treatment in hospital.

The incident reportedly occurred at about 6 a.m. on Friday, November 6, 2026, when the suspect allegedly administered a substance suspected to be poison to the children, aged four and nine.

The victims reportedly became unconscious and were rushed to a nearby clinic, where one of them was confirmed dead. The other child was referred to a general hospital for further treatment and was responding to medical attention, according to the police.

The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, Wasiu Abiodun, disclosed the incident in a statement, adding that the suspect had been arrested and was undergoing interrogation.

Abiodun said preliminary police investigations indicated that Abdullahi claimed she was influenced by a friend to commit the alleged act because she could not bear a child for her husband.

According to the police spokesman, the suspect would be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Minna for further investigation and prosecution.

The police statement read: “On 6th November, 2026, at about 6 a.m., a report was received at Lapai Division that one Mariya Abdullahi of Takuti, via Lapai, administered some substance suspected to be poison to the children of her co-wife.

“Police operatives moved to the scene and discovered that the two children, aged nine and four, had been given the substance to drink, as a result of which they became unconscious.

“They were immediately rushed to a nearby clinic, but on arrival, one of the victims gave up the ghost, while the other was referred to the general hospital and is responding to treatment.

“The suspect was arrested and is undergoing further interrogation. She claimed that she was influenced by a friend to commit the act because she could not bear a child for her husband.

“She will soon be transferred to SCID Minna for diligent prosecution.”

World.title: U-17 WWC: Full list of award winners
World.content:
Nigeria’s Flamingos emerged as the champions of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on Saturday in Morocco.

The victory saw Nigeria secure the title, with Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scoring to seal the win for the Flamingos.

Japan’s Fuki Ito found the back of the net, but her effort was insufficient to prevent the Japanese side from losing the final.

Umejiaku’s impressive performances throughout the competition earned her the Golden Ball award, recognising her as the tournament’s best player.

Meanwhile, United States forward Maddie DiMaria won the Golden Boot after finishing as the tournament’s highest scorer with 12 goals.

DPR Korea’s Kim Son-gyong received the Golden Glove award for the best goalkeeper, while Japan was presented with the FIFA Fair Play Trophy.

Below is the full list of award winners at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup:

Golden Ball: Oluebube Umejiaku (Nigeria)

Oluebube Umejiaku (Nigeria) Silver Ball: Yu Jong-hyang (DPR Korea)

Yu Jong-hyang (DPR Korea) Bronze Ball: Fuki Ito (Japan)

Fuki Ito (Japan) Golden Boot: Maddie DiMaria (USA)

Maddie DiMaria (USA) Silver Boot: Yu Jong-hyang (DPR Korea)

Yu Jong-hyang (DPR Korea) Golden Glove: Kim Son-gyong (DPR Korea)

Kim Son-gyong (DPR Korea) FIFA Fair Play Trophy: Japan
