TCN said by virtue of Section 67 of the Electricity Act, 2023, the determination of the root cause of disturbances, shortfalls and interruptions on the national grid falls exclusively within the defined functions of the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO).

“IKEDC, like every other market participant, has no authority to make such determinations, and NISO has made none attributing the outages in IKEDC’s notice to TCN,” it said.



The company said NISO had already clarified the position in its public statement of November 5, attributing the current decline in power generation to constraints in gas supply to thermal power stations and reduced output from hydroelectric stations due to lower reservoir inflows.



According to TCN, NISO explained that the development reduced available generation, which in turn reduced energy allocated to Discos and led to fewer hours of supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks.

“The shortfall in supply to IKEDC’s customers is a consequence of reduced generation and the resulting allocation, not of any failure of TCN’s transmission network. TCN can only transmit the energy made available to it and cannot transmit energy that is not generated,” it said.



TCN said records for all feeders supplying IKEDC confirmed the picture painted by NISO. Of the interruptions recorded on November 1 and 2, it said 68 per cent were frequency-control load shedding arising from low generation, 26 per cent were due to IKEDC’s non-compliance with load allocation by the National Control Centre (NCC) of NISO, or to faults and works on IKEDC’s own network, while the remaining 6 per cent were TCN planned maintenance, switching or a line limitation.



“None of the recorded interruptions was a TCN equipment fault or trip,” it added.

Of the 46 interruptions recorded on the 33kV feeders named in IKEDC’s notice, TCN said 29 were frequency-control load shedding arising from low generation and 14 were recorded against IKEDC – nine for non-compliance with load allocation and five for faults or trips on its own network.

According to the TCN, the other three were scheduled for maintenance on the Ogba-Alimosho line on November 1.

TCN urged IKEDC and other Discos to “desist forthwith from making unfounded claims about the causes of supply shortfalls to their customers,” saying such claims misinformed customers, undermined public confidence and obscured the real challenges to be resolved by the relevant stakeholders.

World.title: Government, Corporate Activities Lift NGX Overall Market Capitalisation to N226.38tn in First 10 Months of 2026
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

The overall market capitalisation of listed securities rose to a record N226.38 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, driven by increased government and corporate activity on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), according to a report by NGX.

The figure, recorded as of October 30, 2026, rose to N76.64 trillion, or 51.2 per cent, from N149.74 trillion recorded at the close of trading in 2025.

The total covered four categories: Equities, bonds, securities on the Non-Interest Finance Board and exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

The equities segment comprises more than 150 stocks, while debt securities include commercial papers, corporate bonds and debentures, Federal Government bonds, and state and local government bonds.

On a month-on-month basis, the overall market capitalisation increased by N2.98 trillion, or 1.34 per cent, from N223.4 trillion at the end of September 2026.

The Exchange has witnessed increased listings of federal and state government debt securities, strong corporate earnings, improved economic indicators and renewed investor interest in stocks with strong fundamentals.

According to NGX data, equities accounted for the largest share of the overall market capitalisation at approximately 72.9 per cent, followed by bonds at 26.46 per cent.

Securities on the Non-Interest Finance Board and ETFs accounted for 0.59 per cent and 0.02 per cent, respectively.

A breakdown showed that equities market capitalisation rose to N165.114 trillion at the end of October 2026, up 66.5 per cent from N99.18 trillion at the close of 2025.

The market capitalisation of listed bonds increased by 18.6 per cent to N59.89 trillion from N50.51 trillion at the end of the previous year.

The federal government’s bonds, the largest component of the bond market, rose to N57.2 trillion from N49.32 trillion, while corporate bonds and debentures increased to N2.03 trillion from N893.9 billion.

State and local government bonds stood at N571.05 billion at the end of October 2026, up about 91.1 per cent from N298.77 billion at the close of 2025.

NGX data also showed that the market capitalisation of securities on the Non-Interest Finance Board, which commenced operations in July 2026, increased to N1.33 trillion in October from N1.29 trillion in September.

However, ETF market capitalisation declined by 1.4 per cent to N42.24 billion from N42.845 billion at the close of 2025.

The Exchange’s statistics included commercial papers among its debt securities for the first time in August 2026.

Market analysts attributed the growth recorded on the NGX in 2026 to the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) foreign exchange reforms, the federal government’s removal of the petrol subsidy, banking sector reforms and strong earnings by listed companies.

They also cited easing inflation, the CBN’s Monetary Policy Committee’s reduction of the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 23 per cent, and improved financial system liquidity as factors supporting the market’s performance.

The foreign exchange reforms were also credited with supporting increased capital inflows and greater exchange rate stability.

The federal government has increased borrowing to finance the 2026 budget, with some of the resulting debt securities listed on the NGX through the Debt Management Office (DMO).

NGX Group attributed the bullish trend to regulatory clarity, macroeconomic reforms and growing confidence among domestic and foreign investors, describing the gains as placing the Nigerian market among the best-performing globally.

Market analysts similarly identified investor confidence, macroeconomic reforms and improved corporate performance as the principal drivers of the rally.

They cited renewed foreign portfolio investment, stronger company fundamentals and oversubscribed public offerings as indications of a more resilient and increasingly attractive Nigerian capital market.

The Managing Director of Financial Derivatives Company, Bismarck Rewane, had projected that equities market capitalisation could grow by about 190 per cent from N91 trillion to N262 trillion by 2026.

Rewane argued that prospective listings, including Dangote Refinery, which he valued at about $32 billion, and NNPC Limited, could help expand equities market capitalisation from about 20 per cent of gross domestic product to nearly 80 per cent over the medium term.

World.title: Offa Bank Robbery: Kwara Govt Drops 18 Criminal Charges against Saraki, Ahmed, Add Two New Charges
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The Kwara State Government has filed an amendment to its 20-count charge against two former governors of the state, Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki and Alhaji Abdulfatai Ahmed, over the 2018 Offa bank robbery case.

The government, however, dropped 18 of the original charges while retaining only two, and adding two new charges.

In the amended charge sheet with Charge Number: KWS/114C/2026 signed by the State Attorney General, Senior Ibrahim Sulyman (SAN), which was sighted by THISDAY on Friday, the government reduced the total number of charges to four.

In the new charge sheet, counts 1 and 2, accused Saraki, Ahmed, Yusuf Abdulwahab and Alabi Olalekan of “conspiring to belong to gang of thieves” and “belonging to gang of thieves”.

Also, counts 3 and 4 accused the quartet of concealment and disappearance of a “vehicle used for illegal purpose”.

A motion on notice for the amended charges dated November 6, 2026, has been filed by the prosecution and supported by a six-paragraph affidavit deposed to by Sulyman Mohammed-Jamiu, a litigation clerk in the office of the Kwara State AG.

With the new development, the Kwara State Government has dropped all charges relating to armed robbery concerning the Offa bank robbery case against the former President of the Senate, Saraki; Ahmed and the two other defendants who were aides to the immediate past governor.

It would be recalled that at the last sitting of the State High Court on the case on November 5, 2026, the judge, Justice Osuolale Ajayi reserved his ruling on the issue of whether he could continue with the arraignment when the defendant has a pending application for a stay of proceedings on the matter at the Court of Appeal.

The Court of Appeal on November 3, 2026 advised the lawyer to Ahmed, Mr J. A. Mumini (SAN), to make a formal application for the court to issue an order that the parties at the trial court should maintain status quo ante bellum, instead of the oral submission that he made to the court.

The appellate court then adjourned the case to November 12, 2026.

The case at the trial court which commenced in April 2026 has not proceeded to trial as the court is still mired in several preliminary issues which have been taken to the appellate court.

When contacted, a member of Saraki and Ahmed’s legal team described the struggle by the prosecution to press charges against the two former governors as “a mockery of the judicial process and an exercise in futility”.

The lawyer noted that it was “a funny turn of events to accuse two former governors of belonging to a gang of thieves.

“This is not just a disgrace to the institution of governorship of our dear state; it is also a drag on the name of our dear state in the mud.

“And all this struggle is just because the present government desperately wants to see the former governors in the dock. They moved from the case of armed robbery to joining a gang of thieves.

“It is clear that the government is bereft of ideas on how to achieve its aim”.

The lawyer added that, “The present charge sheet like the one they abandoned will record no success.

“It will fall like a pack of badly arranged cards. We will meet them in court.

“This is why we believe the AG should be more assertive in advising his principal to stop chasing shadows.

“They must have resorted to this new amendment to the charges after realising they will not be able to achieve their aims with the unwieldy list of charges earlier filed. The new charges will not turn out better”.

Attempts by THISDAY to get the State AG and other lawyers to the government to respond to the new development concerning the amended charges were not successful.

However, sources close to the state government told THISDAY that the amendment came as a result of advice by the AG and other members of the prosecution team that the former charge sheet cannot help the government to nail the defendants.

World.title: Jonathan Accuses Nigerian Politicians of Desperation, Says They Behave as If They are Superhumans
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja

Former President Goodluck Jonathan has frowned upon the way Nigerian politicians conducted their affairs, saying they behaved as if they owned the world or the country.

Jonathan made the remark at the funeral service of Elder Freeman Ayeimieye, husband of the Bayelsa State Chief Judge, Justice Matilda Ayeimieye, held at St Peter’s Deanery in Yenagoa.

He challenged Nigerian politicians seeking power in the 2027 general election to reflect on the legacy they intended to leave behind, asking whether they wanted to be remembered for killing people and burning down houses in their desperation to win elections.

The former president said political power was temporary and cautioned those seeking elective offices to exercise restraint in their campaign rhetoric and remember that ultimate power belongs to God.

He warned that no political office holder should take God’s mercy for granted or assume that power made them invincible.

“Some of them talk as if they own the world, but in reality, they are mere mortals – individuals. No matter how powerful you are, if you get lost today, nobody will remember you. Nobody cares about you. Nobody should think that he owns the world, Nigeria, or even his own family.

“Sometimes, you will be surprised that some of your children might not even vote for you. That is the funny thing about politics. So, we must tread carefully as all powers belong to God Almighty alone,” he said.

In his tribute to Ayeimieye, the former president said the deceased who was a lay reader in the Anglican Communion, lived a life worthy of remembrance and served as a pillar of the church.

Reflecting on the lessons of burial ceremonies, Jonathan said death was inevitable and urged people, particularly political leaders, to consider how they would be remembered when they were gone.

In his remarks, the state governor, Mr. Douye Diri, recalled the support the deceased gave his wife during her appointment as the Chief Judge of Bayelsa State, saying their interaction had left him with a positive impression of the late Ayeimieye.

The governor said his administration had enjoyed a peaceful working relationship with the judiciary under Justice Ayeimieye, adding that the achievements of his government were the product of cooperation among the three arms of government.

“Since that appointment, I have worked in peace and synergy with the Chief Judge of Bayelsa State and with the Judiciary. Any achievement of this government is because we have worked together. It is not me as governor alone. It is because we have worked together, the executive, legislature and the judiciary.”

In his sermon entitled ‘Seeking God’s Kingdom’, the Bishop of the Niger Delta West Diocese of the Anglican Church, Rev. Nexon Enekeme, cautioned Christians against making titles, positions and material wealth the central pursuit of life, noting that none of these would accompany anyone to the grave.

He urged the congregation to seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, assuring them that other things would follow.

Among those present at the event were the former First Lady Patience Jonathan, wives of the governor, Dr Gloria Diri and Justice Patience Diri; Deputy Governor of Bayelsa, Dr. Peter Akpe; members of the National Assembly; Deputy Speaker of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, Mr Michael Ogbere, and the Chief Judges of Rivers, Delta and Oyo states, alongside other government officials.

World.title: POLITICAL HIT? | UDM councillor shot dead after elections
World.content:
UDM councillor and former Nelson Mandela Bay deputy mayor Luxolo Namette was shot dead in Motherwell, Gqeberha, on Saturday, 7 November 2026. Image: X

The United Democratic Movement (UDM) fears a political motive behind the murder of its Nelson Mandela Bay councillor, Luxolo Namette, who died in a shooting in Motherwell, Gqeberha, on Saturday, 7 November.

The killing comes just three days after South Africa’s municipal elections, with the party now demanding a specialised police investigation.

Police investigate Motherwell murder

Eastern Cape police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana said officers found the body of a 45-year-old man with a gunshot wound to the head in Umnulu Street, NU9, at approximately 15:50.



“Suspects and motive are under investigation,” Gantana said.

SAPS Motherwell has opened a murder case and will release further details as the investigation progresses.

UDM fears political hit

UDM secretary-general Bulelani Bobotyane called on the Political Killings Task Team to investigate whether Namette’s political activities played a role in his death.

“While we do not wish to prejudge the outcome of the investigation, we cannot ignore the possibility that councillor Namette was targeted because of his political activities or his responsibilities as a public representative,” Bobotyane said.

Police have not confirmed a political motive.

Political killings under scrutiny

Namette’s murder follows a string of killings involving political figures during the election period.



On 1 November, the National Joint Operational and Intelligence Structure (NATJOINTS) reported 20 murders involving political representatives, party members and supporters. Police had made seven arrests.

In August, national police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe confirmed that the Political Killings Task Team had taken over the investigation into the murder of ANC councillor Sibusiso Khwela in KwaZulu-Natal.

“The PKTT will lead and coordinate the investigation,” Mathe said at the time.

The UDM now wants the same specialised attention for Namette’s case.

The former deputy mayor began his political career in the UDM Youth Vanguard before serving as chairperson of Nelson Mandela Bay’s Municipal Public Accounts Committee.

“He was one of our own, and his murder has shaken us to the core,” Bobotyane said.

World.title: Relebohile Mofokeng’s three R275 million options

Relebohile Mofokeng looks super comfortable in Belgium. Can the Bafana star secure a move to one of Europe’s top five leagues?

Mofokeng wanted in Europe’s top five leagues

World.title: DA emerges as the BIG winner from Elections 2026 – VIDEO
World.content:
The Democratic Alliance (DA) has emerged as one of the biggest winners of South Africa's 2026 Local Government Elections. Image: X @Our_DA

The Democratic Alliance (DA) has emerged as one of the biggest winners of South Africa’s 2026 Local Government Elections, increasing its national support and strengthening its position in several key municipalities.

However, despite its improved performance, the DA has not overtaken the African National Congress (ANC) as the country’s biggest political party.

WATCH | Five takeaways from South Africa’s 2026 Local Government Elections



With 99.8% of voting districts counted by early Sunday, 8 November, the ANC remained in first place nationally, while the DA occupied second position.

The results point to a changing political landscape, with smaller parties also gaining ground and coalition governments likely to play an increasingly important role in local government.

How did the DA perform?

The latest figures show that the DA secured 24.63% of the national vote, compared with 21.66% in the 2021 Local Government Elections.



This represents an increase of 2.97 percentage points.

The ANC, meanwhile, received 30.78% of the vote, a substantial decline from its 45.59% showing in 2021.

The figures underline the DA’s progress, but also show that the ANC remains ahead nationally.



2026 election results

Party 2026 vote 2021 vote ANC 30.78% 45.59% DA 24.63% 21.66% MK Party 9.74% Did not contest EFF 6.22% 10.31% ActionSA 5.68% 2.33% IFP 4.69% 5.64%

Figures are provisional, based on the IEC count at 09:10 on Sunday, 8 November.

Coalition governments could decide the outcome

One of the biggest stories emerging from the elections is the number of municipalities where no political party has secured an outright majority.

According to the latest available figures:

209 of South Africa’s 213 municipal councils had been declared.

74 councils had a party with a majority.

135 councils were hung.

This means political parties will have to negotiate with one another to establish governing coalitions in many municipalities.



For the DA, this presents both an opportunity and a challenge. Its improved national support could translate into greater influence in coalition negotiations, but securing the necessary council majorities will be crucial.

When will the final results be announced?

The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) is scheduled to officially announce the 2026 Local Government Elections results on Sunday, 8 November, from 18:00.

Until then, the figures remain subject to outstanding counting, verification and declaration processes.



Verdict: A good election for the DA?

The DA has reason to be pleased with its performance.

It increased its national support, while the ANC suffered a significant decline compared with the previous local government elections.

However, the DA remains South Africa’s second-largest political party nationally.



The real test will now be whether it can turn its improved electoral performance into greater control of municipalities and a stronger position in coalition governments.

Kaizer Chiefs looking to add more players in next transfer

World.title: Holiday jobs: Five steps every young South African needs to know
World.content:
Getting a job over the festive holiday can be fun, as well as a learning experience. Image: Pexels

The festive season is just around the corner. For young South Africans looking to gain work experience, develop their skills or earn some money – or all three! – it’s the perfect time to sink your teeth into your first holiday job.

Even though it might only be a seasonal position, i.e. a temporary gig, it’s still important for you to know what you’re getting yourself into. This means understanding your rights as an employee, from working hours to payment.

YOUR #1 HOLIDAY JOB GUIDE

If you’ve managed to secure employment over the festive season, ensure you follow these five steps:



1. READ THE CONTRACT THOROUGHLY

Before signing any contract, ensure that you read through it thoroughly. After all, you need to understand what your role entails, the payment amount (at least the minimum wage), working hours, and whom you can approach for additional training or questions. Other things to consider include overtime and payment on public holidays.

Ultimately, reading through the contract can save yourself the trouble of being bound to obligations that you didn’t agree to.

2. UNDERSTAND YOUR PAYSLIP

Check your payslip for discrepancies, such as underpayment. Image: Pexels

Employers are obligated to provide a payslip showing your hours worked, the wage rate and deductions. It should also show the number of overtime hours (employees under 18 cannot work overtime).



As an employee, you are entitled to at least the minimum wage for every hour worked. If you find any discrepancies in your payslip – such as deduction errors or an underpaid wage – you can report the matter to the Department of Employment and Labour or Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration.

3. KNOW YOUR WORKING HOURS

Per Labour Guide, “The maximum normal working time allowed … is 45 hours weekly. This is nine hours per day (excluding lunch break) if the employee works a five-day week, and eight hours per day (excluding lunch break) if the employee works more than five days per week.”

If you work overtime – which is completely voluntary and subject to an agreement between the employer and employee, preferably in writing – keep in mind that the maximum is three hours per day and 10 hours per week, and you must be paid 1.5 times the normal wage.



4. STAY ON TOP OF PUBLIC HOLIDAY PAY

Working on a public holiday comes with its own set of remuneration rules. Image: Pexels

There may be instances where you may be required to work on a public holiday, such as Christmas Day or New Year’s Day.

If you don’t work on a public holiday, you’re still entitled to your full day’s normal rate if that holiday happens to fall on your usual working day. On the other hand, you should be remunerated double your normal rate if you do work during that holiday.

Note that employers can’t dismiss you if you refuse to work on a public holiday.



5. ASK QUESTIONS

There’s no such thing as a silly or wrong question. Whether it’s seeking advice or answers from a manager, HR department or colleague, it’s important for you to ask questions if there are any aspects about your job that you’re feeling unsure about.

For example, workplace exploitation in the form of underpayment, discrimination, poor safety conditions and much more may go unaddressed if you don’t speak up.

By asking questions, you can ensure that your rights are protected. Plus, it can give you a major confidence boost, and show your employer that you’re willing to engage and learn.



The festive season is supposed to be the most wonderful time of the year. It’s also a prime opportunity to build your CV, earn some pocket money and gain invaluable soft skills.

And who knows – you could either potentially turn this seasonal job into something permanent, or it could help you determine what career path you want to follow. And that alone can be a gift to yourself.

World.title: HOW to make a flawless SASSA Old-Age Grant application
World.content:
Get your SASSA Old-Age Grant application right first time and you're golden. Image: AI generated, for illustrative purposes only

A SASSA Old-Age Grant application is easier when you arrive with the right documents, understand the means/asset test and provide accurate financial information throughout. Missing paperwork or incomplete declarations can delay approval by months and cause a lot of consternation travelling back and forth to SASSA offices.

Furthermore, with the agency tightening reviews and life-certification checks to protect public funds, getting your application right first time is more important than ever. Even the Auditor-General has highlighted weaknesses in the grant payment system, including payments still going to deceased beneficiaries.

SASSA OLD-AGE GRANT APPLICATION

The perfect SASSA Old-Age Grant application begins and ends with detailed knowledge on the eligibility process. Image: File

As regular readers of The South African know, the agency verifies beneficiary information monthly with other government departments and financial institutions. Therefore, anyone misrepresenting themselves in their SASSA Old-Age Grant application are unlikely to get away with it like they once might have done.



As such, first-time applicants must be at least 60 years of age, live in South Africa and be South African citizens, permanent residents or refugees. They must also meet the means test, not be receiving another social grant for themselves and not be cared for in a state institution. The eligibility limits are:

Single applicants: Less than R9 350 per month, or R112 200 annually.

per month, or annually. Married applicants: Combined income below R18 700 per month, or R224 400 annually.

per month, or annually. Assets: No more than R1 584 000 for a single applicant or R3 168 000 for a married applicant.

WHAT DOCUMENTS MUST YOU TAKE?

Visit your nearest SASSA office with your original documents and copies of the following:

Your South African ID booklet or Smart ID card.

Three months of bank statements (up to date).

of bank statements (up to date). Proof of marital status, including a marriage or divorce certificate, where applicable.

A recent proof of residence.

Documents showing income, dividends and other financial interests.

Details and valuations of property and other assets.

Proof of any private pension.

Your UIF membership book or discharge certificate from your previous employer.

If your spouse died within the past five years , their death certificate, will and first and final liquidation and distribution accounts, where applicable.

, their death certificate, will and first and final liquidation and distribution accounts, where applicable. The application is FREE. Complete it with a SASSA official and keep the dated receipt as proof of submission.

HOW LONG DOES SASSA OLD-AGE GRANT APPLICATION APPROVAL TAKE?

Beneficiaries wait with bated breath on news about potential 2027 increases. Image: File

Allow up to three months for processing. If approved, payments are backdated to the date you applied, meaning you should receive a first tranche of up-to three months’ worth.



The easiest way to avoid delays is to ensure every document is current, legible and consistent with the information on your application.

Existing beneficiaries selected for review may also be required to complete eLife certification and biometric verification through the SASSA Services Portal HERE. This online process can save a trip to an office, although technical problems have previously disrupted access.

If you are too old or ill to attend an office, a family member or friend can apply on your behalf. Take a letter authorising them and a doctor’s note explaining why you cannot travel.



For further assistance contact SASSA:

Call: 0800 601 011

Email: grantenquiries@sassa.gov.za

And always respond promptly to any SASSA review notification.

But what do you think? Have you had a smooth experience with your SASSA Old-Age Grant application? If so, or if not, please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Springbok injury update after big win over Italy
World.content:
The Springboks got the first of their Nations Championship Northern Series matches off to a perfect start as they roared to a rewarding 66-7 victory against Italy on Saturday.

However, before kick off, Salmaan Moerat was forced to withdraw from the starting team, denying him the opportunity to make his first Test appearance of 2026.

Lood de Jager ended up starting the match, while Franco Mostert slotted in on the bench, and Rassie Erasmus admitted it was not a waiting game to see how Moerat recovers.



“Salmaan had a little bit of a back spasm on Thursday, but we thought it would clear up,” said Erasmus.

“He looked good at the captain’s practice, but unfortunately in the warm-up he got more back spasms, so hopefully it’s not too serious. He’s the only casualty we have from the game. I don’t think there are any other serious injuries.”

Mostly good news for the Springboks

Erasmus confirmed that there were no other serious injuries from the match, although young flyhalf Yaqeen Ahmed continues to struggle with a sore shoulder.

The Springboks next face France this weekend, and Erasmus called for further improvement for the team despite the big win over Italy.

“It’s almost impossible to put 80 minutes together at 100%. Obviously, we’re not happy with the second half. We scored 45 points in the first half, and the final score was 66, so we got another 21 points in the second half.

“Italy are a proud team, and despite being 45 points down, they started running the ball from everywhere, while we also made some changes that we wanted to see, and with that one loses a bit of rhythm. But when you win 66–7, I don’t think you can start nitpicking problems in the second half. It wasn’t perfect, but it was proper.



“That said, we have to play much better than this if we want to be competitive against France and Ireland. But it’s nice to know that after being a month away from one other, the boys got together and played like that.”

NEXT TESTS

World.title: ‘We kick the ball in the stand’: Ouaddou frustrated by Pirates’ lack of finishing

Orlando Pirates head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou was left frustrated despite his team’s 1-0 victory over Sekhukhune United on Saturday afternoon.

Ouaddou not happy with Pirates win

Many Buccaneers supporters will be hoping for a showdown against Soweto rivals Kaizer Chiefs, which would set up the second Soweto Derby of the season.



Ouaddou knows his side will need to be clinical if Pirates are to retain the Carling Knockout Cup. He has a few weeks to work on the team’s finishing before their anticipated CAF Champions League clash against Simba.

World.title: King Charles would 'carefully' consider China visit
World.content:
LONDON - A British monarch has only ever made one state visit to China: Queen Elizabeth II four decades ago. King Charles III would consider undertaking the second, according to an aide.

"If the government said, 'Will the king go to China?' I think, you know we think about it very carefully," a senior palace aide told reporters this week.

The late queen, Charles's mother, visited China with her husband Prince Philip in October 1986.

The trip included stops in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou, according to reports at the time.

It came two years after the signing of the Sino-British Joint Declaration setting out the terms for the return of Hong Kong, which improved relations between the two countries.

"This is the 40th anniversary of the last state visit," noted the aide, speaking at the end of the king's nine-day tour of the Caribbean.

Charles's trip was dominated by the thorny subject of slavery reparations. He called the transatlantic slave trade a "monstrous injustice" as the UK government mulls an apology.

"I think what we're seeing is a very clear pattern emerging of the government asking the king to head into quite politically charged situations, quite challenging situations," said the aide.

The king, who is politically neutral, "relishes" the "tough parts" of his role and can be a "great secret weapon" for the government, the aide added.

"Whether that's leading on the environment, whether it's renewing and refreshing and reinvigorating relationships with nations where there have been some complex political issues at play, that is what he lives and breathes for," they said.

Charles, who is nearly 78 and still being treated for an undisclosed cancer, was widely praised for his state visit to the United States and delicate handling of US President Donald Trump earlier this year.

Relations between London and Beijing have been strained for years, fuelled in part by tensions over the political situation in former British colony Hong Kong, criticism of Beijing's human rights record and spying allegations.

But UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is now pursuing the same policy of cautious rapprochement started by his predecessor Keir Starmer, who visited Beijing in January.

"China is a hugely important country. It's a very complex country. It would pose you know a lot of complexity in putting a program together," Charles's aide said.

As then prince of Wales, Charles oversaw Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule as Britain's most senior representative at the 1997 handover alongside China's then president Jiang Zemin.

Asked whether Burnham would be asking the king to visit China, his spokesman told AFP that questions about the monarch's travel was "one for the palace".

World.title: What the end of UN peacekeeping in Western Sahara means
World.content:
TUNIS - For the first time in more than three decades, the UN Security Council has failed to renew the mandate for its peacekeeping mission in North Africa's disputed Western Sahara.

The vast mineral-rich desert territory, home to significant phosphate reserves and fishing resources, was a Spanish colony until 1975.

It is largely controlled by Morocco but has been claimed for decades by the Algeria-backed Polisario Front, and remains on the UN list of non-self-governing territories.

- Why are the peacekeepers leaving?

Morocco considers Western Sahara part of its territory and has proposed autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty, while the Polisario seeks full independence.

The UN mission, MINURSO, was created in 1991 to organise a self-determination referendum that has never taken place.

Its mandate expired on October 31 after Russia and the United States vetoed rival Security Council resolutions.

Washington proposed extending the mission while effectively dropping the referendum option and making Morocco's autonomy plan the basis for future talks.

Eleven of 15 council members supported that approach, but Russia rejected it as one-sided.

Instead, Moscow sought to renew MINURSO unchanged, only for Washington to block the move.

"Washington has been enthusiastic about imposing a solution, but it's explicitly biased in this conflict," said Jacob Mundy, a Western Sahara expert and professor at US-based Colgate University.

The US recognised Western Sahara as Moroccan in 2020 when Rabat normalised ties with Israel under a deal backed by President Donald Trump.

- A win for Morocco?

Morocco backed the US proposal but also saw a smaller victory in Russia's veto, which effectively ended MINURSO's mandate.

Rabat welcomed the mission's end as "an important step toward the definitive closure" of the issue at the UN, adding its initial functions were now "outdated".

"For Morocco, the veto was the second-best option," said Riccardo Fabiani, senior analyst at the International Crisis Group.

Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita met Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov in Moscow two days before the vote, and later admitted Rabat had not tried to stop Russia from using its veto.

Rabat sees MINURSO's exit as "the end of UN scrutiny... and another step towards normalising Moroccan control over the territory", Fabiani explained.

Morocco "was going to win either way", added Hamish Kinnear of UK-based consultancy Verisk Maplecroft.

"If the US-drafted resolution passed, Morocco's plan would have been established as the only framework for a political solution -- effectively ruling out the possibility of a UN-facilitated referendum," he explained.

UN peacekeepers were first deployed with the consent of both Morocco and Polisario, but "what Morocco is saying now is it no longer consents to MINURSO", Mundy said.

- What do other sides say?

The Polisario said it would hold Morocco "fully responsible for any serious repercussions" for regional security following the council's vote.

Algeria, Morocco's regional rival and host to thousands of Sahrawi refugees, said Russia's veto was "inevitable", arguing the US proposal's "excessive partiality" sought to "legitimise a situation of occupation".

For Morocco, UN efforts have long stalled, with Bourita recently saying the kingdom was "free to choose the path and framework it wants".

Rabat's autonomy plan has already gained growing support from countries including France, Britain and Spain.

Last year, the Security Council gave the plan unprecedented backing, calling it the "most feasible" solution.

But for many analysts, the issue is still far from over.

- What's next?

The UN has already begun winding down MINURSO, and said this month the liquidation process should be completed "as soon as possible".

The organisation stressed, however, that the mission's departure does not affect the Sahrawi people's "inalienable right to self-determination".

Morocco promptly said it was "coordinating and supporting" the mission's exit.

"Morocco is now betting to continue to normalise its control over Western Sahara while trying to remove it from the UN list of non-self-governing territories," analyst Fabiani said.

But the end of MINURSO could also remove a long-standing buffer between Morocco and the Polisario.

Without peacekeepers on the ground, Kinnear said Morocco would have "greater latitude to conduct operations against the Polisario".

The kingdom has reiterated its commitment to a ceasefire despite repeated Polisario violations since 2020. But tensions with Algeria have remained high since Algiers severed diplomatic ties in 2021.

Last month, Algeria said it was deploying troops to Niger to protect energy assets, which many saw as an unusual break from its traditional non-intervention policy.

"That was no coincidence," Mundy said. "I think it's a signal."

"Algeria feels surrounded -- with Libyan instability driven by the Emirates on one side and Morocco being closely allied with Israel on the other," he added.

Kinnear said direct clashes between Morocco and Algeria were unlikely, but "Rabat will have to weigh Algiers' increasingly assertive foreign policy in the context of Western Sahara".

World.title: Price hikes a tough sell in Japan despite inflation
World.content:
TOKYO - When Japan's "symbol of affordability" Uniqlo decided to increase the price of its basic socks last month, it sparked a backlash before the clothing titan made an immediate U-turn.

That came after Italian-style family restaurant chain Saizeriya issued an almost grovelling apology as it decided to add 20 yen ($0.13) to the price of its trademark Milanese Doria, lamenting its "lack of effort".

The very public angst -- including in one of the world's most recognisable clothing brands -- highlights the struggles Japanese firms face as they battle rising costs in a country where decades of deflation have nurtured a consumer class averse to higher prices.

The Bank of Japan last month declared its two-percent inflation target had been met, after 13 years of ultra-loose monetary policy.

Measures unveiled in 2013 by then-prime minister Shinzo Abe -- and continued by successive governments -- were supposed to end a spiral of deflation that had plagued Japan for decades since the mid-1990s.

However, it wasn't until 2022 -- when the Ukraine war triggered a global energy shock -- that inflation started flickering back to life in resource-poor Japan.

Then the US-Israel war on Iran saw Tehran choke off the strategic Strait of Hormuz, slashing crude exports from the Middle East and impacting global supply chains, in turn sending company costs soaring.

- 'Sorry for our customers' -

While firms in most countries have been able to lift prices accordingly -- albeit to expected anger -- those in Japan have to battle an inherent view that hikes are taboo.

Businesses big and small have found themselves hard-pressed to plough ahead with drastic price hikes to avoid alienating customers.

Decisive increases can be more of a risk for smaller, countryside businesses whose survival often hinges on loyal patronage by regular clients.

Sachi, 68, a ramen shop owner in western Japan's Okayama region, has been holding off on raising prices despite snowballing costs.

World.title: Antonelli 'ready for anything' in Sao Paulo Grand Prix
World.content:
SAO PAULO - New world champion Kimi Antonelli said he will be "ready for anything" in Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix when he starts alongside 2025 champion Lando Norris on the front row.

Elevated one place thanks to Mercedes teammate George Russell's five-place penalty for taking new power unit parts, the 20-year-old Italian was satisfied, but self-critical after finishing third in Saturday's rain-hit qualifying.

"I was a bit too cautious I think," he said.

"I was trying to understand this track in the wet for the first time and it has always been dry here so far in the past. But I felt good in the dry and not so good in the wet!

"I made two big mistakes and it wasn't ideal, but all in all I think that tomorrow, we have a good chance."

He added that he felt cautious about the weather ahead after the long stormy session on Saturday.

"It was very tricky. To be fair, I didn't really know what to expect. Obviously, I have never driven here in the wet, so I didn't know what was coming and I struggled a little bit on the inters.

"I made a big mistake, almost went off in Turn Five, but it still was enough for P3, so I’m happy with that.

"Let's see what the weather is – but overall, you know, I am going to be ready for anything as the weather has been very unpredictable. We will try to be ready for anything."

Russell, who qualified second, was unhappy not to take pole after being told by his Mercedes race engineer to ease off on his final flying lap.

"I felt more like myself and I could fight for pole on every lap," said the British driver.

"It's the first time I've felt that confident in the car for a while and it's in the wet so I don't understand that.

"Congrats to Lando – but that lap was definitely a pole lap! It was a misjudgment on our side and we need to understand what happened. Yes, the rain was coming down but we should have finished the lap."

World.title: Elections 2026 | IEC to announce final results at 6pm
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The IEC will officially announce the final results of the 2026 Local Government Elections later today.

The announcement is scheduled for 6pm at the National Results Operations Centre in Midrand.

President Cyril Ramaphosa will give the traditional keynote address,

with all party representatives in attendance.

The announcement will mark the official conclusion of the election results process.

But South Africans will have to wait at least two weeks before knowing final outcome of the hung councils.

World.title: Malema accuses ANC of empowering DA
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - EFF leader Julius Malema has blamed the ANC for the DA’s strong performance in the 2026 local government elections.

The DA is on course to retain its outright majority in Cape Town, while making significant gains in Gauteng.

The party is also leading in the Tshwane, Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni metros, as vote counting continues.

Malema says the ANC’s decision to enter into a coalition with the DA at national level has helped legitimise the party in the eyes of voters.

Meanwhile, the EFF leader says his party will take stock of its performance and work towards rebuilding its support.

The EFF has lost ground in these elections, dropping to fourth place nationally.

Malema says the party will assess its performance across municipalities and provinces, identifying areas of improvement and where it needs to rebuild ahead of the 2029 provincial and national elections.

World.title: Erasmus demands more after Springboks crush Italy
World.content:
TURIN - Rassie Erasmus insisted that South Africa must improve if they are to beat France and Ireland in the Nations Championship, despite running in nine tries in a demolition job of Italy on Saturday.

The world champions blew away the Azzurri with a 66-7 victory in Turin to notch a fourth consecutive bonus-point victory that kept them top of the Southern Hemisphere standings ahead of sterner tests in Paris and Dublin.

The star-studded Springboks proved far too strong for an understrength Italian side missing 16 players, blowing away the hosts in the first half with six unanswered tries.

However, head coach Erasmus insisted it was an imperfect display from his side despite the emphatic scoreline and rampant attacking rugby.

"It's almost impossible to put 80 minutes together at 100 per cent," Erasmus told a press conference.

"Obviously, we are not happy with the second half. We scored 45 points in the first half, and the final score was 66, so we got another 21 points in the second half.

"Italy are a proud team, and despite being 45 points down, they started running the ball from everywhere, while we also made some changes that we wanted to see, and with that one loses a bit of rhythm.

"But when you win 66–7, I don't think you can start nitpicking problems in the second half. It wasn't perfect, but it was proper.

"That said, we have to play much better than this if we want to be competitive against France and Ireland. But it's nice to know that after being a month away from one other, the boys got together and played like that."

The victory ensured that South Africa bounced back from a surprise September defeat in Australia, only their second loss of 2026.

The other came against New Zealand during the 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' series in the summer, but the Boks won the series 3-1 to cement their status as favourites to retain their crown at next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia.

- Moerat return delayed by spasms -

With a blockbuster clash against Six Nations champions France coming up at the Stade de France on Friday, the only bad news for Erasmus was an injury to lock Salmaan Moerat that forced his withdrawal during the warm-up.

"Salmaan had a little bit of a back spasm on Thursday, but we thought it would clear up," said Erasmus.

"He looked good at the captain's practice, but unfortunately in the warm-up he got more back spasms, so hopefully it's not too serious.

"He's the only casualty we have from the game. I don't think there are any other serious injuries."

Italy enjoyed a memorable Six Nations campaign at the start of the year, beating Scotland before claiming their first-ever win against England in Rome.

However, Gonzalo Quesada's side have now lost four in a row in the Nations Championship after summer defeats on the road to Japan, New Zealand and Australia, and the Azzurri head coach said an honest review was required.

"There are several negatives," Quesada said.

"The big challenge for us now is to be capable of understanding that we faced the best team in the world, who played a great match, and accept it.

"At the same time, we can't afford to just say, 'Okay, they were too good,' and that's it. We could have done better; we were put under too much pressure, particularly in our kicking game, but in all areas of the game."
