Sin embargo, el banco estadounidense espera una mejora en los dos países y para 2026, proyecta un crecimiento de los ingresos del grupo del 10%, por encima del objetivo de Santander. “Prevemos que el margen de intereses aumente un 11%, impulsado por un efecto favorable del tipo de cambio y un fuerte crecimiento orgánico en España, Norteamérica, Sudamérica y el Reino Unido (incluyendo la contribución de TSB a partir de mayo de 2026), así como en EE UU tras el cierre de la operación con Webster”, dice. Para 2027 sitúa el alza de los ingresos en un 9% “con avances en todas las líneas, incluyendo el margen de intereses, las comisiones y otros ingresos no recurrentes”. Goldman Sachas ha elevado el objetivo a 12 meses de 14,1 a 15 euros, lo que supone un potencial del 40%, y ha reiterado la recomendación de compra.

Barclays, que tiene el consejo de sobreponderar, también ha mejorado las previsiones del beneficio por acción para 2026-2028 en un 1 %. Las razones que esgrimen sus analistas son unas proyecciones más sólidas del margen de intereses en España, México, Chile y Brasil; un mayor crecimiento de la cartera crediticia; una mejora en la dinámica de financiación, y una mayor contribución de la gestión de activos y pasivos (ALCO) de lo que habían estimado inicialmente. “Más allá de las cifras, consideramos que la conferencia de resultados fue constructiva”, afirma Barclays. “La dirección se mostró cada vez más confiada respecto a las perspectivas del margen de intereses y reiteró que el coste del riesgo (CoR) en Brasil permanece bajo control, a pesar de un entorno de tipos de interés elevados durante más tiempo —un factor que, a nuestro juicio, estaba lastrando el sentimiento del mercado— y afirmó explícitamente que lo peor ya ha pasado”

Con ello, la confianza de Barclays en “la ejecución del plan a 2028 se ha visto reforzada”. La firma ha subido el precio objetivo a 14 euros y espera una rentabilidad total para el accionista (vía recompra de acciones y dividendos) sobre el 9% en 2028.

Mientras, Javier Cabrera, de XTB, valora los últimos resultados como mixtos. “Esto se castiga en un contexto donde los inversores dudan sobre la capacidad del sector bancario para trasladar la subida de tipos a los clientes sin deteriorar la demanda de crédito. Al igual que pasó con Bankinter, Santander ha mostrado crecimiento, pero insuficiente para despejar las dudas”, comenta.

Por otro lado, la sacudida que está sufriendo la inteligencia artificial en los mercados del mundo, también ha tenido eco en Santander. Así lo considera Antonio Aspas, socio cofundador y consejero de Buy & Hold: “La caída bursátil en Banco Santander ha sido algo más pronunciada en el sector a consecuencia de su mayor exposición a EE UU y a los préstamos para el desarrollo de centros de datos. En este sentido, las dudas sobre los retornos que finalmente conseguirán las abultadísimas inversiones en IA y los centros de datos que necesitan son las que han marcado el rumbo del mercado en las últimas semanas, señalando con caídas a los valores y sectores más expuestos y premiando a otros de corte más tradicional e industrial”.

Para Aspas, “el punto fuerte” de Santander frente a otras entidades es “fundamentalmente su mayor diversificación geográfica”.

La posición actual del consenso de mercado es de un 76% de consejos de compra y el 24% de mantener; no tiene ninguna de venta, según recoge Bloomberg. Y la valoración media arroja un potencial del 27,5%. Santander ha repartido esta semana un dividendo bruto de 0,1270 euros.

World.title: ‘La Regenta’ de Netflix no es bienvenida en la catedral
World.content:
Artículos estrictamente de opinión que responden al estilo propio del autor. Estos textos de opinión han de basarse en datos verificados y ser respetuosos con las personas aunque se critiquen sus actos. Todas las columnas de opinión de personas ajenas a la Redacción de EL PAÍS llevarán, tras la última línea, un pie de autor —por conocido que éste sea— donde se indique el cargo, título, militancia política (en su caso) u ocupación principal, o la que esté o estuvo relacionada con el tema abordado

En la plaza de Alfonso II de Oviedo los turistas pueden hacerse una foto con la estatua de Anita Ozores y la portada de la catedral de fondo. Parece que la Regenta acaba de salir de confesarse con Don Fermín y está un poco sofocada, pese a que en Vetusta nunca hace mucho calor (hasta este verano, al menos). ¿Molestará al cabildo ovetense este homenaje a tan impía novela, perpetrado a las puertas mismas del templo y pensado para que este aparezca bien enmarcado en las fotos de Instagram? Si no soportan que Netflix ruede la nueva adaptación de la novela de Clarín en su interior, me imagino que no tendrán mejor opinión de ese culto idólatra.

Muchos se han felicitado de que una obra literaria escrita en 1884 siga escandalizando a la curia: el primer enemigo de La Regenta fue el obispo ovetense Ramón Rodríguez Vigil, para quien era “un libro saturado de erotismo, de escarnio a las prácticas cristianas y de alusiones injuriosas a respetabilísimas personas”. Al autor lo llamaba “salteador de honras ajenas”. Como escritor, envidio una crítica así. Ojalá algún obispo me prodigase uno solo de esos cumplidos. No hay mejor publicidad para un libro provocador que la furia de quienes se sienten provocados por él, pero ese reclamo siempre lleva veneno y presagios de venganzas. No creo que en Netflix celebren haber dado con la Iglesia.

Según cuenta Ricardo Labra en el interesantísimo ensayo El caso Alas Clarín: la memoria y el canon literario, “puede que ninguna otra creación literaria haya perturbado tanto a una ciudad [que La Regenta], y que ninguna otra ciudad haya luchado tanto por escaparse de las páginas de una novela”. En el portazo del deán de la catedral de Oviedo resuenan otros golpes mucho más siniestros. Resuena el silencio que casi sepulta a la novela durante 80 años: hasta la década de 1960 no empezó a apreciarse como una obra maestra indiscutible. Resuena la destrucción vandálica del busto de su autor, reducido a cascotes en el Campo de San Francisco una madrugada de 1937. Resuenan también los disparos del pelotón de fusilamiento que mató a Leopoldo Alas hijo, rector de la Universidad de Oviedo, al empezar la guerra y ajusticiado oficialmente por republicano, aunque su hija y muchos lectores e historiadores estaban convencidos de que lo mataron por ser hijo del detestado Clarín. Entre tanto ruido funebrero, el portazo de la catedral reverbera con un anacronismo fuera de compás, pero sorprendentemente sincronizado con esos tambores furiosos que se acercan cada día.

World.title: Buenos ‘momentos’ en Málaga haciendo lo que no hacen los cruceristas
World.content:
Otoño es la estación de los cruceros en Málaga. Entre octubre y noviembre llegarán 113 con 165.000 pasajeros. Esos son muchos forasteros para una ciudad de 603.000 habitantes, y no digamos para los cinco lugares que casi todos visitan: la alcazaba, el museo Picasso, la catedral, el castillo de Gibralfaro y el Centre Pompidou. Las calles Larios, Granada y Alcazabilla registran estos días tal densidad de turistas que la Gran Vía madrileña, en comparación, parece una fotografía desolada de Patrick Sansone. El viajero inconformista está de suerte, porque otoño es también la estación del Moments (hasta el 15 de noviembre), festival internacional de artes y culturas contemporáneas que este año celebra su 13ª edición y que es un salvavidas en un océano embravecido de guiris, tópicos y restaurantes de cadenas.

El creador y director del festival, Juanjo M. Fuentes, nos da las claves para sobrevivir en su ciudad a la invasión crucerista. Suyas son las pistas que ofrecemos a continuación para descubrir una Málaga distinta, alternativa, sin multitudes ni franquicias, una ciudad salpicada de fotografías contemporáneas, músicas experimentales y charlas y encuentros fistrosóficos en homenaje al malagueño más rompedor de todos los tiempos, con permiso de Pablo Picasso: Chiquito de la Calzada.

Juanjo M. Fuentes, director del festival Moments, junto al mural de Chad Eaton. Andrés Campos

Lugares para crear o para ver cómo crean otros

Pocos cruceristas se ven en Altallama, que es uno de los 37 espacios donde se desarrolla el festival. Este centro ideado y dirigido por mujeres es muchas cosas: sala de exposiciones, lugar de encuentros culturales, atelier, coworking, estudio de tatuaje, cafetería y tienda de bellas artes. En estos momentos puede verse la exposición de Gema Hamartia Hipótesis alternativa de la geometría del agua y, casi en cualquier momento, a la propia artista, que trabaja aquí. En el mismo barrio —antaño de chabolas y hoy de universidades—, en un muro de la plaza de El Ejido, hay un pavo real de 23 metros que el californiano Chad Eaton Timber pintó como si fuera una de sus serigrafías, con gruesos trazos blancos y negros, durante el Moments de 2018. Otro mural impactante de aquel año es el que convirtió la cancha de baloncesto del IES Carlinda en un cuadro de Mondrian, obra de Iker Muro Murone.

Más información El Caminito del Rey desafía de nuevo al vértigo: abre el puente colgante más largo de España

En Altallama hay un art menú que permite adquirir pequeños lotes de materiales para distintas técnicas —carboncillo, acuarela, gouache, ceras…— y ponerse a crear allí mismo. También puede uno hacerlo por las calles de la ciudad. Para esto último, lo mejor es contactar con Urban Sketchers Málaga, un grupo de aficionados que organiza regularmente quedadas para dibujar del natural, poniendo muchas veces el foco —qué remedio— en la enorme masa de turistas que fagocita los principales monumentos.

Si nos gusta el arte, pero no lo tenemos, podemos ver cómo crean otros a los que les sobra. En el Polígono Industrial Ronda Exterior (Bodegueros, 25), 11 jóvenes artistas malagueños han transformado un antiguo almacén de baños portátiles en un taller atiborrado de pinceles, bustos, caballetes, experimentos textiles, panes coloreados, amigos, curiosos, periodistas, turistas extraviados, lienzos en blanco y otros tan abigarrados como los cuadros dalinianos que pinta Vito Ramírez Vitillo. En la única puerta de este estudio compartido cuelga un cartel con lo que san Pablo escribió a los tesalonicenses y Lenin repitió a los burgueses ociosos: “El que no quiera trabajar, que no coma”.

El espacio creativo Altallama, uno de los espacios donde se desarrolla el festival Moments. Andrés Campos

Una tarde con Chiquito y otra con un rockero fotógrafo

Un momentazo del Moments, valga la redundancia, será el III Ciclo Fistrosofía 2026… al ataquer!!!, unas charlas sobre Chiquito de la Calzada que se celebrarán el 12 de noviembre en la Peña Flamenca Juan Breva. Entre otros, participará Juan Zavala, codirector y guionista del documental El otro Chiquito. El Día de los Pecadores, como lo ha bautizado la organización, se redondeará yendo luego al bar Drunk-O-Rama, lugar de referencia underground con dos décadas a sus espaldas. Habrá una exposición colectiva titulada Esta obra viene de Bonanza: 20 años de Drunk-O-Rama, una subasta benéfica de las obras y un concurso festivo de camisas chiquitianas. Huelga decir cómo hay que ir vestidos.

Otro día habrá que ponerse serios e ir a ver la exposición fotográfica Noticings, de Patrick Sansone, que estará en el espacio MEET hasta el 31 de enero de 2027. No veremos multitudes en el antiguo edificio de Tabacalera de Málaga y, desde luego, no en las imágenes que este artista de Misisipi captó con sus cámaras analógicas en pequeñas localidades y carreteras del sur de Estados Unidos entre 2019 y 2024. Todas tienen el aire apocalíptico del confinamiento y el opresivo de un sueño que se vuelve pesadilla, el americano: carteles y relojes rotos, maniquíes abandonados, solares vacíos… “Aquella persona”, contaba Sansone a los asistentes el día de la inauguración, casi disculpándose por haber incluido a un ser humano en una de sus fotografías, “estuvo una eternidad esperando el autobús. No me quedó más remedio que disparar”.

Cuando vino a Málaga a presentar las fotografías de Noticings, Sansone se alojó en Villa Alicia. Es un hotelito ideal para cualquiera que desee aislarse del barullo, en una colonia centenaria del barrio de La Victoria, a pie del monte homónimo, donde todas las casas tienen nombre de mujer: Villa Carmen, Villa Obdulia, Villa Belén, otra vez Villa Carmen, Villa Isabel, Villa María, Villa Alicia… La familia propietaria y los huéspedes de las otras 13 habitaciones nunca olvidarán a Patrick Sansone tocando maravillosamente la guitarra bajo la planta alucinógena que hay pintada en el vestíbulo. Porque antes que fotógrafo, Sansone es un gran músico, de la banda estadounidense de rock alternativo Wilco.

Patrick Sansone, en el vestíbulo del hotel Villa Alicia, en Málaga. Andrés Campos

Productos ecológicos de proximidad y vinos naturales

Después de ver la exposición Noticings es buena idea ir a comer o a cenar a La Taberna de Curro Castilla, un restaurante vasco-malagueño que está a cinco minutos de paseo del espacio MEET. Cuatro aciertos del chef José Salguero: el gazpachuelo malagueño, la ensaladilla rusa, el bacalao al pil-pil y el pulpo en dos tiempos con salsa brava. Tampoco es mal plan llegarse al centro histórico para probar lo que hacen en La Casa del Perro, uno de los primeros restaurantes de Málaga que apostó por los productos ecológicos de proximidad y los vinos naturales. Aunque cada día cambian los 20 platos de la pizarra, rara vez borran los puerros a la vinagreta con mojama selecta. José Sacristán es cliente habitual, y entre las fotos de ilustres comensales sorprende una reciente de Frodo, o sea el actor Elijah Wood.

En el barrio de la Trinidad, cerca del centro pero sin la presión turística que hay en este, se encuentra Rogada Wine Bar, espacio de vinos naturales, picoteo sencillo y playlist en la que manda Thundercat. Este bar participa en el festival Moments celebrando Entre Pan y Vino (el 6 de noviembre), un festín con cosas ricas de la vecina Cádiz: bocadillos de chicharrón y de atún de Barbate maridados con vinos naturales de uva palomino.

De compras auténticas por el centro

La Casa del Perro, restaurante y tienda de vinos naturales en Málaga. Andrés Campos

Viendo la proliferación exagerada de franquicias en el centro, asombra y hasta emociona tropezarse con negocios de toda la vida, como Luis Carrasquilla, que lleva 47 años disfrazando a los malagueños, o como Antigüedades Los Remedios, que tiene alguno más. La librería Proteo-Prometeo no parece a primera vista muy antigua, pero su historia se remonta a 1969 y, si uno se fija en lo que hay a mano izquierda, nada más entrar, verá una pared sin anaqueles, libros ni enlucidos que enmascaren el tosco tapial y los ladrillos con que estaba hecha la muralla islámica de Málaga, que eso es lo que se descubrió al

el establecimiento en 2003. Los que buscan comercios y productos auténticos solo tienen que andar 150 metros para dar con Alegría, una tienda que acaba de abrir y que está llena hasta los topes, no de abanicos e imanes de nevera, sino de las mejores cerámicas artesanas de Andalucía, como las que hacen los Tito en Úbeda (Jaén) o el taller Rama en Villaverde del Río (Sevilla). Algo más hay que andar —tampoco mucho: un kilómetro— para comprar excelentes vinos naturales. Poca gente sabe más de ellos en España que Emilio Pacheco, sumiller y propietario de La Alacena. También se pueden tomar aquí mismo por copas.

En la tienda Alegría se venden cerámicas artesanas de Andalucía. Andrés Campos

Noches de arte, birras y croquetas

A las 18.15, nada más abrir, El Muro Bar Independiente (Muro de San Julián, 1) ya está a tope de gente que tardea en la terraza con el último sol y se toma unos chupitos en la barra. Si uno no sabe cuál pedir, el camarero se levanta la camiseta y le muestra la botella de Fisk que lleva tatuada en la tripa. Mucho más serias son las protestas —últimamente, contra los desahucios— que aparecen cada día escritas en la pizarra del negocio y en su cuenta de Instagram. Este bar alegre y protestón es uno de los espacios donde suele haber conciertos, sesiones de DJ y actividades del festival Moments, al igual que Drunk-O-Rama (Ramón Franquelo, 5). Ya hemos visto la que se va a organizar aquí el Día de los Pecadores, el 12 de noviembre. También hay noches de arte, birras y croquetas. En ellas, se puede comprar directamente a artistas locales y tomarse una pinta por tres euros (4,80 si se pican dos croquetas). Pero aunque no haya nada especial, ya lo es sentarse en cualquiera de sus mesas con una cerveza IPA artesana Drunk-O-Rama y contemplar los murales pintados en las paredes por Jeremy Fish y Carmela Maracas. También colabora con el festival Moments la Sala Core (Convalecientes, 11), que es digna heredera del antiguo Velvet Club —está en el mismo local y suena parecido—, el cual fue referente y refugio de la música alternativa y el rock en directo en el centro histórico de Málaga.

Caracolear por el monte y surfear en el ‘skate park’

Si más que de trasnochar somos de madrugar (pero mucho), nuestro sitio en Málaga es la cafetería El Caracol (Cristo de la Epidemia, 37), que abre a las 5.30 entre semana y a las 7.00 sábados y domingos. Aquí se puede desayunar unos tejeringos o unos churros madrileños y, como la ciudad está aún despertando, subir paseando o trotando al cercano monte Victoria.

Senderistas en el monte Victoria, desde donde puede verse el centro de Málaga. Andrés Campos

Por el camino veremos el llamado Bosque Mágico o Valle de los Árboles Tallados, tocones de viejos eucaliptos derribados por el tiempo —el atmosférico y el cronológico— que un artista local, Manuel Ledesma, ha labrado pacientemente hasta hacer con ellos unas figuras que recuerdan a La torre de Babel de Pieter Brueghel el Viejo y a los monasterios de Meteora. Una vez arriba del monte Victoria, a 193 metros sobre el mar y a alguno menos sobre la ciudad, disfrutaremos de una vista de Málaga mejor que la que hay desde el castillo de Gibralfaro, menos turística, más sosegada. Es un sendero circular de 3,46 kilómetros que puede seguirse sin dificultad con el mapa y el track que se proporcionan en Wikiloc.

¿Y si no somos de madrugar, pero nos gusta la actividad? Entonces, una buena alternativa es ir al Skate Park Málaga, que abre a la 11.00 los fines de semana y a las 16.00 el resto de días. Esta instalación deportiva para las modalidades de BMX, Skate, Roller y Scooter está equipada con un bowl grande y profundo como una piscina olímpica, que es famoso dentro y fuera de España y que ha sido diseñado por el rider dos veces campeón del mundo Rubén Alcántara. Los skaters habituales nos recomiendan, para equiparnos, la tienda Disaster Street Wear, en la calle Córdoba, a tres minutos de la Alameda Principal.

El 'skate park' de Málaga. Andrés Campos

Para comer, la hamburguesa de atún rojo con mayonesa de albahaca, rúcula y tomate seco en aceite de trufa que preparan en Goofy Burguer, el bar del parque. Y para escuchar, Little Postcards From Home, el disco que presentó Ray Barbee, la legendaria figura estadounidense del skate, durante la pasada edición del Moments. Las olas de hormigón del enorme bowl, sobre las que, más que patinar, se surfea, son un mar libre de cruceros, sin turistas en la costa. Buen lugar para el viajero inconformista. Incluso el que no sabe, se lo pasa bien mirando.

World.title: EL PAÍS alcanza los 500.000 suscriptores
World.content:
La apuesta de EL PAÍS por la información frente al caos recibe el apoyo de una comunidad global en auge. En el año de su 50º aniversario, este periódico alcanza ya los 500.000 suscriptores. El hito llega en un momento de liderazgo en España y de expansión en América, con especial foco en Estados Unidos. EL PAÍS lanzó su modelo de suscripción en plena pandemia y su comunidad más fiel no ha dejado de aumentar desde entonces hasta lograr ahora el medio millón de abonados. Un punto de partida para seguir creciendo en todos los ámbitos de habla hispana desde un diario que nació hace medio siglo como “independiente de la mañana” y hoy es “el periódico global”, con más de 500 periodistas cuyas informaciones se leen en 136 países.

En un momento en el que la batalla por captar la atención de la opinión pública se recrudece desde múltiples estímulos, los lectores de EL PAÍS refuerzan su apoyo a una oferta informativa que les acerca la actualidad mediante el contraste de los hechos, la suma de voces y la profundidad sobre la compleja realidad. Esta confianza consolida la apuesta del periódico por las investigaciones, la ampliación de las coberturas internacionales, los nuevos formatos narrativos y el refuerzo de la independencia editorial. Así ocurre con despliegues como los recientes sobre el accidente mortal de trenes en Urda o las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato en Estados Unidos. Los suscriptores garantizan con su compromiso este proyecto editorial que persigue ofrecer la mejor información y la defensa de los valores democráticos que hace 50 años impulsaron su nacimiento en plena Transición Española.

El director del periódico, Jan Martínez Ahrens, reflexiona sobre la llegada a los 500.000 abonados: “Desde lugares, experiencias y continentes muy distintos, todos los días los suscriptores eligen leernos, ver nuestras fotografías y vídeos, escuchar nuestros podcasts… A pesar de la desinformación, de la simplificación interesada y de los algoritmos, todos los días nos eligen y nos leen con exigencia y con confianza. Nos obligan a estar a su altura, a ser siempre mejores y a seguir avanzando juntos”.

Además de su edición nacional, EL PAÍS cuenta hoy con ediciones internacionales como EL PAÍS US —cuyo equipo se ha ampliado recientemente con reporteros de diversas nacionalidades hispanas y una larga trayectoria en Estados Unidos para conectar allí con una audiencia hispanohablante cada vez más relevante—, EL PAÍS América y EL PAÍS in English, además de otras específicas en México, Colombia, Argentina y Chile. Las newsletters del diario han superado el millón de usuarios registrados, y la cabecera cuenta tanto con el exitoso podcast Hoy en EL PAÍS como con una división audiovisual que sobrepasa los tres millones de suscriptores en Youtube. Además, la comunidad de seguidores de EL PAÍS en todas sus redes sociales alcanza un total de 27 millones en todo el mundo.

“Acceso a información veraz, accesible y de calidad”

Para Ana Ventosa, que nació en Albacete hace 33 años y vive en Barcelona, ser suscriptora de EL PAÍS tiene el valor de “tener acceso a información veraz, accesible y de calidad”. Profesora e investigadora en la Universidad de Barcelona, Ventosa también mira hacia el futuro de este periódico y le pide lo siguiente: “Que siga adaptándose a los cambios que se dan a la sociedad, que siga representando la diversidad y que sea accesible para personas que no tienen capacidad de acceder a la información. Y que trabaje la relación con los jóvenes y adolescentes que ahora mismo están faltos de referentes, que pueda llevar luz a profesiones minoritarias y femeninas, que saque información sobre mujeres poderosas e independientes, que acompañen a las chicas y a las niñas de hoy en día a creerse que pueden llegar allá donde quieren”.

Entre sus apuestas para las generaciones más jóvenes, EL PAÍS ha lanzado una iniciativa para que los nacidos entre 2001 y 2008 puedan suscribirse a la edición digital del periódico gratis durante tres meses.⁠ También se ha puesto en marcha Amigos de EL PAÍS, una nueva modalidad de suscripción destinada a quienes desean mantener una relación más cercana con el periódico y acceder a experiencias exclusivas. Junto a la actualidad diaria, el periódico continúa apostando por nuevas narrativas en vídeo, audio, infografía y visualización de datos. Entre las apuestas más recientes figuran producciones como La ola ultra o Milagros con cita previa. También, espacios de entretenimiento como Juegos, con la última incorporación de Conexiones, en el que hay que descubrir la relación oculta que une a cuatro palabras.

Cincuenta años después del nacimiento de EL PAÍS, este periódico crece cada día gracias al respaldo de sus lectores, que no solo quieren acceder a la información, sino que además deciden sostenerla. Según los análisis más recientes del Instituto Reuters, entidad de la Universidad de Oxford para el estudio del Periodismo en cuyo informe anual sobre el consumo de noticias digitales cuenta en España con la colaboración de la Universidad de Navarra, un 54% de los españoles se declara “muy o totalmente” interesado por la actualidad. En paralelo, tres de cada cuatro ciudadanos dudan de la veracidad de las noticias en internet y un 74% de encuestados muestra preocupación por distinguir lo verdadero de lo falso.

Esta tendencia muestra el creciente interés por la información de calidad frente al caos y donde el periodismo tiene la oportunidad de reivindicar el servicio que presta a la sociedad. Juan Carlos Puente, de 64 años y suscriptor de Bilbao, espera de EL PAÍS en el futuro “que siga con ese rigor, que de alguna manera en este entorno de desinformación y bulos mantenga la veracidad y el contraste de sus publicaciones”. Puente trabaja como responsable de ventas para la administración pública en una multinacional y concluye que este periódico le ayuda “a entender lo que pasa en el mundo”.

World.title: Tea leaves and turmoil: a Dutch classic
World.content:
If the characters in The Tea Lords feel real, it is because they are. The grande dame of Dutch literature, Hella S. Haasse, based her internationally acclaimed magnum opus about plantation life in the Dutch East Indies on a trove of letters and documents pulled from extensive archival research.

The book follows Rudolf Kerkhoven, who finishes his studies at what is now TU Delft and moves to a remote tea plantation on Java, a place he nicknames “Eldorado”. The young man is hoping to follow in his father’s footsteps but struggles to adjust to life in Indonesia. While the venture eventually prospers, Kerkhoven’s intimate thoughts show that he does not enjoy the success.

“Never in his life had Rudolf felt such profound relief as when the Telank dropped anchor in the roadstead of Batavia,” Haasse writes.

The reader sees Kerkhoven’s struggle with the land, which can be inhospitable as well as with his wife, who has issues with fertility and with himself. The young man, 24-years old when the novel starts, is deeply anxious and concerned about his position in society and whether he is adhering to the complicated social rules of his class.

The book also follows the complicated political and social structures at the time, as well as an indepth look at the business of tea, something many of us consume frequently but think about rarely.

Like the correspondence referenced in the book, the plot moves slowly, if at all – an interesting juxtaposition to today’s instant communication.

The Tea Lords is not a compilation of letters, but rather a work loosely based on one family’s experience as plantation holders. Haasse found the Kerkhoven family documents in the Indies Tea and Family Archive, but she also drew from her own childhood. She was born in Batavia, modern-day Jakarta.

Haasse is a staple read for Dutch schoolchildren. Born in 1918, her novella Oeroeg is also set in the Dutch East Indies and was written as the gift for Dutch-language Book Week in 1948. Oeroeg is translated into English as The Black Lake and is still taught in classrooms around the country.

Nearly 50 years later, The Tea Lords was published as Heren van de thee in 1992. It was also published during Dutch Book Week and Haasse is the only author to have taken home the Book Week Prize three times.

She was also awarded the Constantijn Huygens Prize and the P. C. Hooft Award, as well as the NS Public Prize twice. She died in 2011 at the age of 93.

Nearly a decade after The Tea Lords was first published, it was translated into English by Ina Rilke. The Guardian called the work “a graceful, marvellously achieved improvisation that only a novelist of the greatest imagination and sympathy could have written.”

It’s a patient read but a fascinating look at life during an often romanticised time. You can get your copy of The Tea Lords at the American Book Center.

World.title: Cabinet sets out AI plan, seeks partners beyond US and China
World.content:
The cabinet is establishing a vision of how to integrate AI into Dutch society so as to take advantage of its benefits, control reliance on foreign powers and strengthen national security.

Digital economy minister Willemijn Aerdts released 28-page vision letter to parliament on Friday, acknowledging that AI will “largely determine our future”.

“We want a Netherlands where AI makes everyone better and helps us move forward. Where a nurse has more time for patients, entrepreneurs can grow, and technology helps us with the major challenges of our time,” she said.

“That requires choices. Where do we want to lead the way and where do we draw the line? We don’t have to be able to do everything ourselves, but we do want to decide for ourselves which direction we take.”

The vision names Canada, Japan, Singapore and South Korea as “middle powers” the Netherlands wants to work with, alongside other EU member states.

It also says the Netherlands will keep working on “stable and predictable relations” with the US and China. The letter notes that the Netherlands has joined Pax Silica, a US-led partnership on chips, computing power and AI infrastructure.

The only funding figure in the vision is €120 million for Dutch participation in an EU-wide AI project, which was already set aside in September. The letter says more “targeted and structural investment” is needed in infrastructure, talent and research, but gives no amounts.

“This is a toothless tiger,” Volt leader Laurens Dassen told broadcaster NOS. “AI should be a top priority. It isn’t if there is no budget.”

Plans for computing power and datacentres, which use large amounts of electricity and water, will follow in the first quarter of 2027.

The cabinet is also exploring whether to set up a Dutch AI safety institute modelled on the UK’s AI Security Institute. An advisory report is due in December.

Aerdts and the education minister plan to agree a “media pact” with public and private media organisations, which will also cover how AI systems use journalistic content. No details on that have been given yet.

World.title: Activists occupy site of Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam
World.content:
Police are clearing a building site in Westpoort after pro-Palestinian activists occupied it this morning in protest to the city’s plans to build a massive data centre there, which will be leased to Microsoft.

Microsoft has acknowledged selling cloud and computing software to the Israeli military. The action was originally organised by the climate and justice group Geef Tegengas and joined by Extinction Rebellion and other groups. Other groups turned up and some stormed the site, and hung up Palestinian flags.

There was a confrontation between the police and activists this morning, according to broadcaster NOS, although the demonstration was allowed to continue after police surrounded them.

Some activists climbed onto cranes and the roof of the construction.

The €1 billion, 78MW campus is being built by Pure DC and is let in full to Microsoft. Critics say it gets round the 2022 national ban on hyperscale data centres because on paper it is three smaller data centres. According to NRC, it will use as much electricity in a year as the whole of Amsterdam.

Microsoft told NOS that it is aware of the demonstration. “We understand that this project stirs up strong emotions and respect people’s right to express their opinions peacefully. However, we do not condone actions that violate the law or endanger people’s safety.”

World.title: Cancelled Jewish exhibition back on table after mayor steps in
World.content:
Amersfoort Mayor Lucas Bolsius has said he wants a cancelled Jewish exhibition at the Amsersfoort Museum to go ahead, and the museum has now agreed to look at how it can be staged. The museum announced earlier this week that it was cancelling the exhibition due to the situation in the Middle East and rising global tensions.

The exhibition, “300 Years Amersfoort Shul”, has been years in the making, and its last-minute cancellation has caused outrage in the Jewish community.

“Apparently, many struggle to distinguish between Jewish identity and Israel. The reflex to cancel performances in situations like this is becoming increasingly common across the cultural sector,” Alexander van Dijkhuizen, chairman of the Jewish Community of Amersfoort, is reported as saying in US Jewish newspaper The Algemeiner.

“It is essential not only to reflect on the past, but also to acknowledge the difficult circumstances facing the Jewish community today.”

Hard to manage

When museum director Paul Baltus cancelled the exhibition, he said possible reactions to it were hard to manage.

“As a small and vulnerable organisation, I do not want to expose my staff to that kind of pressure,” he told the AD. “While security guards can be hired and cameras installed, the reality is that our volunteers would still have to deal with a range of possible reactions.”

But the mayor said he wasn’t informed about that decision, and he met with the museum and Amersfoort’s Jewish community on Thursday to discuss how the exhibition can go ahead.

“I am enormously saddened,” the mayor told the city council on Wednesday. “Jewish history and present-day life belong to our city. That must get the attention it deserves.” He said it was painful that the community was being made to feel it is not permitted to exist.

After Thursday’s meeting, the city said in a statement that the city, the museum and the Jewish community would look together at how 300 years of Jewish life in Amersfoort could be shown in an exhibition. “It was a good and intensive conversation,” Bolsius said. “We jointly concluded that we consider it important that there is an exhibition telling the story of 300 years of Jewish culture in Amersfoort.”

The Amersfoort Synagogue dates back to 1727 and is the oldest functioning Ashkenazi synagogue in Western Europe. The Jewish community has planned a wide-ranging programme of concerts and performances to mark the synagogue’s 300th anniversary.

Earlier this week, a Jewish student association lecture at Maastricht University was cancelled less than an hour before it was due to start, with the university saying it couldn’t guarantee participants’ safety.

World.title: Skaters get three hours on natural ice as first frost arrives
World.content:
The first frost has appeared after temperatures dropped below freezing overnight in parts of the Netherlands, in Brabant, Limburg and parts of Zeeland, according to the national weather service KNMI.

It also allowed the season’s first natural ice skating in Gelderland for a couple of hours in early morning.

The lowest temperature was recorded in Woensdrecht in Brabant, at minus 1.2°. Ell in Limburg reached minus 1.1° and Westdorpe in Zeeland minus 0.4°.

It does not yet count as an official frost day though. For that, the temperature at the KNMI’s base in De Bilt, near Utrecht, has to fall below zero. Overnight it stayed at 0.8° there.

In Winterswijk, in Gelderland, the local skating club opened the country’s first natural ice rink of the season, even though there was only ground frost there. The club uses special techniques to make ice quickly.

“When you tell people that, they say ‘it can’t be done’. But it can,” chairman Auke Spijkstra told broadcaster NOS. “It’s wonderful to see all those enthusiastic people.” About 20 skaters took to the ice. The sun soon melted it, and the rink closed again at around 10am.

World.title: Verwey-Jonker Institute facing bankruptcy amid AI rise
World.content:
The Verwey-Jonker Institute, an independent research institute in Utrecht, appears to be on the brink of bankruptcy, citing budget cuts and the rise of AI as the culprits. The Institute has applied to court for a suspension of payments.

Moving to a less expensive location and downsizing its board hasn’t been enough to save the beleaguered Institute. Broadcaster NOS also reported there’s been unrest within the agency’s leadership.

The Verwey-Jonker Institute, founded in 1993, addresses societal issues, providing research to governments, municipalities and others with “social value and impact”, according to its website. They work on issues such as poverty, youth, education, discrimination and domestic violence, among others.

The Institute says technological developments mean many of their clients are now using AI instead of engaging researchers.

While they say they want to continue their work, it will now be up to an administrator to see just how they can do that.

World.title: Graffiti group posts video of attack on Amsterdam metro
World.content:
A group of some 20 masked and hooded graffiti writers stopped a metro in Amsterdam Nieuw-West and sprayed the entire train with paint within minutes, leaving passengers inside stranded.

The action took place at the Henk Sneevlietweg stop last Saturday on Halloween. A video uploaded Tuesday on YouTube by the anonymous graffiti writers’ group Locos Worldwide, titled “Amsterdam Nightmare”, shows the sprayers entering the station and speed-spraying the train in orange, purple and black before running away cheering.

They also threw a bicycle onto the tracks and spray painted the driver’s window, leaving the train unable to move.

Shaken and shocked

“Our driver is quite shocked by the incident,” a spokesman for Amsterdam transport company GVB said. “We can also imagine that this was a frightening situation for travellers.”

The GVB, which called the incident a “serious form of vandalism”, has filed a police report. It’s still not known who is responsible for the action, but the GVB says it plans to seek compensation from the “perpetrators” when they are identified.

They tagged the train with apparent acronyms ‘NSPSKU’ and ‘LCSNTC’. NSPS has been tagged on transit vehicles in the past.

Police say they are taking the incident “seriously” and have appealed to the public to come forward with any video images they may have.

The GVB says that while graffiti does happen, the scale of the Halloween night action is extraordinary. Not only was the driver severely shaken, but the ordeal was a “potentially terrifying situation for passengers as well”.

And, according to the GVB, it put them at risk. “There was not only a subway smeared, but also a bicycle thrown on the track. That entails major security risks,” a spokesman said.

Five years ago, Locos Worldwide uploaded another video showing a masked group spray painting an in-service Amsterdam metro. The group also posts similar actions that have taken place across Europe, including in Paris, Madrid and Copenhagen.

Credit rating agency S&P has revised Poland’s outlook to negative, saying that the country has seen “one of the most significant fiscal deteriorations globally” and that “political polarisation hinders fiscal consolidation”. It also lowered the country’s long- and short-term local currency ratings. S&P’s decision follows similar ones by the other members of the big three rating agencies. Fitch has had Poland on negative outlook since last year, while Moody’s cut the country’s credit rating in September this year to its lowest level since 2002. In a statement issued on Friday evening, S&P said that its “negative outlook reflects the risk that elevated budgetary deficits and rising government debt could constrain policy flexibility in the face of future shocks”. “This could expose Poland to shifts in investor sentiment or necessitate a sharp fiscal adjustment that would weigh on economic growth,” they added. 🚨Bardzo źle to wygląda! S&P o finansach Polski: „Takie pogorszenie sytuacji budżetowej należy do najpoważniejszych na świecie”. Dług netto ma wzrosnąć o ponad 20 pkt proc. PKB w 5 lat i przekroczyć 70% PKB w 2029 r. S&P obniżyła rating długu w PLN i perspektywę do negatywnej. — Piotr Nowak (@PiotrNowak_PL) November 7, 2026 Poland has struggled with ballooning budget deficits in recent years, driven by a rapidly expanding defence budget in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and longer-term increases in social spending. Last year’s deficit, at 7.3% of GDP, was the second-highest in the European Union. This year it is forecast to drop slightly, to 6.7%, according to recent finance ministry projections. But next year’s budget foresees a deficit of 7.1%. Those figures are much higher than those the government pledged to reach when, in 2024, Poland was placed under the EU’s excessive deficit procedure. For example, the deficit was supposed to fall to 3.7% of GDP in 2027. Moody’s, one of the big three global credit rating agencies, has cut Poland’s rating from A2 to A3. The last time the agency had Poland at such a low level was 2002. It is also the first time any of the big three agencies has downgraded Poland since 2016 https://t.co/qUAEouqhlx — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 19, 2026 S&P says that it projects Poland’s net debt exceeding 70% of GDP by 2029. That rise of “more than 20 percentage points over five years marks one of the most significant fiscal deteriorations globally”. The agency notes that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in 2027, making any “meaningful consolidation unlikely” before then. Moreover, the veto power of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki means the government “faces constraints in advancing its legislative and fiscal consolidation agenda”. Pointing to the ongoing crisis around the constitutional court, S&P also warns that “renewed institutional tensions could weigh on policy predictability”. However, the agency notes that Poland’s economy remains “resilient”, with real GDP growth projected to average around 3% between 2027 and 2029. It also points to the fact that the country has seen a peak in EU-funded investment this year, while exports have picked up. As well as shifting Poland’s overall outlook to negative, S&P downgraded its local currency ratings – meaning its assessment of the country’s willingness and ability to service debt denominated in domestic currency – from A/A-1 to A-/A-2, the same level as its foreign currency ratings. “Our fiscal projections are now weaker than previously envisaged, and we note a track record of recent fiscal slippages amid a challenging policy environment, which underpin our assessment of Poland’s reduced fiscal flexibility,” wrote the agency. Finance minister Andrzej Domański acknowledged S&P’s decision to lower Poland’s outlook to negative in a social media post. However, he pointed to the section of the agency’s report in which it said that the government is constrained by presidential vetoes. Nawrocki has vetoed a record number of bills since becoming president last year, including several fiscal measures. “Despite the presidential vetoes, we will continue taking steps to strengthen the country’s finances,” wrote Domański. 🇵🇱 Agencja S&P utrzymała rating Polski na poziomie A-, obniżając jednak jego perspektywę do negatywnej. W uzasadnieniu decyzji czytamy wprost: „Rząd premiera Donalda Tuska napotyka ograniczenia w realizacji swoich planów legislacyjnych i konsolidacji finansów publicznych ze… — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) November 6, 2026 However, Nawrocki notes that the ballooning budget deficits preceded his coming to power, and has blamed the government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk for overseeing budgetary “chaos” and causing “a deep crisis of credibility”. In response to S&P’s announcement, Marcin Ociepa, deputy head of the parliamentary caucus of Law and Justice (PiS), the largest opposition party, accused the government of “trying to shift responsibility for Poland’s credit rating downgrade [sic] onto the president”. “Any family that managed its finances the way Donald Tusk manages our country’s finances would drown in debt and go bankrupt,” wrote Ociepa. “That is exactly what awaits Poland if this government remains in power.” ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: 2,000-year-old Vandal artefacts anonymously handed to Polish museum
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A collection of artefacts associated with the Vandals and dating back almost 2,000 years has been handed anonymously to a museum in eastern Poland. The collection includes a sword, spear and javelin heads, shield components and spurs. Museum staff do not know who originally discovered the burial or exactly where it was located, leaving the circumstances of the find largely a mystery. The Father Stanisław Staszic Museum in Hrubieszów announced in a Facebook post that the objects had been passed to them anonymously through an intermediary. The items are in poor condition and will undergo urgent conservation, with the iron components of the weapons particularly vulnerable after centuries in the ground. They were also exposed to high temperatures during a burial practice in which the deceased was burned along with their personal belongings. The museum says that the nature of the objects indicates that their owner held a high social position. The most notable object is a sword preserved in three pieces, reflecting the Vandal practice of deliberately breaking or bending weapons and other grave artefacts as part of funeral rituals. The collection also contains two spearheads, both broken. Other items include a shield boss with a spike, a shield grip, a fragment of a knife, a belt buckle and two spurs. Fragments of a bone comb and a bronze fibula, used to fasten a cloak, were also recovered. The circumstances surrounding the discovery and recovery of the objects remain unknown, but the museum says that, according to the information it has received, the burial site was discovered in an agricultural field several years ago in the municipality of Werbkowice. “We intend to verify the exact location through archaeological excavations, most likely next summer,” they added. “Based on the information we have gathered, there are strong indications that there may be more similar burials in the area that have been disturbed by agricultural work.” The opportunity to recover the objects and transfer them to an appropriate institution arose only recently. The museum said that a local metal detectorist played a key role in arranging the transfer, acting as an intermediary in securing the artefacts. The recovery of the artefacts follows another recent archaeological discovery in the same region. In August, the museum announced that a metal boss from a warrior’s shield dating to the second century was found at a scrap metal yard near Hrubieszów. The Vandals were an ancient Germanic people believed to have reached the territories of present-day Poland around the 3rd or 2nd century BC. They lived in the region for several centuries and are generally associated by researchers with the Przeworsk culture, which flourished across parts of present-day Poland during the Iron Age and Roman period. Around the turn of the 4th and 5th centuries AD, amid the expansion of the Huns, they left Central Europe and moved westwards into the declining Roman Empire. As the Vandals left Central Europe, the Slavic population gradually moved into the region over the following centuries. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish deputy PM proposes “constitutional reset” to resolve crisis around top court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The leader of one of the parties in Poland’s ruling coalition has put forward plans for a “constitutional reset” that he hopes can resolve the crisis around the country’s top court. The proposal, presented on Thursday by deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, head of the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), would remove all current judges on the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) and allow new judges to be chosen only with the approval of 60% of members of parliament and the president. To take effect, the measure would require amending Poland’s constitution, something that has happened only twice since the document was adopted in 1997 and which also requires a three-fifths majority in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament. Deeskalacja sytuacji wokół Trybunału Konstytucyjnego jest konieczna aby przywrócić obywatelom niezależny sąd konstytucyjny. Apelują o to przedstawiciele organizacji społecznych, Rada Przedsiębiorców, Naczelna Rada Adwokacka, Helsińska Fundacja Praw Człowieka i Episkopat Polski.… pic.twitter.com/3RCsKRlSiM — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) November 5, 2026 Kosiniak-Kamysz’s announcement comes amid the fallout from events last Friday, when eight new judges elected to the TK this year by the government’s majority in parliament seized control of the court. They announced that its chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, had been suspended for failing to fulfil his duties, including by refusing to allow most of those judges to take up their seats on the court. Święczkowski denounced the takeover as an illegal “coup d’état”. He has been backed by the tribunal’s remaining six judges, who, like him, were appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government, which brought the TK under its political influence when it ruled from 2015 to 2023. As well as pitting judges aligned with the national-conservative PiS, which is now the main opposition party, and the current more liberal government against one another, the dispute also centres around the legitimacy of certain judges. The government points to the fact that PiS unlawfully appointed three judges to the TK in 2015. As a result, both Polish and European courts have found the tribunal in its current form to be illegitimate. Meanwhile, Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with PiS, has refused to swear in five of the eight judges appointed by the government’s parliamentary majority this year, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 The standoff has led some NGOs and experts to call for a “constitutional reset”, whereby the TK would be reformed to make the process of selecting judges more consensual and less politicised. Indeed, the current government even proposed legislation in 2024 that would have required new TK judges to be approved by a three-fifths parliamentary majority. The plans would also have removed unlawfully appointed judges from the PiS era and annulled rulings they were involved in. That prompted the president at the time, Andrzej Duda, who was also aligned with PiS, to send the bills to the TK, which was still packed with PiS-era judges, for assessment. The tribunal rejected them as unconstitutional the following year. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Now, Kosiniak-Kamysz has proposed new legislation intended to resolve the issue. His solution would create a mechanism under which parliament, at the request of the National Council of the Judiciary (KRS), could declare the TK “permanently incapable of performing its duties”. Such a status could only be declared with the support of a three-fifths majority of both houses of parliament – the Sejm and the Senate – combined. It would have to come at the request of the KRS because, says Kosiniak-Kamysz, the terms of judges cannot be shortened without the participation of other judges. The process of appointing new TK judges would involve the speaker of the Sejm proposing candidates after obtaining the opinions of the heads of the Supreme Court and the Supreme Administrative Court – which are separate from the TK – as well as professional bodies representing legal professions. The candidates proposed by the speaker would also have to receive the prior consent of the president. For a new TK judge to be approved, they would have to receive the support of three fifths of members of the Sejm and Senate combined. 💬 336 głosów posłów i senatorów. To wykracza poza większość jakąkolwiek koalicyjną dzisiaj sformułowaną – @KosiniakKamysz w Warszawie pic.twitter.com/iLUuM5TSxQ — 🍀 PSL (@nowePSL) November 5, 2026 Whereas TK judges currently all serve nine-year terms, under Kosiniak-Kamysz’s proposal, five of the judges would serve three-year terms, five of them six-year terms, and the final five would serve for nine years. Unlike now, the new judges would not have to swear their oath before the president, but before parliament. Kosiniak-Kamysz emphasised, however, that the measure was intended as a “one-time” emergency tool. “Later, we will return to the method of selecting judges described today in the constitution, or a better one, if there is a majority for it.” The current method of choosing new TK judges requires only the support of a majority in the Sejm. However, judges must then swear an oath “before the president”, an issue that has become a bone of contention this year. The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 Kosiniak-Kamysz’s plans would require changes to Poland’s constitution, which specifies the manner in which TK judges are chosen. A constitutional amendment requires the support of a three-fifths majority in the Sejm and a simple majority in the Senate. It does not need presidential approval. PSL itself has only 28 members of the 460-seat Sejm and four senators. Kosiniak-Kamysz acknowledged that “it won’t be an easy road” to win the necessary support for his idea. He appealed not only to his fellow ruling parties, but also to opposition groups that have expressed their backing for a constitutional reset, such as the centre-right Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) and far-right Confederation (Konfederacja). On Thursday evening, one of Confederation’s leaders, Sławomir Mentzen, shared a photo of himself meeting Kosiniak-Kamysz, with the caption: “It’s going in the right direction”. However, some voices within the ruling coalition expressed scepticism towards the idea. Borys Budka, a former leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) – which is the largest governing party – said it was “hard to imagine changing the constitution alongside someone like PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński”. Tomasz Trela of The Left (Lewica) likewise said that, “if anyone thinks The Left will change the constitution arm in arm with PiS, they’re mistaken”, reports Polsat News. World.title: Chinese fashion platform Shein to invest €500 million in Polish logistics hub

Chinese fast fashion platform Shein has announced a €500 million (2.2 billion zloty) investment to expand its logistics centre in Poland, a move it says will create around 2,000 new jobs by the end of this year. The announcement comes amid growing controversy over the impact of Chinese e-commerce platforms on European businesses and follows a recent decision by the European Union to introduce a special fee on low-value parcels sent from outside the EU and European Free Trade Area. SHEIN investește 500 mil. euro în Polonia. Extinde hub-ul logistic europeanhttps://t.co/WNbib4dFta pic.twitter.com/KiI1AB4wFM — Cristi Dorombach (@piticu21) November 4, 2026 The investment will expand Shein’s existing logistics facility in Magnice, near the city of Wrocław in southwestern Poland, which has been operating since 2022. The expansion will bring total employment at the site to around 10,000 by creating 2,000 jobs in logistics, supply chain management, technology and warehouse operations, according to local news service Wroclaw.pl. The facility will also host 6,500 autonomous robots for sorting items. Shein says that the move will help it cut delivery times in Europe, allowing some orders to arrive within 48 hours. “This investment in Poland clearly demonstrates our commitment and belief in the potential of the European market,” said Leonard Lin, the firm’s global head of public affairs. “Poland has become one of the pillars of our operations in Europe,” he added. “This latest investment is a testament to our confidence in the country’s potential, the competencies of its workforce, and its business environment.” The expansion comes as Shein faces a tougher trading environment in Europe. Its sales in the region fell by 13.9% year-on-year to $3.77 billion in the second quarter, while net profit dropped by 67%. The decline comes as the EU steps up efforts to curb the influx of low-cost imports from Chinese platforms such as Shein, Temu and AliExpress, which European retailers say pose unfair competition. In July, the bloc introduced a €3 fee on parcels worth less than €150. From 1 November, a further €2 handling fee was added to all imported parcels, regardless of their value, to cover customs processing costs. China overtook Germany to become Poland’s biggest source of imports for the first time in July, ending a period of around 35 years in which Germany had consistently held top spot https://t.co/U6rQwfEJ7I — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2026 Shein has also faced accusations of labour-law violations at its facilities in China, including concerns that it may use cotton produced through forced labour. The company disputes many of the allegations, saying that it prohibits forced and child labour and regularly inspects working conditions at its suppliers. China is an increasingly important trading partner in Poland. In July, it overtook Germany to become Poland’s largest source of imports for the first time, driven by rising purchases of cars, computer hardware and consumer goods. Poland has detained and charged six people – five Poles and one Russian – suspected of running an operation to illegally supply Russia with military components. Investigators say that over 2 million zloty (€450,000) worth of equipment was smuggled into the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. The arrests, which took place on 21 October and 2 November, were announced on Thursday morning by Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) and National Prosecutor’s Office. 🚨 ROSYJSKI WYWIAD. PRZEMYT CZĘŚCI DO PRODUKCJI UZBROJENIA. 6 ZATRZYMANYCH.@ABW_GOV_PL rozbiła grupę podejrzaną o działalność na rzecz rosyjskich służb specjalnych. 🔴6⃣ osób zatrzymanych, 🔴2⃣1⃣przeszukanych lokalizacji, 🔴 4⃣osoby z zarzutami szpiegostwa – wszystkie trafiły… pic.twitter.com/L90n3rf5rY — ABW (@ABW_GOV_PL) November 5, 2026 Prosecutors report that all six suspects have been charged with participating in an organised criminal group that sought to export weapon components from Poland to Russia in violation of a ban on such trade. Four of the suspects have also been charged under Poland’s espionage law, accused of acting on behalf of Russian intelligence in return for financial benefits. Those four individuals have been placed in pretrial detention. The other two were released with preventative measures put in place. The ABW says that the criminal group “illegally supplied Russia with significant quantities of military components, including those used in the production of ammunition and weapons systems”. “This type of activity may lead to the strengthening of the Russian arms industry and the military capabilities of the Russian Federation, and thus pose a serious threat to Poland’s security and interests,” wrote the agency. Prosecutors say that the group operated at least between June 2023 and December 2025 in Poland, Lithuania and Russia. Members were responsible for procuring goods and transporting them to Kaliningrad, which borders Poland and Lithuania. “Vehicles equipped with hidden compartments were used to transport the goods,” wrote the prosecutor’s office. “The suspects repeatedly crossed the Polish-Russian border, and some of the transports were intercepted by Polish border guards.” Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, revealed that the six suspects include five Polish citizens, aged 25 to 52, and one Russian woman, aged 37. Onet, a leading news website, reports, based on unnamed sources, that the Russian citizen acted as a liaison between the group and the foreign intelligence agency behind the operation. Funkcjonariusze @ABW_GOV_PL zatrzymali 6 osób podejrzanych o udział w zorganizowanej grupie przestępczej działającej przeciwko Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej. Wśród zatrzymanych jest pięciu Polaków w wieku od 25 do 52 lat i 37-letnia Rosjanka. 🛑 Sąd – pod zarzutem szpiegostwa -… — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) November 5, 2026 Poland has seen a huge rise in espionage cases in recent years. The ABW launched 48 investigations related to espionage last year, more than twice as many as in 2024. In those two years taken together, there were more espionage investigations than over the previous three decades combined. Last month, a Polish man was jailed for five and a half years for spying on behalf of Russia. The tasks assigned to him included reconnaissance of an airport as part of a possible plan to assassinate Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky while he travelled through Poland. In July, a Russian married couple with refugee status in Poland were convicted of working as spies on behalf of Moscow. In October, a member of Poland’s military reserve, who holds both Polish and Ukrainian citizenship, was detained on suspicion of espionage. World.title: Polish far-right leader Braun to face second trial
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun will again stand trial, after prosecutors filed an indictment against him for a series of anti-Ukrainian, anti-Jewish, anti-LGBT and anti-EU acts committed during his presidential election campaign last year. Braun is already separately on trial for a number of other alleged crimes, including an attack on a Jewish religious ceremony in parliament. He is also facing further charges for a range of other alleged offences. Grzegorz Braun stanie przed sądem. Prokuratura Okręgowa w Warszawie skierowała dziś akt oskarżenia za zuchwałą kradzież flag Ukrainy w Białej Podlaskiej i Unii Europejskiej w Katowicach, zniszczenie wystawy LGBT w Sejmie oraz zniesławienie organizatorów akcji Żonkile i Muzeum… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 4, 2026 On Wednesday, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw announced that it had indicted Braun for four alleged crimes. It was able to do so after the European Parliament, where Braun sits as an MEP, stripped him of immunity earlier this year. One of the charges, for criminal defamation, stems from Braun’s claim, during a televised presidential debate in April last year, that the yellow paper daffodils distributed each year in Warsaw to mark the anniversary of the 1943 Jewish Ghetto Uprising against German Nazi rule are “symbols of shame”. Prosecutors say that Braun’s words were “extremely xenophobic, manipulative and aggressive”, and that they defamed the organisers of the daffodil campaign, in particular the POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews in Warsaw. During the same debate, Braun also warned about the “Judaisation” of Poland, saying that “Jews have far too much say in Polish affairs”. That prompted protests by some of his opponents, one of whom filed a notification to prosecutors. Two other charges relate to thefts of flags. In one incident, Braun and his supporters removed a Ukrainian flag hanging outside city hall in the town of Biała Podlaska during a campaign event. In another, he removed a European Union flag from the industry ministry in the city of Katowice and set it on fire. Braun regularly rails against what he calls the “Ukrainisation” of Poland, warning of the supposed dangers of having so many Ukrainian refugees and migrants in the country. He is also a vocal critic of the EU. On those and other issues, Braun’s rhetoric often echoes Russian propaganda. The final charge, of destruction of property, relates to an incident in June 2025, when Braun vandalised an exhibition about the LGBT+ community in the Polish parliament. He regularly condemns what he calls the “perversions” of LGBT+ people, and has called for homosexuality to be criminalised. The European Parliament has again stripped Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face charges of denying Nazi crimes. The decision marks the sixth time it has lifted Braun’s immunity, and the second time for charges of Holocaust denial https://t.co/O9FN1YbchE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2026 The charges Braun faces carry prison sentences of up to five years in the case of destruction of property, and up to one year in the case of criminal defamation and theft. Additionally, the deputy leader of Braun’s Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party, Roman Fritz, was indicted for assisting in the theft of the EU flag, while four other men (who have not waived their right to anonymity under Polish law) were indicted for their alleged roles in stealing both the EU and Ukrainian flags. All four incidents for which Braun has been indicted took place when he was campaigning for the May 2025 presidential elections, in which he finished a surprise fourth, with 6.3% of the vote. Since then, KKP has continued to perform strongly in polls, with its support currently standing at around 9%. If it obtained that kind of result at next year’s parliamentary elections, it would be likely to play a major role in deciding what kind of government could be formed. Our essential guide to Poland's parliamentary elections, which will take place one year from now. How does voting work? What do polls suggest the outcome will be? Which issues may animate the campaign? And what role will President Nawrocki play? https://t.co/fmdoFpBaxz — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 15, 2026 Much of Braun’s political brand has been built around provocative statements and actions. The politician is already on trial for his attack on a Jewish Hanukkah ceremony taking place in parliament, at which he put out the candles with a fire extinguisher. In their statement on Wednesday, the Warsaw prosecutor’s office noted that the latest hearings in that trial had been cancelled after Braun presented a medical certificate justifying his absence. However, the prosecutors pointed out that, last Friday, the day that the hearings had been due to begin, Braun attended a protest by opposition supporters outside the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw, which that evening had been taken over by government-backed judges. Braun was pictured “jostling with police riot police, addressing the crowd and giving interviews”, showing “no signs of health problems that would prevent him from attending the hearing”, wrote the prosecutors. They have therefore asked the court to investigate the doctor who issued the medical certificate. Polish political leaders have reacted to the results of Tuesday’s US midterm elections, in which the Democrats won control of both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republicans. The outcome was welcomed by Poland’s ruling coalition, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk declaring that “democracy won”. The response was more muted from the right-wing opposition and the office of conservative President Karol Nawrocki, who is a Trump ally. 🚨 🇺🇸 Tusk gives Trump some great advice. But will the US president listen? Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk urged the US president to seek compromises after the Republicans' defeat and not to rely on vetoes as his main way of governing. Trump had earlier threatened to become… pic.twitter.com/s3E6G5zIQT — NEXTA (@nexta_tv) November 4, 2026 Tusk addressed the election results on Wednesday afternoon local time at a press conference alongside his Czech counterpart, Andrej Babiš. “Today, democracy won in America,” said a smiling Tusk. “I love democracy; it is a beautiful thing.” “As President Donald Trump himself said just after the election, the Democrats did a good job, and I really could not agree more with him this time,” added Tusk. “I hope that the result will stabilise the situation also in our region.” Although the United States remains Poland’s most important security partner, Tusk’s government – a broad, pro-EU coalition that ranges from left to centre right – has at times had uneasy relations with the Trump administration. It has been critical of Trump’s conciliatory approach towards Russia, his often tough stance on Ukraine, as well as his pursuit of US control over Greenland. Meanwhile, the head of the parliamentary caucus of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, Zbigniew Konwiński, told broadcaster Polsat News that “personally, I was happy with the Democrats’ victory”. “We know how Donald Trump behaves, how volatile he is in his political declarations, how he can sometimes put Ukraine in a more difficult position than Russia, so I would rather look for the positives in what happened,” said Konwiński. “If we look at recent years, the more Democrats, the stronger the Democrats, the better for Poland,” he added. .@Konwinski_PO: Cieszę się z wygranej Demokratów w USA, bo to lepszy scenariusz dla Polski. @marcinfijolek pic.twitter.com/gJ3TnlMn0l — Graffiti_PN (@Graffiti_PN) November 4, 2026 The speaker of Poland’s parliament, Włodzimierz Czarzasty, who is also the leader of one of KO’s junior coalition partners, The Left (Lewica), has clashed with the US ambassador to Poland twice this year over Czarzasty’s criticism of Trump. Today, Czarzasty shared and commented on a social media post by Trump, published in the wake of the Democrats’ victory, in which the US president showed an image of his signature red cap with the word “VETO” on it. “Where have I heard this before?” wrote Czarzasty, referring to the fact that Nawrocki has vetoed a record number of bills passed by parliament, where Tusk’s coalition has a majority. Czarzasty then went on to list a series of characteristics that he suggested both Trump and Nawrocki share, including “arrogance”, “lack of respect for women”, a “suspicious past”, “transactional exploitation of their position”, and “admiration for politicians with fascist tendencies”. Skąd ja to znam? Arogancja. Buta. Nieuzasadniona pewność siebie. Brak szacunku dla kobiet ( a to popchnę jakąś dwojga nazwisk, a to zakpię prymitywnie). Dziwna przeszłość. Instrumentalne traktowanie dziennikarzy. Pieniądze za spotkania. Transakcyjne wykorzystywanie funkcji.… pic.twitter.com/ryT2BMOZb2 — Włodzimierz Czarzasty 📚📖 (@wlodekczarzasty) November 4, 2026 Nawrocki has closely aligned himself with Trump. During last year’s Polish presidential election campaign, Trump invited Nawrocki for a private meeting at the White House. His then-homeland security secretary, Kristi Noem, visited Poland to endorse Nawrocki. Nawrocki himself has not thus far commented on Tuesday’s midterm election results. However, Marcin Przydacz, the head of the president’s International Policy Bureau, did address the issue in a social media post. “As predicted, in the US midterm elections voters decided on change,” wrote Przydacz. “Poland will continue its good cooperation with the US, because it is our ally, and collaboration is in our mutual interest.” Przydacz also added that the results were “a reminder for Tusk” that “no government lasts forever”. In Poland, too, “the moment will come when voters will decide on change – and it might be quite soon”, added Przydacz, in a nod to next year’s Polish parliamentary elections. Zgodnie z przewidywaniami w wyborach połówkowych w USA wyborcy zdecydowali o zmianie. Wcześniej wygrywali Republikanie, dziś Demokraci. Polska będzie kontynuować dobrą współpracę z USA, bo jest to nasz sojusznik, a kooperacja jest w naszym wspólnym interesie. O tym, kto sprawuje… — Marcin Przydacz (@marcin_przydacz) November 4, 2026 Tusk’s foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, meanwhile, used the US election results to revive his long-running feud with Elon Musk, who is no longer part of the Trump administration but donated enormous amounts of money to support the Republicans ahead of the midterms. Last year, Musk and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticised Sikorski after he suggested that Musk had threatened Ukraine. In a post on his social media platform, X, Musk told Sikorski to “be quiet, small man”. On Wednesday, Tusk shared a screenshot of a tweet he had published last year, after Musk left the Trump administration, in which Sikorski wrote: “See, big man, politics is harder than you thought.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers.
