اعتراض وتدمير صاروخين طواف (كروز) بمنطقتي الرياض والجنوبية. pic.twitter.com/pUlP8Fe4g7 — المتحدث الرسمي باسم قوات التحالف (@CJFCSpox) November 8, 2026

Earlier, the Saudi air defenses also intercepted a missile targeting the Eastern Province.

The Saudi Civil Defense earlier issued alert warnings of potential danger in Riyadh City and Najran Provice, but lifted them shortly afterwards. The authority also raised warnings on Buqayq and Al-Ahsa Governorates and Dammam City but lifted them immediately after the danger has passed.

التحالف:



الدفاع الجوي اعترض ودمر صاروخين باليستيين أطلقتهما الميليشيا الحوثية الإرهابية باتجاه الرياض. pic.twitter.com/ssHlmSisv2 — المتحدث الرسمي باسم قوات التحالف (@CJFCSpox) November 8, 2026

The coalition has reported at least 15 ballistic and cruise missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles intercepted or destroyed across the Kingdom this month.

On Saturday, air defenses destroyed a cruise missile launched toward Riyadh Region. A day earlier, two ballistic missiles targeting Najran were intercepted, with debris falling and authorities assessing possible damage. Two drones were also destroyed in Riyadh and Makkah regions on Nov. 6.

Other interceptions included a ballistic missile targeting Madinah Region on Nov. 5, three drones directed toward the southern, Eastern and Makkah regions on Nov. 3, and two drones and a ballistic missile targeting Riyadh and the southern region on Nov. 2.

The coalition also reported intercepting a drone and a ballistic missile aimed at the southern region on Nov. 1.

Airport attacks disrupt air travel

The latest attacks follow a series of Houthi strikes on Saudi airports, energy facilities and other infrastructure that have caused significant disruption to civilian aviation.

King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh suspended operations following attacks in October that killed and wounded civilians. Its closure was extended to allow safety inspections before operations gradually resumed under restrictions.

Several international airlines extended suspensions of services to Riyadh into November, while disruptions also affected airports in Dammam, Abha and Najran.

Attacks linked to wider regional conflict

The renewed Houthi campaign comes amid the US-Israeli war against Iran, which began on Feb. 28 and has intensified tensions across the Middle East.

The Iran-aligned Houthis have expanded their attacks against Saudi targets as the wider confrontation has escalated, raising concerns over threats to civilian infrastructure, energy supplies and maritime shipping lanes.

On Nov. 1, Al-Maliki announced that coalition forces had conducted a precision operation to neutralize vital resources used by the Houthis to support their military activities, particularly their ballistic missile and drone programs.

He said the group was exploiting those resources to sustain attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Yemen and Saudi Arabia, as well as threaten maritime shipping in the southern Red Sea.

The coalition warned that it would continue taking operational measures to deter further attacks and protect the security of the Kingdom and the region.

World.title: Departing UN chief calls this ‘a moment of truth’ in fight to curb global warming
World.content:
UNITED NATIONS: As United Nations climate talks kick off in Turkiye on Monday, Secretary-General António Guterres has an urgent message for world leaders: “This is a moment of truth.”

He’s delivered variations of this ominous warning about climate change, caused by the burning of fossil fuels like oil and gas, in the past decade, often with increasingly hyperbolic language. Three years ago, he even said, “the era of global boiling has arrived, “ referring to rising temperatures and increasing extreme weather, both results of climate change.

But this time, it will be his last global warming sermon as head of the United Nations as his second and last term expires at the end of the year. And the sense of urgency is palpable in a world with worsening killer heat waves, storms, floods and droughts amid ever higher temperatures and, on top of all of it, El Niño, a naturally occurring climate pattern that scrambles weather systems around the globe.

“This is a moment of truths. We can no longer wait, we can no longer have endless discussions in which everybody tries to push the responsibility to someone else. Everybody must do more, everybody must do more now,” Guterres said he will tell leaders of the UN climate conference, known as COP31, scheduled Nov. 9-20.

The “moment of truth” message weighs so heavily that the Secretary-General used the phrase three times in 20 minutes during a recent exclusive interview with The Associated Press from his 38th floor conference room at UN headquarters. He discussed his one last push in the fight against climate change and a ten-year tenure where he became one of the most visible advocates urging often recalcitrant countries to do more to reduce their emissions of heat-trapping gases.

One of the most difficult days

The gravity of global warming reality also weighs heavily as he recalled his personal climate moment of truth. It was, he said, “one of the most difficult days of my life.”

It came last year when he consulted with scientists before a major speech on climate. As he had for nine years, Guterres was going to insist that the 2015 Paris Agreement’s main goal — limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) since pre-industrial times — was still alive. He was going to say the world needs to do far more to keep below that threshold, and that it was doable.

“Scientists told me you cannot say that because that’s no longer true,” said Guterres, an engineer before his political career. Too much carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, the result of burning fossil fuels, had been released into the atmosphere.

“That was an enormous shock for me,” he said. Now the UN is trying to limit how much past that threshold the world heads.

It felt like a failure, Guterres said.

“But it’s not the world that’s failed, it’s the political leadership that’s failed,” Guterres said. Protecting the planet, he said, requires a long-term strategic view. Yet in many political systems “there is no strategic view. And policies change frequently, not allowing the kind of constant determined investment that is necessary,” Guterres said.

He pointed to his tenure as Portugal’s prime minister in the late 1990s to show it’s possible to invest long term in a greener future. He added that a worldwide boom in wind and solar power as cheaper alternatives to fossil fuels gives him hope.

With wars raging in Ukraine and Iran and worries about artificial intelligence — which he also tried to rally world leaders around — there are a lot of threats out there, Guterres said.

“The problem is that all these things are getting combined,” Guterres said, noting the huge electricity and water consumption and carbon emissions of AI.

War-related energy shocks show that relying on fossil fuels is a fundamental security problem, he said.

Warning of a disaster that then came

Three years ago, Guterres toured the highest peaks of Nepal, warning of a future with swollen glacier-fed lakes bursting and devastating floods and landslides.

“I am here today to cry out from the rooftop of the world: Stop the madness,” Guterres said in 2023. “The glaciers are retreating, but we cannot,” he said. “We must end the fossil fuel age.”

“Unfortunately they came sooner than what I expected,” he recalled in the interview. Floods in August killed more than 1,400 people with another 5,600 missing. Scientists said climate change played a role in the disasters.

Guterres said someone needs to pay to help the victims of climate change, who often didn’t cause the problem.

“Fossil fuel companies are making huge profits and obviously those windfall profits should be taxed and those taxes should be applied in supporting the countries that are having the more dramatic impacts of climate change,” Guterres said.

Talking earlier this month with a science team on a drifting platform in the middle of the Arctic Ocean, Guterres mentioned that his trip to Mount Everest and chats with researchers changed him. He said the conversations created “a sense of fury in relation to those who go on, if not denying, at least refusing to take the measures that are necessary to stop this madness.”

Praised as a climate champion despite limitations

“António Guterres has consistently been eloquent, forceful and right on target in all of his many statements and initiatives to address the climate crisis,” former US Vice President Al Gore said. “He’s been so active on this issue because he understands clearly that it is the greatest challenge facing humanity.”

European Climate Foundation CEO Laurence Tubiana, who presided over the negotiations that resulted in the Paris Agreement, said Guterres “has done what he could, even pushing the ball much, much farther than any other SG, to the point that he may have been represented in a very adversarial context.”

Because nations don’t have to do what the UN or its leaders ask and superpowers have veto authority, Guterres said his position as secretary-general “has no real power. We have not much money you know. But there is one thing we have: A voice.”

That’s why he simply has three words of advice to whoever succeeds him: “Tell the truth.” The UN Security Council is still deciding on who will be the next secretary-general.

The one message Guterres said he wants the public to remember on climate change: “Take it seriously because it is an existential threat. And the first thing we need to fight is for our own lives.”

World.title: Iran says it has lifted its self-imposed limit on missile ranges
World.content:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guard says it has lifted a self-imposed limit of 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) on the range of its ballistic missiles, suggesting the country may seek to develop missiles capable of reaching more distant targets as fears of renewed all-out war rise.

The comments by the spokesman of Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard came days after the country’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khomeini, warned that “any kind and level of threat” from the US or Israel would face a response without geographic limits.

Asked at a Tehran news conference about the limit on missile ranges, Gen. Hossein Mohebbi said, “That restriction has been lifted for us.”

Iran is not known to have missiles that can go beyond the 2,000-kilometer (1,200-mile) limit. However, US officials have said technology from Iran’s space program can be repurposed to build intercontinental ballistic missiles.

World.title: Saudi healthcare entities, leaders claim top honors at London customer experience awards
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s healthcare sector won 36 gold, silver and bronze awards at the International Customer Experience Awards 2026 in London, including 29 awards secured by Health Holding Company and its affiliated health clusters, in recognition of efforts to improve service quality and the beneficiary experience.

Riyadh First Health Cluster led participating healthcare entities with 11 awards, followed by Madinah Health Cluster and Eastern Health Cluster with six awards each. Al-Ahsa Health Cluster received five awards, while Najran Health Cluster won a silver award for Best Patient Experience in the category for organizations with more than 5,000 employees.

The Ministry of Health’s branch in Najran Region secured four awards, including one gold and three bronze medals.

The Ministry of Interior’s Medical Services, represented by Security Forces Hospital in Dammam, won gold for Best Contact Center, silver for Best Patient Experience — Strategic Approach, and bronze in the Customers at the Heart of Everything category for organizations with more than 1,000 employees.

In a further achievement, two Saudi healthcare leaders received gold awards for customer experience leadership, competing against executives from international institutions and companies across multiple sectors.

Dr. Ibraheem Bani Hameem of the Ministry of Health’s Najran branch won gold in the CX Leader of the Year category, while Madinah Health Cluster CEO Abdulrahman Al-Harbi received gold in the same category for organizations with more than 1,000 employees.

The awards highlight the growing international recognition of Saudi healthcare institutions and professionals, as well as advances in leadership, service development and beneficiary engagement across the sector.

Separately, Eastern Health Cluster received a Best Practice distinction in the Financial Resource Management category at the International Best Practice Competition 2026.

The achievements support the goals of the Health Sector Transformation Program, one of the Saudi Vision 2030 realization programs, which aims to improve access to healthcare, enhance service quality and efficiency, strengthen the beneficiary experience and promote institutional excellence.

World.title: Five expatriates arrested for illegal soil excavation in Eastern Province
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s Special Forces for Environmental Security (SPES) have arrested five expatriates for illegally exploiting natural deposits in the Eastern Province, seizing four pieces of equipment used to excavate and transport soil, the Saudi Press Agency reported on Sunday.

The suspects, nationals of Pakistan, Bangladesh and Yemen, were taken into custody for violating the Kingdom’s Environmental Law, with legal action initiated against them, according to the SPA report.

The arrests are part of continuing enforcement operations by the SPES to protect the Kingdom’s natural resources, vegetation and wildlife and prevent activities that damage the environment.

The forces have stepped up action against a range of environmental violations in recent weeks, including the illegal transportation of local firewood, unauthorized entry into protected areas, pollution of soil and violations of camping and fire-safety regulations.

Crackdown on environmental violations

In another enforcement operation reported by SPA on Oct. 28, the forces apprehended a citizen for transporting two cubic meters of local firewood inside the Imam Turki bin Abdullah Royal Nature Reserve.

The seized firewood was handed over to the relevant authorities. The forces said transporting local firewood and charcoal carries a fine of up to SR16,000 per cubic meter.

On the same day, four citizens were arrested for entering the King Salman bin Abdulaziz Royal Reserve without permits. Unauthorized entry into protected areas carries a fine of SR5,000.

The forces also arrested a citizen on Oct. 25 for lighting a fire in an undesignated area inside the Imam Faisal bin Turki Royal Reserve, in violation of regulations designed to protect vegetation cover. The offense carries a fine of up to SR3,000.

On Oct. 27, another citizen was apprehended in the Asir region for camping without a permit in a forest or national park, an offense also punishable by a fine of up to SR3,000.

Protecting soil and natural resources

The enforcement campaign has also targeted activities that directly damage the Kingdom’s soil and natural resources.

On Oct. 9, the SPES arrested a Sudanese resident in the Eastern Province for dumping concrete materials and polluting the soil.

The forces said activities that directly or indirectly damage or pollute soil, adversely affect its use or destroy its natural properties are punishable by fines of up to SR10 million.

The latest arrests involving the five expatriates highlight the authorities’ efforts to prevent the unauthorized extraction and exploitation of natural deposits, an activity that can damage land and undermine environmental sustainability.

Saudi Arabia has introduced a range of environmental protection measures as part of its efforts to preserve natural resources, expand protected areas and improve environmental compliance under its broader sustainability objectives.

Public urged to report violations

The SPES has urged residents and citizens to report environmental and wildlife violations. It said all reports would be treated confidentially and that people reporting violations would bear no liability.

Reports can be made by calling 911 in the Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh and Eastern Province regions, and 999 or 996 in other regions of the Kingdom.

The public’s cooperation is considered an important part of efforts to protect the environment and ensure compliance with the Kingdom’s environmental regulations.

World.title: Strong earthquake shakes central Japan, shattering store windows and injuring at least 22
World.content:
TOKYO: A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.

Japan’s Meteorological Agency put the quake’s magnitude at 5.7, while the US Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.

A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.

Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee.

The quake, which struck at 1:04 a.m., was located about 40 kilometers (25 miles) below the earth’s surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighboring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments.

The meteorological agency warned people to brace for possible strong quakes in the coming week, especially the next two to three days.

“Please be on the lookout for mudslides, falling rocks and the possible effects from rainfall,” Ayataka Ebita, an agency official, told reporters.

He said no apparent change was detected so far to the Nankai Trough plate, where scientists say a megaquake can possibly hit.

The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.

Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes. Authorities frequently instruct people to stock up on bottled water, food and batteries, have plans ready to hide under tables and keep comfortable walking shoes at hand.

World.title: Pakistan-built robots serve taste of future to Karachi diners
World.content:
Karachi – Wheeling its way between dining booths at a neon-lit restaurant in Pakistan’s Karachi megacity, a robot waitress drops off a fresh pizza to an awaiting family.

While global buzz is growing around agile humanoids made in the United States, China and elsewhere, robotic staff are a rare sight in the South Asian country.

“Welcome to Sicilian. My name is Robia,” the waitress says in an electronic voice, looking down at diners through blinking red LED eyes.

Robia and her colleague Jojo are the DIY creations of Pakistani engineer Syed Osama Aziz, who is bringing a sci-fi reboot to Karachi’s storied dining scene.

They have spherical white heads and dark visors, similar to a motorcycle helmet, and sport black shawls around their neck in the style of a dupatta worn by women in the region.

Aziz, who also established The Sicilian restaurant, developed the machines using mostly locally manufactured parts, designing their circuit boards and programming them in his own lab.

“The equipment, the things needed to make robots, are not so easily available here, so we had to arrange them,” he told AFP.

The duo were developed through his robotics company, Cobot, with help from friends and some electronic components imported from abroad.

In China and other East Asian countries especially, robots are an increasingly common sight, shuttling food to customers in chain restaurants and taking on other jobs from cleaning to greeting hotel guests.

But they remain a novelty in Pakistan, where Aziz’s home-grown creations are attracting curious diners.

When they arrive at a table, the customers must either take the food off their serving tray themselves or wait for a human member of staff to assist them.

– Excited customers –

Aziz, whose workshop manufacturing the robots is located in Multan in Pakistan’s central Punjab province, hopes to make his creations more sophisticated in the future.

“Our plans are to add camera-based processing and image-processing features,” he said.

“That means the robot will also recognise you by looking at you, and it will remember what you ordered last time, and accordingly it will be able to give you better suggestions.”

For now, the robots are proving a hit with families, who flock to the restaurant to watch the machines in action.

“The best thing about it is that it introduces itself,” excited customer Ahmer Zameer told AFP, explaining the robot also “tells you what things you can order”.

Children reach out to touch the robots while their parents snap photographs and selfies.

Young customer Sonia Dilosker said she was impressed by the androids’ appearance and preferred their approach to serving customers, “because it is a machine and without any emotions”.

Restaurant staff say the novelty has brought a surge in customers — some travelling from across the sprawling port city to meet the robots.

“Our business has grown. People are coming from far away for this. They have seen a robot for the first time here,” staff member Hellen told AFP.

“People are excited to see this.”

World.title: Nuggets hold off Pacers in NBA Mexico City game
World.content:
Los Angeles – Denver star Nikola Jokic scored 19 points and grabbed 13 rebounds as the Nuggets held off Indiana’s second-half surge to triumph 114-102 on Saturday in the NBA’s Mexico City game.

Three-time NBA Most Valuable Player Jokic added eight assists, coming up just shy of a triple-double.

Cameron Johnson added 18 points and Jamal Murray chipped in 16 for the Nuggets, who saw a 27-point lead sliced to seven midway through the fourth quarter but held on for the victory before a sellout crowd of more than 20,000 at Mexico City’s Arena CDMX.

Indiana’s Pascal Siakam led all scorers with 23 points.

The league headed south of the border for its 16th regular-season contest in Mexico.

Along with 19 pre-season games, the country has hosted the most NBA games outside of the United States and Canada.

The Pacers, again playing without injured Tyrese Haliburton, jumped to a quick 5-0 lead and were up 7-4 when the Nuggets produced a 10-0 scoring run to seize a lead they wouldn’t relinquish.

Denver pushed the advantage to as many as 27 on the way to a 64-41 halftime edge.

The Pacers hit back with a 37-point third quarter and pulled within 102-95 on a Jarace Walker running basket with 7:27 remaining.

The Nuggets responded with a quick basket from Spencer Jones and a thunderous Aaron Gordon dunk as they kept the Pacers at bay.

The game was one of seven on Saturday’s slate, which also featured the Cleveland Cavaliers hosting the defending champion New York Knicks.

It’s the second heavyweight clash in as many nights in Cleveland, where the Cavs beat LeBron James and the Eastern Conference-leading Philadelphia 76ers on Friday.

It’s a rematch of last season’s Eastern Conference finals, in which the Knicks swept the Cavs on the way to their first NBA title since 1973.

World.title: PSG march on with 11th straight win
World.content:
Paris – Illia Zabarnyi scored the only goal of the game as a weakened Paris Saint-Germain claimed an unspectacular 1-0 win over Troyes in Ligue 1 on Saturday to make it 11 consecutive victories in all competitions.

Ukraine defender Zabarnyi headed in Senny Mayulu’s cross to break the deadlock in the 39th minute at the Parc des Princes, and that proved sufficient to beat their newly-promoted opponents who lie in the bottom three.

PSG were without a host of key players, with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele, Nuno Mendes, Maghnes Akliouche and captain Marquinhos all injured while Achraf Hakimi was rested and Joao Neves started as a substitute.

They still had enough to beat their dogged but limited opponents, with Troyes expected to struggle to secure Ligue 1 survival despite the backing of the City Football Group.

Fresh from hammering Villarreal 6-0 away in the Champions League in midweek, Luis Enrique’s PSG side have now won seven games on the bounce in Ligue 1 and are now three points clear of Paris FC at the top of the table.

Their 11-game winning streak in all competitions is their longest run of consecutive victories under Luis Enrique, who was appointed in 2023.

“It is so difficult and rare to achieve,” Luis Enrique said of the winning run.

“Football is always a really hard game to control. But I am happier to have won the eight games since the last international break than the 11 in a row overall.

“After the players come back from international duty we will try to keep doing the same thing.”

Zabarnyi’s goal, which followed a quickly-taken Desire Doue corner, was his second of the season and the expectation was that PSG would go on to run out emphatic winners.

However, Spain World Cup final hero Ferran Torres failed to make the most of several promising openings — he has now gone eight games without a goal after netting seven times in his first six PSG appearances.

“There’s no need to be worried for him. It’s normal. What matters to me is that the attacking players keep getting chances, and today their goalkeeper played very well,” Luis Enrique added.

– Paris FC give chase –

As PSG fans let off fireworks at one point in the second half, Troyes saw Renaud Ripart put a great chance wide before Lucas Maronnier had a late effort disallowed for offside.

PSG are next in action after the international break away to Nice in a fortnight, before the reigning European champions host Roma in the Champions League.

Earlier on Saturday, PSG’s neighbours Paris FC won 1-0 away to Auxerre thanks to a second-half goal by in-form striker Lassine Sinayoko.

Mali forward Sinayoko, a summer signing from Auxerre, opportunistically turned in an assist by Pablo Pagis, who was called up to the France squad for the first time by new coach Zinedine Zidane on Friday.

Sinayoko, 26, is the top scorer in Ligue 1 with nine goals in 10 games. Liam Rosenior’s Paris FC are second, three points behind PSG.

However, Lille and Lyon are both within striking distance of the two capital clubs before they play on Sunday.

Also on Sunday, Lens play host to Marseille seeking to erase the nightmare memory of Wednesday’s 9-1 Champions League loss at home to Como, which was a record-equalling defeat in the competition.

World.title: Thousands of Syrian troops to deploy to Yemen, Saudi Arabia: sources to AFP
World.content:
Dubai – Thousands of Syrian troops are set to deploy to Saudi Arabia and Yemen, with some already on the ground, multiple Yemeni officials told AFP, as Riyadh rallies international help to repel the Houthis and bolster the government in Aden.

It came after the two countries signed cooperation agreements this week including a defence deal, with Syria considering joining the recently enacted mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan.

Hundreds of Syrian troops have already been deployed to both sides of the border, according to three separate Yemeni military sources and a defence official, with more to come.

Later on Saturday, Syria’s official SANA news agency cited a diplomatic source who insisted Damascus had not sent troops to Yemen “at this time”.

However, a source from the Presidential Leadership Council, Yemen’s top governing body, told AFP that Syria would send as many as 3,000 troops to help fend off the Houthis.

The arrangement was greenlit during Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa’s visit to Riyadh this week, during which the two countries agreed to various deals, according to the PLC source.

“Syria is a long way from Yemen, but shares Ryadh’s interest in containing the influence of the Iran-allied axis in the region,” said Noah Bonsey of the International Crisis Group.

Later, a high-level Yemeni defence ministry source told AFP that while the first phase would involve around 3,000 troops, with some already in place, as many as 10,000 could eventually be deployed.

Those already stationed on the Yemeni side of the border at the moment are leading drone operations against the Houthis in the area, one of the military officials told AFP.

The kingdom — a key backer of Syria’s post-Assad government in place since late 2024 — has been pressing allies for help as it comes under daily fire from the Iran-backed group that recently seized swaths of the Red Sea coastline from the Riyadh-backed government.

The Houthis have ramped up attacks on the kingdom in recent weeks, forcing Riyadh airport to close for two weeks after fatal strikes there and threatening Saudi Arabia’s vast economic diversification plans.

– Boots on the ground –

According to the Yemeni defence ministry source, technical teams from the Syrian and Saudi defence ministries are currently in Riyadh putting the final touches on arrangements for Syrian forces to take part in operations against the Houthi militias.

Just last week, Syria’s top diplomat said publicly that Damascus was considering whether to join the NATO-style Mecca defence alliance that binds Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

The diplomatic source quoted by SANA said the agreement with Riyadh “focuses on training military forces and building their capabilities” and that “coordination visits” to Syria would take place next month.

This cooperation “could potentially develop in the future into a mutual defence agreement or Syria joining the Mecca Alliance,” the source said.

The Syrian army is comprised of a patchwork of groups, mostly Islamists including foreign jihadists that overthrew former strongman Bashar al-Assad in December 2024 after more than a decade of civil war.

That conflict devastated Syria’s economy and infrastructure and it is relying in particular on wealthy Gulf nations such as Saudi Arabia to help fund the vast cost of reconstruction.

– Alliances –

In August, Riyadh, Islamabad and Ankara signed their defence pact in Mecca, Islam’s holiest city, which states an attack on one country is to be considered an attack on all three.

Pakistan and Turkey have not announced any attacks on the Iran-backed Houthis.

Egypt’s parliament later approved President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s request to allow defensive military support for Saudi Arabia “if requested”.

Last month, French President Emmanuel Macron made a surprise visit to Riyadh and said France was sending troops to help shield a key Saudi oil terminal from Houthi attacks.

Also in October, the UK government announced it would deploy British fighter planes to help Saudi Arabia against the attacks.

Since the summer, Yemen has been gripped by renewed fighting after the collapse of a four-year-old truce.

The country has been reeling from war since 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, with a Saudi-led coalition entering the conflict a year later in support of the government.

World.title: Israel president taps Eisenkot to form new government
World.content:
Jerusalem – Israel’s president announced on Saturday he would task Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government following last week’s election, in what Netanyahu’s rivals see as a first step to remove the country’s longest-serving prime minister.

The opposition bloc led by Eisenkot, a former military chief and political newcomer who has tried to appeal to secular and liberal Israelis, has opened the door to a once improbable alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, which could give it the numbers to form a coalition.

President Isaac Herzog said that after consultations with all parties during the week, he would grant Eisenkot the first chance to form a government after the October 27 election, in which neither side secured a majority in a country deeply polarised by Netanyahu’s hard-right rule and worn down by three years of war.

The formal appointment would take place in an official ceremony on Sunday at the president’s residence in Jerusalem, Herzog’s office said.

Eisenkot was recommended by parties representing 67 lawmakers as opposed to 46 for Netanyahu’s bloc.

But the recommendations for Eisenkot included members of Israel’s Arab minority — whose seat haul soared in the election on the back of anger against Netanyahu — and right-leaning segments of the opposition oppose relying on Arab votes.

– Netanyahu pushes unity government –

Herzog, who originally came from Israel’s now defunct left-wing Labour Party but who has a non-partisan role and has forged a working relationship with Netanyahu, has signalled that he would like to explore a national unity government that would seek to bring together Jewish Israelis from across the political spectrum.

Pressure for a unity government could build if Netanyahu follows through on threats to resume war on Iran, although US President Donald Trump has not given the green light and received his own drubbing in Tuesday’s midterm elections.

Netanyahu, who has led Israel on and off for nearly two decades and guided its sharply rightward turn in recent years, faces corruption charges and potentially jail if he leaves office. He also faces an arrest warrant over the Gaza war from the International Criminal Court, whose authority he rejects.

Netanyahu has already called for a unity government but the opposition has stood firm on removing him first.

He has attacked opposition leaders for even considering working with Israeli Arabs, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after the creation of Israel in 1948.

The incumbent premier said on Saturday that a potential coalition between opposition parties and Arab lists, which he called Islamists, would “dismantle the State of Israel from within” and urged the formation of a unity government comprising “all the Zionist parties that want to safeguard our state.”

In response, Eisenkot’s Yashar party urged Netanyahu’s allies and members of his Likud party to form a unity government led by Eisenkot and to “publicly announce the dissolution of their alliance with the extremists”.

Opposition bloc member Avigdor Liberman, a former Netanyahu aide turned fierce critic who nonetheless shares his hawkish views on the Palestinians, has made clear that he will not sit with Eisenkot if he relies on Israeli-Arab votes.

But on Friday, Liberman — a staunch secularist whose support base initially was Russian-speaking immigrants — made a U-turn on another group he had shunned and said he was open to discussions on a law that would enshrine an exemption for ultra-Orthodox Jews from mandatory military service.

Liberman and another opposition leader, Naftali Bennett, had made closing the exemption a core campaign promise and had viscerally criticised ultra-Orthodox Jews as burdens on the state, responding to wide resentment by other Israelis at a time when reservists are serving multiple tours in Gaza and Lebanon.

Eisenkot has proposed requiring national service for all Israelis but allowing citizens to choose a civilian option rather than the military, opening the door to integrating the ultra-Orthodox.

In a message delivered on Friday before Israel shut down for the sabbath, Eisenkot said it was urgent to replace Netanyahu, calling him a threat to the “very existence of Israeli democracy”.

He called for the swift formation of a government, which could initially rely on outside support, with more parties joining eventually.

Following his appointment, Eisenkot will have 28 days to come up with the 61 votes needed for a government. If he comes up short, Herzog can provide a 14-day extension before he has to offer the mandate to someone else.

If neither side succeeds, Israel will head to fresh elections. The country held five elections between 2019 and 2022 due to repeated deadlocks.

sct-glp/dcp

World.title: Trump offers press secretary role to UFC chief Dana White
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was offering a press secretary role to mixed martial arts executive and “violent fighter” Dana White.

“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social account.

“Dana, please take the job!” he said.

While White did not explicitly accept the job, the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss posted a photo — possibly AI-generated — that showed him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned “On to the next chapter.”

The White House has been without a press secretary since October 16 when Katie Zacharia left the position after less than a week on the job.

White, 57, is president and CEO of the UFC, the largest and most successful organization in the world of mixed martial arts. UFC’s violent cage fights are broadcast across the globe.

Trump also listed six UFC fighters that he hoped White would bring to the White House as advisers, “even though some are not from our Country.”

Two of the fighters mentioned are Russian and one is Brazilian.

The White House amplified the announcement by publishing a screenshot of the president’s post on one of its official accounts.

Trump and White are old friends, and Trump has often tried to associate his MAGA brand of politics with the hugely popular UFC.

On his 80th birthday in June, UFC held a bloody cage match on the White House South Lawn. He has also attended bouts in Miami, New York and New Jersey since winning his second White House term.

When Trump won reelection in 2024, White appeared alongside the Republican for his victory speech.

Since Trump’s reelection, White has joined the board of directors of Meta, which many saw as a sign of the tech company’s conservative shift.

World.title: Ukraine says Russia ramps up strikes to pressure Kyiv at talks
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday accused Russia of intensifying strikes across the country to put pressure on Kyiv at upcoming talks after an overnight barrage triggered power cuts as temperatures drop.

The latest strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure came days before the trilateral US-brokered meeting in Abu Dhabi scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday aimed at reviving stalled diplomatic efforts towards peace.

Ukraine’s energy ministry said “a massive attack on a number of energy facilities” had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding region.

Zelensky said the timing of the aerial barrage showed that Russia had a “very particular view of diplomacy” as it struck ahead of “another joint effort with our partners to reinvigorate negotiations”.

“By intensifying its attacks on Ukraine and our infrastructure at this very moment, Russia is trying to additionally lay the groundwork for putting pressure on Ukraine’s position and that of its partners,” Zelensky said.

Moscow has battered Ukraine’s energy grid and infrastructure throughout its four-and-a-half-year invasion and Kyiv was now bracing for another harsh winter as temperatures begin to hover around freezing.

Zelensky also said Russia had throughout the night launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, among which, according to him, were KN-23 missiles manufactured and supplied by North Korea.

They hit “one of the key energy facilities that was damaged”, Zelensky said.

Russia has turned to North Korea for support throughout invasion.

Earlier in the war, Pyongyang dispatched thousands of troops to help Russia fight back a Ukrainian counterattack in its western Kursk region.

The Russian defence ministry in a statement Saturday said it had struck “facilities belonging to the military-industrial complex, the energy sector, and transport infrastructure” in Kyiv and its surrounding region.

– ‘Shortage’ of interceptors –

Zelensky urged the United States to increase its flagging aid to Ukraine.

“Unfortunately, there is still a significant shortage of interceptors for Patriot systems, and the United States is in the best position to help address it,” Zelensky said.

The overnight strikes damaged energy facilities and a key bridge in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said earlier on Saturday, warning that the energy supply situation was “extremely difficult”.

Consumers in the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Kyiv, Zhytomyr and Kharkiv regions were left without power, the energy ministry said.

It did not say how many homes were affected.

On Tuesday and Wednesday, Ukrainian officials are expected to sit down with Russian negotiators and US envoys for the first such direct talks in months.

The diplomatic track has been stalled since February when Washington shifted attention to its war with Iran.

US President Donald Trump’s repeated attempts to broker an end to the war have foundered over Moscow’s sweeping territorial demands, particularly its insistence on controlling all of Ukraine’s eastern Donbas region, including areas still held by Kyiv.

Zelensky has rejected surrendering Ukrainian-held territory, warning that Russia could use it as a springboard for another attack.

Russia, which launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, now occupies roughly one-fifth of Ukrainian territory.

World.title: Rahm and McIlroy primed for Abu Dhabi title battle
World.content:
Abu Dhabi – Jon Rahm will take a one-shot lead into the final round of the Abu Dhabi Championship, with Ryder Cup team-mate Rory McIlroy among the players breathing down his neck.

Rahm broke out of a three-way tie for the overnight lead with a six-under 66 on Saturday, picking up five shots on the back nine, including an eagle at the 11th.

“Fantastic round. Wishing I would have hit a couple better putts in the last two holes, right, just misread those two putts. But overall, obviously very good golf,” said Rahm.

The Spaniard is 18-under overall and a stroke clear of Tyrrell Hatton and Francesco Laporta. They began the third round level with Rahm, who is playing in his first event since leaving the rebel LIV Golf tour last month.

Rahm is targeting his first win outside of LIV since triumphing at the Masters in 2023.

“It would be amazing. It’s been a good year so far. But to win again on the DP World Tour would be special,” said Rahm.

McIlroy sits two shots off the lead at Yas Links after a five-under 67, having surged with four birdies on the front nine before a double-bogey at the 10th and a dropped shot at the 17th slowed his momentum.

“Encouraged, as I played some really good golf out there but also a little rueful,” said McIlroy, who overshot the green on the par-four 10th hole and took a costly six.

He rebounded with four straight birdies but failed to find the green out of the bunker on the par-three 17th and lost ground on Rahm.

“Overall, good day. Kept myself within touching distance and I have a good shot at it tomorrow, which is all I want,” said McIlroy.

“I’m going to have to go out and shoot a low one, something in the mid to low 60s to get it done tomorrow, and that will be the goal.”

McIlroy is bidding for a fifth successive Race to Dubai title and record-equalling eighth in total. He trails Eugenio Chacarra and Patrick Reed in this season’s standings.

Chacarra is 10 shots off the pace in Abu Dhabi, while Reed lies on a distant one-under after three rounds.

World.title: US, UAE, China, Canada and more: Diwali greetings pour in from across the world
World.content:
World leaders and diplomats across the globe extended warm greetings on the occasion of Diwali, wishing people celebrating the Festival of Lights happiness, good health and prosperity.

Indian diplomatic missions and representatives of several countries also marked the festival with community gatherings and cultural celebrations, highlighting the message of light, harmony and togetherness.

UAE president Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Sunday conveyed his Diwali greetings to people celebrating the festival in the United Arab Emirates and across the world. Sharing glimpses of the celebrations on X, Green described the occasion as particularly special as he celebrated the festival for the last time in India in his capacity as high commissioner.





"#Diwali with the high commission family is always special, and even more so as I celebrate my final Diwali in India as high commissioner. A memorable day of warmth, festive cheer & lots of dancing. A few highlights," he wrote.

World.title: 'Engines failing': DKS accuses Centre of 'cover up' amid ethanol blending row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Sunday targeted the Centre over allegations of excessive ethanol blending in petrol, claiming that thousands of vehicles were experiencing problems, including repeated engine failures and reduced mileage.

He said the state government had collected samples from 67 locations and was investigating complaints about ethanol levels exceeding the prescribed limit.

"Engines are stopping repeatedly, and mileage has decreased," Shivakumar said, adding that around 30% of the investigation had been completed. He said the state government had already informed the Centre about the locations and that its findings would be made public.



"We have conducted an investigation first. 30% [of the work] is complete. Tomorrow, our Minister will officially hold a press conference and give all details. The government cannot cover it up," he said, as quoted by news agency ANI.

Shivakumar alleged that excessive ethanol mixing was taking place at petrol pumps rather than during the supply process. "We have checked, and the mixing is happening at the petrol bunks.





Where it is being distributed, mixing is happening there. We have all the documents," he said.

Calling the issue a major concern for the country, the chief minister alleged that cheaper ethanol was being mixed with petrol to increase profits. "Because it is available at a lower price, they are mixing it to make a profit. We condemn this. It is dangerous. People need to be made aware and protected," he added.

The remarks come amid a dispute between the Karnataka government and public sector oil marketing companies over allegations that petrol sold at some outlets in the state contained ethanol levels significantly higher than the prescribed 20% limit.

Karnataka food, civil supplies, consumer affairs and legal metrology minister Rizwan Arshad had earlier said tests on samples collected from seven locations, including Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Ramanagara, Mangaluru and Tumakuru, had recorded ethanol levels as high as 31.2%.

They also questioned the sampling procedure and testing methodology used in the state government's October 2026 exercise, arguing that the findings were based on third-party laboratory certificates that did not follow the prescribed statutory and technical procedures.

NEW DELHI: Punjab Police, with the assistance of central agencies, has secured the deportation of wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi from Ethiopia after a 10-month-long international manhunt under Operation SHAHID.Punjab Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav said on Sunday that the state government had announced a reward of Rs 5 lakh for information leading to the gangster's arrest.Announcing the development in a post on social media platform X, Yadav said the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) Punjab, in coordination with the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC) of Counter Intelligence, Punjab, and central agencies, coordinated the operation to bring Afridi back from Ethiopia."In a major breakthrough, Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) Punjab, in coordination with the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (#OFTEC) of Counter Intelligence, Punjab with the support of central agencies, secures the deportation of Gurwinder alias Afridi, a key kingpin of the Doni Bal-Prabh Dassuwal gang, from Ethiopia following a 10-month-long international manhunt under Operation SHAHID," the DGP said.According to Yadav, preliminary investigations indicate that Afridi was allegedly directing targeted killings, extortion-related firing incidents and other organised criminal activities in Punjab while operating from abroad.The operation involved sustained intelligence gathering, surveillance and tracking across several countries in Asia, South America and Africa, with the support of national and international agencies, he said.Yadav also acknowledged the role of the ministry of external affairs and other central agencies in facilitating the operation."We thank the ministry of external affairs and all other central agencies as part of this international cooperation," he said.The DGP reiterated that Punjab Police remains committed to dismantling gangster networks, curbing organised crime and maintaining peace and security across the state.

NEW DELHI: Contributions received by the Congress in excess of Rs 20,000 totalled Rs 130.7 crore in 2025-26, which is barely one-fourth of its Rs 517.4 crore donation receipts in 2024-25.As per the 2025-26 contribution report of the Congress filed with EC, Prudent Electoral Trust contributed 19% of Congress's total donation kitty in the relevant year. In 2024-25, Prudent had accounted for 41.8% of contributions received by Congress.Prudent is the only electoral trust through which donations, largely corporate, were routed to Congress last year. At Rs 25 crore, the trust's contributions to the party, however, were only 11.5% of the Rs 216 crore funds it had channelled to the party in 2024-25.The steep 75% decline in Congress's total contributions in excess of Rs 20,000, compared with 2024-25, could be due to several factors. Given that 2024-25 was the general election year, a marked rise (84% as compared to 2023-24) in contributions to the main opposition party was on expected lines. What is interesting though is that the Rs 130.7 crore contribution receipts in 2025-26 are nearly 53% less than the amount it had received even in 2023-24.The steep decline was witnessed despite 2025-26 being the year of Bihar assembly elections and the run-up to elections in Assam, Keralam, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry held in April 2026.The Congress audit report for 2025-26, which is not available yet, will throw light on the party's other sources of funding. In 2024-25, Congress's collection from the issuance and sale of coupons was over Rs 350 crore.Among the key contributors last year, other than Prudent, were Star Cement Ltd (Rs 5 crore), Sajjan Bhajanka (Rs 4 crore), Afnan Constructions (Rs 3 crore), Prem Kumar Bhajanka (Rs 2 crore) and IPSUM Proadvisors and SMS Builders (Rs 1 crore each).Just nine contributions of Rs 1 crore or more accounted for Rs 43 crore, or nearly one-third of the party's total receipts. In comparison, 1,321 contributions of Rs 5 lakh or less together added up to Rs 37.2 crore, accounting for just 28.5% of the total. The median contribution among the 1,735 entries was Rs 3 lakh, highlighting how a relatively small number of large donations accounted for a substantial share of the party's funding.
