Maya, an elephant calf found alone as a newborn on a riverbank 18 months ago, was airlifted from Keralam to Vantara's hospital in Jamnagar on Nov 5, after fractures in both front legs left her unable to stand.Acting on an initiative by RIL exec director and Vantara founder Anant Ambani, the organisation deployed a specialised veterinary team following a transfer order from Keralam's chief wildlife warden, P Pugazhendi.Found near Kaprikkad on Apr 19, 2025, the weak, dehydrated newborn had not received her mother's milk and couldn't even suckle. Assistant forest veterinary officer Binoy Babu and caregivers fed and nursed her for over a year.In July 2026, Maya slipped while playing and injured her shoulder. Despite physiotherapy, splints & supplements, her bones became increasingly fragile. By Oct, she had front-leg fractures, a chest infection and pressure sores. Her prognosis was grave.After Kerala's chief wildlife warden sought wider expert opinion, Vantara veterinary adviser Kushal Konwar Sarma identified a possible parathyroid-related disorder that may respond to treatment.Yaduraj Khadpekar, head veterinarian at Vantara's Elephant Care Centre, concurred, and the medical board unanimously agreed.Maya travelled by a life-support airlift, accompanied by three Vantara elephant veterinarians, paravets and caregivers, along with Binoy C Babu and her familiar caregiver, Nikhil Babu. She will receive round-the-clock monitoring, pain management, advanced diagnostics, hydraulic lifting support and hydrotherapy where appropriate. Vantara - a global wildlife rescue, care, welfare and conservation initiative based in Jamnagar - will facilitate her return to Abhayaranyam after treatment.

World.title: An wins Korea Open for 11th badminton title of year
World.content:
Badminton world number one An Se-young said she was "very proud" of her achievements after winning an incredible 11th title of the year at her home Korea Open on Sunday.

Also read | Fighting Sindhu loses to nemesis An Se Young to sign off with runner-up finish

The 24-year-old beat Japan's Akane Yamaguchi 21-12, 15-21, 21-16 in the final in Yeosu to extend an unbeaten run that stretches back to March.

An has been head and shoulders above the rest of the competition this year but she said she still had to be on her guard against world number two Yamaguchi.

"She's a player who can always keep the score close so I tried to keep the intensity up all the way until the end," An told the Badminton World Federation.

"When the match was over, I was very proud of myself.

"It felt a bit different because it's my home tournament."

It was An's 11th straight win over Yamaguchi.

Yamaguchi's most recent win over the world number one came in the final of last year's Korea Open.

"Whenever we play each other, sometimes I win and sometimes she does, so I didn't think too much about last year's result," said An.

"Yamaguchi is a player who brings different styles into every match, so I knew it wouldn't be easy and it wasn't."

Of the titles An did not win this year, she finished runner-up at the All-England Open and pulled out injured from the Japan Open.

She claimed her second world crown in August in New Delhi and became the first woman to win two Asian Games singles titles in Nagoya in September.

"We don't play many matches in Korea so this feels like a dream moment," said An.

"I'm just so proud and happy that so many people in Korea are now supporting badminton."

World.title: Body of Punjab anti-drug activist Jhota brought to Mansa for last rites
World.content:
The mortal remains of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder last month triggered protests and a political row, were brought to his native place here on Sunday for last rites.

Following a post-mortem at PGIMER in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026), Jhota's body was taken to his native place, where last rites would be conducted.

Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13. The store owner, who had fired at Jhota after the activist confronted him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man, was subsequently arrested.

A large number of people turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.

On Saturday (November 7, 2026), a member of the joint action committee had said Jhota's cremation would take place at his native place in Mansa on Sunday.

The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota's murder.

The cremation will be held at Jhota's fields on Chakerian Road in Mansa. Jhota's father, Bhim Singh, on Saturday (November 7, 2026) called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse.

"We will take the body to our residence first and thereafter, between 12 and 1 pm, Jhota will be cremated on Diwali Day," said Singh while speaking to reporters in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Jhota's body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday, after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives.

On Friday (November 6, 2026), Jhota's father said he would go on a fast demanding the immediate transfer of Mansa Senior Superintendent of Police Vaibhav Chaudhary.

Jhota's family, along with the JAC, had been sitting on a protest in Mansa seeking justice for the slain activist. On October 28, two JAC members, Lakhvir Singh and Mohanjit Singh Sheron, were arrested during the protest.

On the evening of November 5, the JAC members were released from Nabha district jail after a meeting between the protesters and government representatives, including Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan and Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian, on November 4.

The murder incident, which took place while Jhota was hosting a Facebook Live session, triggered a political slugfest in Punjab, which goes to polls early next year.

Opposition parties in Punjab had stepped up their attack on the Mann government over the drug issue and law and order after Jhota's murder.

The JAC had been pressing for the resignations of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav.

The Punjab government had earlier handed over the probe into Jhota's death to the CBI following his family's demand. The state government had suspended a station house officer, a deputy superintendent of police and a drug inspector in connection with the case.

The family has been demanding setting up a trauma centre in Jhota's name and compensation for each of the four injured persons in the incident, which were agreed to by the government.

Other demands the government agreed to include installation of Jhota's statue at either a park or a stadium.

World.title: Congress donations fall nearly 75%, sharpest decline in a decade
World.content:
The Congress party's receipts from donations above ₹20,000 plunged nearly 75% to ₹130.69 crore in 2025-26, the steepest annual fall in such contributions in a decade, an analysis of the party's filings with the Election Commission shows.

The party had received ₹517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the commission.

A comparison with the preceding 12 financial years shows that the last steeper fall was in 2015-16, when Congress' disclosed donations dropped roughly 86% from ₹141.46 crore the previous year.

The latest decline follows two years of higher collections. Congress received ₹281.48 crore in disclosed donations in 2023-24, rising to ₹517.39 crore in 2024-25, the year Lok Sabha elections were held.

BJP received ₹6,074.02 crore in donations exceeding ₹20,000 in 2024-25, nearly 12 times Congress's collection. BJP's corresponding figure for 2025-26 is not available as the party's contribution report has not been made public by the ECI yet.

The BJP collected more than the Congress in each of the 12 financial years examined.

Funding through Prudent Electoral Trust accounted for a substantial part of Congress' latest decline. The trust's contribution fell from ₹216.34 crore in 2024-25 to ₹25 crore in 2025-26, a drop of about 88%.

Prudent was the only electoral trust listed in the party's latest contribution report.

Also Read | The murky world of political party finance

Among other large contributors were Star Cement, which gave ₹5 crore, Sajjan Bhajanka, who contributed ₹4 crore, and Prem Kumar Bhajanka, who donated ₹2 crore.

The Congress' 2025-26 fund collection, though sharply lower than the previous year, was not its lowest over the period examined.

Its disclosed donations were lower in several earlier years, including ₹74.52 crore in 2020-21, ₹95.46 crore in 2021-22 and ₹79.92 crore in 2022-23.

These figures exclude electoral bonds, which were reported separately when the scheme operated. Including bond receipts in the earlier years, the Congress' latest collection in 2025-26 was its lowest since 2020-21.

The contribution report does not show the party's total income, which also includes smaller donations, membership fees, coupon collections and interest.

The Congress' audited account for 2025-26, which has not been uploaded yet, is needed to establish its overall financial position. In 2024-25, coupon collections alone brought the party ₹350.12 crore.

World.title: Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Hari Boxer detained in U.S., extradition process underway
World.content:
Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Harichand Jat alias Hari Boxer has been detained in the U.S. by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and efforts are underway to bring him to India, Rajasthan Police said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

The Rajasthan Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) secured the detention through sustained coordination with international agencies, including the CBI and Interpol, police said.

Hari Boxer (40), a resident of Chatarpura village in Kotputli-Behror district of Rajasthan, was allegedly operating criminal activities in India from abroad and played a key role in supplying weapons to the Lawrence Bishnoi-Rohit Godara gang.

He was involved in extortion threats and firing incidents in Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, including Mumbai and Pune, AGTF ADG Dinesh MN said.

The accused allegedly threatened wealthy businessmen through WhatsApp and Signal-based VoIP calls and resorted to firing at individuals or their family members if extortion demands were not met.

He was also wanted in connection with several firing incidents, including the shooting outside Bollywood director Rohit Shetty's Mumbai residence, following which he allegedly claimed responsibility through a social media post.

More than 22 cases, including attempts to murder, extortion, Arms Act violations and organised crime, are registered against him in various police stations in Rajasthan.

Hari Boxer allegedly fled India in April 2023 using his own passport and travelled through Dubai, the Dominican Republic and Guyana before reaching the U.S. through Mexico via an illegal migration route, police said.

A Red Corner Notice was issued against him through Interpol on November 14, 2024, following coordination with the CBI.

AGTF subsequently shared intelligence and technical inputs with international agencies, including nine Interpol notices to the US between December 2024 and July 2026. A provisional arrest request, updated dossier and fingerprints were also forwarded, police said.

The detention followed coordinated efforts by AGTF's operational, Interpol and technical teams.

Further proceedings to bring him to India are underway.

World.title: Nithya Raman | The urban planner
World.content:
After defeating Karen Bass, the incumbent Mayor of the second most populous city of the U.S., Nithya Raman wrote on X, “Los Angeles, I am deeply honored to be your next mayor.” A member of the city council since 2020, Ms. Raman has a track record of civic activism, advocating for affordable and increased housing. Entering the electoral race at the very last minute, she is now L.A.’s the first South Asian Mayor-elect as well as the first candidate to defeat an incumbent Mayor of the city since 2005.

Born in Keralam, Ms. Raman spent a part of her early childhood between Thiruvananthapuram and Thrissur. Her father, Venkataraman, used to work for Keltron, and her mother, Sudha, was a former employee of the Indian Overseas Bank. The family migrated to the U.S. when Ms. Raman was six. She graduated from Harvard University in 2003, and then got a master’s degree in urban planning from MIT. She became a U.S. citizen at 22.

World.title: Jon Ossoff | Ambition without ambition
World.content:
There is something of an investigative journalist in Jon Ossoff, who served as managing director and chief executive officer of Insight: The World Investigates, a London-based investigative television production company. During his Senate campaign as Democratic candidate in Georgia and even before, he had been mounting a blistering campaign against corruption. It resonated with the voters struggling with rising food prices and unaffordable fuel.

Mr. Ossoff won the November 3 election against Republican Mike Collins, becoming the only incumbent Senate Democrat to defend a seat in a State President Donald Trump carried in 2024. Ever since his win in the 2021 Senate race in Georgia, the charismatic Mr. Ossoff has been making the lists of possible candidates for the Democratic ticket in the 2028 Presidential election. But, like Barack Obama before his 2004 Senate win and scores of others before him, Mr. Ossoff, now 39, who in 2021 became the youngest U.S. Senator since 1980, has been vehemently denying any such aspiration. The media, however, has been quick in spotting in him similarities with Mr. Obama, especially the former President’s speech delivery.

World.title: Iran says two tankers caught fire in Hormuz after hitting mines
World.content:
Two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday (November 8, 2026), according to state news agency IRNA.

Also read | Explosions heard in areas in southern Iran, Iranian media report

Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.

The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

"Two oil tankers violating regulations — one in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the strait — caught fire and are currently engulfed in intense flames after striking naval mines while attempting to cross through unauthorised routes," the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said in a statement.

"The two tankers had reportedly committed multiple violations, including switching off their navigation and positioning systems, as they attempted to transit through an unauthorised route," the statement added.

The Guards did not specify the name or nationality of the tankers.

Tehran has made multiple announcements in recent weeks saying that ships have caught fire in the Hormuz strait.

U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.

The IRNA separately reported late on Saturday (November 7) that sounds of explosions were heard in parts of the country.

"Sounds resembling explosions were heard in Qeshm, Sirik, Jask, and Bandar Abbas. The cause of the sounds remains unknown," the news agency wrote on Telegram.

Officials confirmed an "impact" in the port city of Jask, the IRNA said.

U.S. President Donald Trump previously talked up the possibility of resuming heavy strikes on Iran but has since walked back from the idea.

Nevertheless, the U.S. military has conducted occasional limited strikes.

World.title: Kremlin hopes U.S. election shake-up won't shift Trump's negotiations on Ukraine
World.content:
The Republicans' defeat in the U.S. midterm elections was watched closely in Russia, where some observers are predicting it could herald more support for Ukraine when the Democrats take over Congress in January.

But if the Kremlin is hearing the ticking of a clock on its nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion of its neighbour, it seemingly remains unperturbed.

Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that U.S. President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

“There is groundwork already in place, and another round of trilateral negotiations is set to take place very soon,” Mr. Peskov said of talks planned for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11) involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. representatives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

He also praised the “successful humanitarian peace-building efforts” by first lady Melania Trump, adding that “we hope that all of this will continue.”

Last week's limited ceasefire around the Russia-occupied city of Oleshky, brokered with her help, allowed for the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of some residents.

Mr. Peskov shrugged off a question from reporters on whether the new Congress would challenge Mr. Trump's stance on Russia and Ukraine. He called it an “internal matter” for the U.S.

Trump's recent moves have appeared to favour Moscow

Trump’s recent moves appear to favour Moscow

In recent months, Mr. Trump's actions appeared to favour Moscow

Last month, he struck a diesel fuel import deal with Russia in a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on the Kremlin, to the dismay of Ukraine and its European allies. He also claimed that Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil refineries caused a spike in diesel prices in the U.S. He urged Kyiv to halt the strikes, even though rising global energy prices were largely driven by the Iran war.

Mr. Trump also issued an executive order to put on hold sweeping new sanctions that clamped down on the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause was in the national interest. Lawmakers from both parties blasted Mr. Trump's move as benefiting Russian President Vladimir Putin.

At the same time, Ukraine reported a throttling of Starshield, the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX. Mr. Trump denied being behind the brief slowing of Starshield, but the move to limit the system that serves as the backbone of Ukraine's drone operations and battlefield communications was widely seen as part of Washington's efforts to pressure Kyiv.

The diesel deal appeared to falter this week after U.S. federal and state officials warned that handling any shipments could bring legal consequences, and two U.S.-bound tankers changed course. The Kremlin sought to play down the development, saying deliveries will continue.

Kyiv desperately needs to replenish its supplies of U.S.-made Patriot interceptors to fend off Russia's ballistic missile attacks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made repeated requests for Washington to speed up delivery of the defensive systems, but U.S. stockpiles have been exhausted by the Iran war, and the U.S. has prioritised replenishing its own arsenals.

On October 30, the Trump administration said it has approved a proposed $2.1 billion sale of Patriot interceptors for Ukraine after Kyiv had accused the Pentagon of delaying delivery.

Mr. Trump also appeared to echo the Kremlin's view that Mr. Zelenskyy was an obstacle to peace while saying Mr. Putin was more open to a deal.

Mr. Trump on Thursday (November 5) conferred with Mr. Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who attended a White House ceremony with the first lady recognising last week's humanitarian truce. The President didn't meet any of the Ukrainian officials also at the event but hinted that some kind of grand deal about European security was in the works.

Many in Russia argue that the Democrats' victory could put congressional pressure on Mr. Trump to tread more carefully and toughen his stand on Russia.

Dmitry Medvedev, who served as Russian President in 2008-12, predicted that Mr. Trump would be less inclined to press Ukraine when a new Congress is seated.

"He doesn't need an extra confrontation with Democrats,” said Mr. Medvedev, who now serves as deputy head of Russia's Security Council.

New House and Senate could boost aid to Ukraine

There has been strong bipartisan support for Ukraine, raising the prospect of veto-proof passage of more aid to Kyiv or tough new sanctions on Moscow.

On Wednesday (November 4), Mr. Zelenskyy told German broadcaster ZDF that while there has been backing for Kyiv from both parties, the Democrats “speak very clearly about supporting Ukraine."

In other remarks on Thursday (November 5), the Ukrainian leader also noted the midterm elections could have a positive effect on U.S. assistance, including speedier delivery of the Patriot interceptors. “I believe our chances of getting additional assistance from the United States may now grow,” he said.

Abbas Gallyamov, a former Putin speechwriter-turned-political analyst who lives abroad, argued that his old boss had missed a chance of striking a deal on Ukraine before the Democrats won and now could face a less cooperative Washington.

“Putin's prospects have significantly worsened,” Mr. Gallyamov wrote in a commentary. “He thought that the time was on his side and wasn't in a hurry to use the window of opportunity that had opened after Trump's victory, and now this window is starting to close.”

Some policy experts, however, cautioned against expectations of a dramatic shift.

The Democrats could put more funding for Ukraine on the agenda and increase pressure on Mr. Trump over the diesel deal or Russia sanctions waivers, but hard limits on the President's power are unlikely, said Jorn Fleck, senior director of the Atlantic Council's Europe Center.

“Even with a strong majority in both chambers of Congress, Democrats will struggle to impose meaningful limits on Trump's conduct of foreign policy, given his constitutional powers and willingness to push the envelope,” Mr. Fleck said in a commentary.

“Unshackled from having to face voters at the ballot box again, Trump may shift into deal-making overdrive to cement his legacy.”

Some expect a more hard-lined Trump

Konstantin Kosachev, a Deputy Speaker of the upper house of the Russian parliament, argued that Mr. Trump's executive powers in the foreign policy sphere would allow him to pursue his course regardless of congressional opposition.

He said if authorities in Kyiv believed that the Republicans' defeat would make the Trump administration more receptive to Ukraine's requests, they could be mistaken.

“They will not find a more pliable or constrained Trump," Mr. Kosachev said. “Rather, they will face a more resolute one, who is no longer looking over his shoulder at upcoming elections.”

For all the importance of Congress, "the U.S. President's role in foreign policy remains paramount — a fact Trump understands better than anyone else,” he said.

Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna struck a similar tone in an interview on Thursday (November 5) with The Associated Press, saying "the President is President Trump,” and he has the ability to dictate foreign and security policy. “Unpredictability” should be expected, he added.

Mr. Kosachev said that by pinning their hopes on a victory by the Democrats, Kyiv and its allies in London, Brussels and other capitals in Europe have sided with Mr. Trump's domestic political adversaries.

"Consequently, they are all but guaranteed two years of a hard-line Trump,” he said.

World.title: President Zardari, PM Shehbaz wish Hindu community on Diwali, reaffirm commitment to minority rights
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday extended greetings to the Hindu community in Pakistan and worldwide on the occasion of Diwali, reaffirming their commitment to minority rights.

Diwali is a Hindu festival involving lighting candles, worship, celebrations and prayers. It is celebrated to mark the day when Hindu deity Lord Rama returned home after his 14-year exile. It is a five-day festival and during this time, houses are cleaned and windows are opened to welcome Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth.

PM Shehbaz calls for interfaith harmony

In his message on the occasion, PM Shehbaz said, “The festival of lights conveys a profound message of promoting peaceful coexistence in human relations and social life.

“The enduring belief in a bright, prosperous and hopeful future is one of the most cherished attributes of Diwali.”

He described the Hindu community as “a valued and integral part of our national fabric”.

“The diverse cultural and religious traditions within our society constitute a valuable social asset. Pakistan takes immense pride in its religious and cultural diversity,” he added.

The premier reiterated the government’s commitment to protecting the religious and civil rights of minorities, as guaranteed by the Constitution of Pakistan.

“The Constitution of Pakistan guarantees the protection of the religious and civil rights of minorities. The government remains firmly committed to safeguarding the rights, dignity and religious freedoms of all citizens, irrespective of religion, faith, colour or ethnicity. Promoting religious harmony, mutual unity and respect is our shared responsibility,” he said.

The premier added: “A society that embraces diverse cultures and traditions and upholds the principles of peaceful coexistence is one that ensures equal educational and economic opportunities for all its citizens.”

He called on the nation to foster interfaith harmony, strengthen bonds of fraternity and brotherhood and work together towards a future founded on peace, tolerance and mutual understanding.

’Pakistan belongs equally to all its citizens’

In his message, President Zardari said, “The festival of lights celebrates the symbolism of triumph of good over evil, light over darkness and hope over despair. Its message of compassion and renewal reminds us that each of us can bring light into the lives of others through kindness, understanding, compassion and care.”

He added that Pakistan’s Hindu community is “an integral part of our national life”, highlighting its contributions to education, healthcare, business, public service, social welfare, arts and culture.

He reaffirmed that “Pakistan belongs equally to all its citizens”.

The president added that “Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah envisioned a country where faith, caste or creed would be no barrier to equal citizenship and equal rights”.

“We must honour that vision by ensuring that every citizen can practice their faith freely, live in dignity and enjoy equal protection under the law. For me, Quaid-i-Azam’s promise of equal citizenship is a sacred national commitment.”

He added, “No Pakistani should ever have to prove their belonging because of their faith. This country is their home, its freedoms are their right, and its future is theirs to shape.”

He called on the nation to reject prejudice and discrimination by sharing in each other’s celebrations.

“Our diversity is not our weakness but a great strength.

“It should be clear to all of us that protecting the rights of religious minorities is our shared responsibility.”

World.title: PHC removes pleas against emergency, detentions from cause lists
World.content:
PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court on Saturday removed around 105 petitions from its Nov 10 cause lists, including those challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province as well as the alleged illegal detention of dysfunctional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and several other PTI lawmakers, leaders and workers.

The move comes a day after the high court’s administrative committee, acting in compliance with a restraining order issued by the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), decided not to proceed with petitions filed under Article 199 of the Constitution on or after Oct 12.

The FCC had also decided not to entertain fresh petitions and to return them to the petitioners, directing them to approach the “appropriate” forum.

On Nov 5, a two-member FCC bench declared: “Since the armed forces have been called to act in aid of civil power in the entire province of KP pursuant to the Oct 11 order… the proceedings before the PHC instituted under Article 199 on or after Oct 12 shall, in terms of Clause 4 of Article 245, remain suspended.”

Step taken in light of Constitutional Court’s restraining order

It also directed KP advocate general Sanaullah Khan to produce within seven days a report, identifying areas in the province where the armed forces are no longer required to act in aid of civil power.

The FCC declared that it might consider modifying its order under Article 245 of the Constitution, which provides for the deployment of armed forces in aid of civil power, after examining the report.

The FCC order has affected several high-profile cases, as well as routine matters falling under Article 199 of the Constitution.

The most significant of the deleted petitions were those challenging the imposition of emergency in KP under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution.

These petitions were filed by PTI chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, leaders of Tehreek Tahafuz-i-Aeen Pakistan and the National Democratic Movement, the KP Bar Council and others.

During the previous hearing on Oct 20, a two-member bench sought comments on the petitions from the respondents, including the federal government, within a fortnight and fixed Nov 10 for the next hearing.

Similarly, petitions challenging the alleged illegal detention or abduction of Sohail Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar, scores of lawmakers, and other PTI leaders and workers were also deleted.

In these petitions, the court had initially issued notices on Oct 20 to the KP chief secretary, home secretary, inspector general of police (IGP) and Peshawar Capital City Police Officer, directing them to submit a detailed report within 10 days regarding the whereabouts of the chief minister and clarify whether he had been arrested or was implicated in any criminal case.

However, the respondents failed to submit the report within the stipulated time. Consequently, on Nov 3, a bench referred the matter to the chief justice, suggesting the constitution of a larger bench to hear it.

Several petitions challenging detentions under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, which had also been fixed for Nov 10, were deleted from the cause list.

The deleted petitions also included one filed by KP Assembly Deputy Speaker Suriya Bibi, challenging the government’s sealing of her official residence.

In that petition, the court had earlier granted her interim relief, ordering the de-sealing of her residence and allowing her to stay there. However, the government did not comply with the order, prompting the court on Nov 5 to seek an explanation as to why it had not yet been implemented.

Similarly, multiple petitions filed by aggrieved property owners against the government’s anti-encroachment operations in different areas were also de-listed.

Moreover, several petitions pertaining to “missing persons” and those filed by Afghan nationals seeking relief in the government’s ongoing repatriation drive were also removed from the cause list.

The Interior Ministry issued an order on Oct 11 under Article 245 of the Constitution, authorising the deployment of Pakistan Army troops in aid of civil power in KP for the duration of the proclamation issued under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution.

Meanwhile, the Insaf Lawyers Forum (ILF) has said that no judicial or administrative order should become a means of violating citizens’ fundamental rights and constitutional protections.

It termed the “limiting” of the fundamental rights of 45 million people in KP through a court order a serious blow to the supremacy of the Constitution, independence of the judiciary and the right to justice.

In a statement, ILF central information secretary Masooma Mir noted that Article 199 of the Constitution provided citizens with a constitutional avenue to approach the high court, while Articles 9, 10-A and 25 guaranteed fundamental rights, including the right to life, fair trial and equality.

She added that protecting those rights was the fundamental responsibility of the state and the judiciary.

Ms Mir said courts existed to protect citizens’ constitutional rights, not to restrict their access to justice.

She urged the Pakistan Bar Council, KP Bar Council, Supreme Court Bar Association and other lawyer bodies to play an active role in the current constitutional crisis to safeguard the rights of the people of the province.

Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

World.title: Ruling coalition inches ahead on electoral reforms
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The ruling coalition partners have formally submitted the names of their nominees for the proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, while nominations from opposition parties are still awaited.

Talking to Dawn, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry confirmed that he had received the names from coalition parties, including the PPP.

Declining to disclose the names, the minister said the committee would comprise 30 members from the National Assembly and the Senate, with parties receiving representation proportionate to their strength in the two houses of parliament.

Under the formula, he said, the PPP would have seven members on the committee, while the PML-N would be allocated 10 seats. However, he added: “The PML-N may have to sacrifice some of its members to accommodate smaller parties.”

Opposition yet to submit nominees for parliamentary panel on reforms as PTI doubts govt intent

The minister said he had requested the chief whip of the main opposition party, PTI, Aamir Dogar, to provide a list of the party’s nominees for the committee, but Mr Dogar had sought some time. The other opposition party, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), had also not submitted the names of its proposed members, he said.

The PTI had objected to the composition of the committee, he said, adding that he had informed the party that all previous parliamentary committees had been constituted on a proportional basis.

The minister expressed hope that the PTI would announce its decision next week.

Interestingly, Dr Chaudhry said his own party, the ruling PML-N, had shortlisted names for the committee, but these would be submitted to the National Assembly Secretariat only after final approval from the party leadership.

Replying to a question, Dr Chaudhry said that if opposition parties decided to boycott the committee, the leadership of the ruling coalition parties would make a final decision on the matter.

In a recent post on X, Dr Chaudhry had said that the allocation of seats in the Senate for the committee would give two seats each to the PML-N, PPP and PTI. The Awami National Party (ANP), Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), National Party and JUI-F would each be allocated one seat, he had stated.

“The final decision on the names of committee members will be made by the leader of the house [the prime minister] and the deputy prime minister after consultations with the opposition, coalition partners and relevant parliamentary leaders,” Dr Chaudhry said.

Earlier this week, the government, taking ownership of an initiative to bring all parliamentary parties, including the opposition, to the negotiating table on electoral reforms, had formally approached its allies to join the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER).

PTI serious about reforms

When contacted, PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said the party was serious about electoral reforms but had doubts that the government wanted to ensure PTI’s representation on the committee merely to legitimise the process.

“The government wants to have five opposition members on the committee. With five members, we will not be able to implement our proposals,” he explained.

Replying to a question, Sheikh Waqas said the matter would first have to be discussed in the party’s political committee and then in its parliamentary and core committees.

“We held meetings of both committees a few days ago, but due to Imran Khan’s health issues, it was decided to limit their agenda to one point — the health of Imran Khan,” he said.

He said the PTI was very clear about its position on electoral reforms and wanted electronic voting machines and a mechanism to ensure that no one could rig elections.

“It was the PTI that introduced electronic voting machines and tried them in Pakistan,” he said.

Asked how many days the PTI would take to decide whether to become part of the electoral reforms committee, Mr Waqas said meetings of the parliamentary and core committees would be held within two to three days to make a decision.

“However, I want to make it clear that the PTI wants electoral reforms and will become part of any sincere effort to ensure that true representatives of the masses run the country,” he said.

Talking to Dawn, JUI-F spokesperson Aslam Ghouri said the party had not yet made any decision regarding the PCER.

He expressed hope that the matter would soon be discussed by the party’s executive committee.

Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

World.title: Usman Khawaja denies throwing 'anyone under the bus' with comments about Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal
World.content:
Usman Khawaja insisted on Sunday he did not “throw anyone under the bus” by claiming the entire Australian team was in on the 2018 “Sandpapergate” plot and defended taking eight years to go public.

The retired batsman re-ignited the infamous ball-tampering scandal in Cape Town on Saturday ahead of the release of his autobiography this week, where a chapter is dedicated to the issue.

He alleged that it was not just Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft — who were all subsequently banned— who were responsible.

“It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us,” he said.

Khawaja claimed Australia also employed the tactic during the previous Test at Port Elizabeth.

In response Darren Lehmann, who was head coach at the time, denied there was widespread knowledge of the plot while Cricket Australia said it was “comfortable” with the findings of its original investigation.

That probe found only Smith, Warner and Bancroft were in the know.

“When I mentioned it was all of us, that’s implying that whether we like it or not, we’re all responsible for what happened together as a team,” Khawaja said in a lengthy Instagram post on Sunday.

“We need to take that collectively. That is all.” He added: “I haven’t thrown anyone under the bus.

“The guys that are currently in the team right now and the other people that were there on the South African tour, including me, we’re not the victims.

“These three guys (Smith, Warner and Bancroft) took the blame for all of us.

“They’re the victims … people telling them that they’re cheats, getting nailed by the crowd. Public humiliation.”

Khawaja, who retired this year after 88 Tests, defended waiting so long to make the claims, denying it was a marketing ploy to sell his book.

He said he wanted to go public in 2018 once Smith, Warner and Bancroft were suspended.

“But Smudge (Smith) being the man and leader he was, he talked me out of it.

“He wanted to take the blame. I argued with him, but he was having none of it. That’s the first time I tried to come out.”

Khawaja said he again almost spoke up in 2021 when bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly that they knew about the ball-tampering.

But after extensive talks with then-coach Justin Langer he decided not to.

The 39-year-old said he never felt comfortable talking after that while back in the Australian team from 2022.

“Call me a chicken or whatever you want. I didn’t know how to do it because I was still in the team,” Khawaja said. “I was always conscious of putting my team first, but I’m not in that team anymore.”

World.title: Trump orders US Justice Department to look into Democrats for 'threatening' people with impeachment, other penalties
World.content:
President Donald Trump ordered the US Justice Department on Saturday to look into Democrats for “threatening a lot of people” with impeachment and other ​forms of punishment, saying in a social media post that their actions amount ‌to a “criminal act”, without providing evidence.

Democratic candidates routed Trump’s Republicans in midterm elections on Tuesday, giving them control of Congress starting in January. Party leaders have promised to reassert Congress’ oversight of the executive branch once ​they are in power by holding hearings and conducting investigations into Trump administration actions.

In ​his post, Trump accused Democrats of sending “threatening letters to many people, all innocent”.

Members ⁠of Congress have released copies of letters seeking documents on matters such as tech company donations ​for the large ballroom Trump is building at the White House.

Trump’s post also referred to Democratic ​Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, who suggested in remarks last month at the University of Chicago that Congress should investigate people who have enabled Trump’s policies.

“I want young people coming out of school to say, ‘Should I ​go work for the Trump administration?’… I want them to be like, ‘Lord, that might be ​buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want. And so I might avoid participating in that,’” Slotkin said. “I ⁠want that deterrence message sent.”

Her comments, within weeks of the midterm elections, were criticised by some Republicans. Republican Senator Mike Lee of Utah wrote on social media that Slotkin was threatening young people who wanted to go into politics. Slotkin responded that Lee had lied about her comments ​and wrote, “Spare us the ​manufactured outrage”.

Trump’s Justice Department ⁠has investigated Slotkin before. A former CIA analyst, she was among a group of Democratic lawmakers with national security backgrounds whom the department investigated ​after they posted a video urging service members and intelligence officials to ​disobey illegal ⁠orders from the administration.

A grand jury rejected the attempt to indict them.

Slotkin said in a social media post on Saturday that the issue should not be controversial. “If you break the law or use ⁠taxpayer dollars ​to enrich yourself, you should be held accountable. If ​you didn’t break the law, then it’s all good,” she said.

The Justice Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

World.title: Siblings acquitted in blasphemy case after 20 years
World.content:
• SC sets aside death sentences upheld by LHC

• Observes findings on mental illness raise doubts about culpability

ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Saturday acquitted two brothers in a blasphemy case under Section 295-C of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), setting aside their death sentences earlier upheld by the Lahore High Court (LHC) over a decade ago.

A three-judge SC bench, headed by Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi and comprising Justices Shakeel Ahmad and Ishtiaq Ibrahim, took up criminal appeals against the Sept 17, 2015 decision of the LHC.

The brothers, Liaqat Ali and Umar Draz, have spent around 20 years behind bars. They were convicted by a sessions judge in Jhang on March 27, 2006. The trial court sentenced both brothers to death and imposed a fine of Rs500,000 each, with five years’ rigorous imprisonment in default. The high court dismissed their appeals and upheld the convictions.

The main SC judgement was authored by Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim. Justice Shakeel Ahmad concurred with the order but also annexed an additional note.

According to the complaint, Umar Draz had begun making explicit blasphemous statements, leading to a marital dispute between him and his wife that culminated in divorce on March 13, 2006. Draz explicitly affirmed in writing his conversion from Islam in the divorce papers.

During the return of his former wife’s dowry articles, a written document auth­ored by co-appellant Liaqat Ali was recovered. It also contained blasphemous assertions.

On March 18, 2006, when the complainant and witnesses confronted the brothers over the alleged blasphemous material, both appellants acknowledged and verified the contents of the documents and unequivocally declared their willingness to reiterate their assertions before any forum.

Before the SC, their counsel confined his submissions to the plea of mental unsoundness, arguing that the appellants lacked the requisite mens rea (guilty mind) at the time of the alleged offence.

The SC examined three psychiatric assessments. An initial three-member medical board at DHQ Hospital, Faisalabad, found both appellants mentally sound in 2007. However, an eight-member Board of Certification diagnosed them with “bipolar affective disorder with psychotic symptoms” in 2023.

A nine-member Board of Certification in September 2025 concluded that both brothers were suffering from “bipolar disorder current episode manic”. It described the condition as a chronic illness that was most likely permanent in acute cases, with absent insight and an inability to understand their acts at the time.

The SC observed that the unanimous opinions of specialised boards comprising senior professors of psychiatry carried greater weight than the earlier assessm­ent by a board with only one psychiatrist.

It also noted that bipolar disorder was episodic and had a genetic component, and that both brothers had been independently diagnosed with the same condition.

“The appellants have spent around 20 years behind bars. In the light of the opinion of medical board which raises doubts regarding the culpability of the appellants, the benefit of doubt cannot be withheld from the appellants,” the judgement said.

While acquitting the appellants, the SC also expected the executive director of the Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore, to ensure that their medical treatment was not discontinued.

Additional note

In his concurring note, Justice Ahmad agreed with the acquittal but cautioned that a psychiatric diagnosis alone did not satisfy the requirements of Section 84 of the PPC. The judge distinguished medical insanity from legal insanity, noting that the key question was whether, at the time of the offence, the accused was incapable of knowing the nature of the act or that it was wrong or contrary to law.

He argued that legal accountability had to be balanced with humanity, explaining that true justice also included mercy when the law recognised a person’s lack of mental capacity.

The note said the medical reports, along with the surrounding circumstances, created reasonable doubt. It also referred to Islamic principles of legal capacity and responsibility.

Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

World.title: Woman alleges harassment by ex-husband on court premises
World.content:
LAHORE: A British Pakistani woman pursuing maintenance litigation against her former husband for their three daughters has alleged harassment and intimidation by him on the court’s premises.

In her application submitted to the Islampura police, the complainant, Laleen, alleged that she had visited the sessions court for a hearing against her ex-husband, a businessman.

She had obtained a Khula (judicial divorce) from him seven years earlier and a guardian court had decided the matter of the daughters’ custody in her favour, which attained finality.

The woman alleged that upon exiting the courtroom, she was confronted by her former husband alongside unidentified individuals.

She claimed the men harassed her, hurled verbal abuse and continued issuing threats even in the judge’s chamber.

LHC dismisses plea challenging guardian court’s decision on maintenance allowance for three daughters

According to the complaint filed on Oct 23, the former husband repeatedly demanded custody of their daughters, issued death threats, and physically shoved her.

The complainant further alleged that the suspects prevented her from dialling the police helpline (15) or immediately reaching the police station, subjecting her to severe mental distress before she managed to escape.

Despite providing video evidence, she alleged, the police were reluctant to register a case.

However, the inquiry officer concerned at Islampura Police Station told Dawn that the matter had been investigated but no cognisable offence was made out.

Laleen has appealed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, urging her to intervene and ensure justice.

“I have been cleared in numerous malicious cases,” she said.

“Given CM Maryam Nawaz’s work for women and children, I request her support in the matter,” the woman stated.

She also seeks removal of her youngest daughter’s name from the Exit Control List.

A family court had awarded each daughter Rs100,000 per month in maintenance from January 2017, along with educational expenses and a 10pc annual increase.

The father had challenged the decree, arguing that the maintenance amount was excessive and beyond his means.

However, the Lahore High Court (LHC) upheld the decision, dismissing his appeal and ruling that a father cannot evade his financial obligations by concealing his assets and income.

The court noted that the educational expenses reflected the standard of living the children had enjoyed before the marital dispute and that a father could not reduce that standard merely because the children were now residing with their mother.

It held that the maintenance must correspond to the children’s needs, social background, educational requirements and the father’s financial standing.

However, the children have yet to receive maintenance, since the execution proceedings are still pending.

In a recent judgement, the LHC underscored the systemic issue of delays in execution of decrees, observing that prolonged enforcement proceedings defeat the very purpose of adjudication and reduce court judgements to “mere paper declarations.”

The court noted that although cases are decided within the statutory timelines, the real hardship for litigants often begins at the execution stage.

Published in Dawn, November 8th, 2026

World.title: BISE postpones papers in Jhelum over Punjab CM Maryam's visit
World.content:
RAWALPINDI: The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Rawalpindi has postponed the Computer Science papers of the Intermediate Second Annual Examinations 2026 scheduled for November 10 (Tuesday), fixing November 30 as the new date.

On the recommendation of the Jhelum deputy commissioner, the BISE Rawalpindi rescheduled the papers in view of the expected visit of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to Jhelum and Pind Dadan Khan on November 10.

According to a letter addressed to the BISE Rawalpindi chairman, the deputy commissioner recommended postponing the computer science papers in Jhelum district.

The letter available with Dawn stated that the Punjab chief minister was expected to visit Jhelum district on November 10, for which extensive administrative, security and protocol arrangements were being made by the district administration.

“In this regard, due to the consequent deployment of administrative and security personnel, it is not feasible to ensure the smooth and uninterrupted conduct of the said examination in the district. It is, therefore, requested that the examination be postponed and rescheduled for another suitable date to avoid any inconvenience to students and ensure the smooth conduct of both the examination and the VVIP visit,” the letter stated.

Acting on the request, the BISE Rawalpindi rescheduled the computer science papers for both morning and evening groups. According to BISE spokesman Arslan Cheema, Mubashir Saeed, Controller of Examinations at the board, issued a notification announcing the revised schedule.

He said the computer science papers of the Intermediate Second Annual Examination 2026, scheduled for Tuesday, November 10, had been postponed in Jhelum district following the recommendation of the deputy commissioner in view of administrative arrangements in the district.

Mubashir Saeed clarified that the papers would be held as originally scheduled at all examination centres in other districts falling under the jurisdiction of the Rawalpindi board. The new date for the postponed Computer Science papers in Jhelum district has been fixed for Monday, November 30, 2026.

On that day, the computer science paper for the morning group will be held during the morning session, while the corresponding paper for the evening group will take place during the evening session at the previously assigned examination centres.

According to the controller of examinations, new roll number slips will be issued for the convenience of students. However, previously issued roll number slips will also remain valid.
