World.title: China Clears New Formula for Patients Who Must Limit Protein
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019209/China Clears New Formula for Patients Who Must Limit Protein
World.content:
China has approved its first domestically developed amino acid-based nutritional powder, designed to give patients with phenylketonuria (PKU) — a rare genetic disorder that affects metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine — greater freedom in what they eat. Treatment of PKU requires lifelong dietary restrictions to prevent developmental disorders and brain damage.

The new formula officially entered the Chinese market on Oct. 30 and was jointly developed by Shanghai-based Xinhua Hospital, affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, the Shanghai Institute of Pediatric Research, and dairy producer Bright Dairy.

PKU affects about one in every 11,000 newborns in China, with an estimated 120,000 to 150,000 registered patients nationwide.

Due to a genetic defect, people with PKU cannot break down phenylalanine, an amino acid found in protein-rich foods. The resulting buildup can damage brain cells, requiring patients to follow a low-phenylalanine diet by cutting out meat and eating low-protein grains, while relying on milk powder-like formulas to supplement the other amino acids they need.

Earlier formulas contained 30% to 60% amino acids, with the rest composed of fats, carbohydrates, and other nutrients.

“As patients grow older, they need more protein. That means consuming more of these formulas, which also means taking in more fats and carbohydrates, increasing the risk of obesity,” Cai Wei, director of the Shanghai Institute of Pediatric Research and leader of the research team, told domestic media.

In contrast, the new formula contains 95% amino acids, allowing patients to meet their amino acid needs without consuming as much fat or as many carbohydrates, and giving them more freedom to enjoy other normal low-protein foods.

Zhuang Yingying, a 33-year-old PKU patient, told domestic media that patients previously relied heavily on imported products, and overseas supply disruptions were common. Special low-protein foods such as rice and noodles cost five to 10 times as much as regular varieties.

The formula, designed for PKU patients aged 1 and older, could save some families more than 1,000 yuan ($140) a month, according to domestic media.

Domestic PKU formulas have existed for decades, but long faced hurdles in gaining regulatory approval in China, partly because of gaps in national standards for food-grade amino acids, according to a 2020 report by domestic media outlet China Times. High registration costs and the small patient population have also discouraged manufacturers from entering the market.

China approved its first PKU medical formula in 2018, an imported product, while the first domestically produced formula received regulatory approval in 2025.

Since 2018, some parts of China, including Shanghai and neighboring Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces, have introduced public health insurance coverage for foods formulated for PKU patients. In Shanghai, annual coverage ranges from 8,000 yuan for infants under 1 to 12,000 yuan for patients over 10.

Development of the new formula began in 2024 and received regulatory approval in September 2026. The research team has also worked with companies to develop everyday foods for PKU patients, including noodles, steamed buns, cookies, and mochi.

Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: From the Shanghai Morning Post)

World.title: Pedro Taduran retains world crown by clear unanimous decision
World.content:
STILL THE CHAMP. Filipino boxing champion Pedro Taduran celebrates his successful title defense against Brandon Moreno of Spain.

Pedro Taduran, the pride of Libon, Albay, still stands as the Philippines' sole world boxing champion after a decisive win over Brandon Moreno of Spain

MANILA, Philippines – There was no knockdown, only a convincing unanimous decision for Pedro Taduran.

Applying relentless pressure, Taduran trounced Brandon Moreno of Spain by scores of 120-108, 115-113, and 115-113 to retain the IBF (International Boxing Federation) minimumweight crown and remain the lone Filipino world champion on Saturday, November 7 (Sunday, November 8, Philippine time) at the Kiva Auditorium in Albuquerque, New Mexico, USA.

The heavy-hitting Taduran said he didn’t find the opening to put Moreno down and settled for outworking and wearing down the erstwhile unbeaten challenger.

“It was a bit hard (to knock him down) as he throws punches before I could come in. I made my move when I felt that he was losing steam,” Taduran told Rappler in Filipino.

Living up to his favorite tag, Taduran improved to a 21-win, with 14 knockouts, 4-loss, 1-draw record, while handing the Spaniard his first loss after 16 wins with 5 knockouts.

Although two inches shorter at 5-foot-3, Taduran was the aggressor from the start, with Moreno keeping him at bay with jabs.

Once Taduran found his rhythm and unloaded punches in bunches, however, Moreno began to open up and get hit.

Joven Jimenez manned Taduran’s corner with his ward, former IBF junior bantamweight king Jerwin Ancajas.

According to Jimenez, they had to compress everything in two weeks as Taduran was overweight (126 pounds) and undertrained when he started working out at the Knuckleheads Boxing Gym in Las Vegas, Nevada.

Taduran, the pride of Libon, Albay, said he will head to Las Vegas on Sunday and will return to the Philippines by Tuesday, adding that MP Promotions president and matchmaker Sean Gibbons will work out his next fight.

Marty Elorde, Taduran’s manager, said the verdict was expected, but the close scores given by two judges contrasted sharply with the shutout given by one. – Rappler.com

World.title: Trump offers White House press secretary job to UFC CEO Dana White
World.content:
WHITE HOUSE. File photos shows US President Donald Trump listens to UFC CEO Dana White during UFC Freedom 250 on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S. on June 15, 2026.

UFC CEO Dana White says he will be traveling to Washington DC to meet with US President Donald Trump but gave no further details

President Donald Trump offered the White House press secretary position to UFC CEO Dana White, his longtime friend and supporter, in a social media post on Saturday, November 7.

White, 57, said Saturday in London that he will be traveling to Washington, DC, to meet with Trump but gave no further details.

“I’ve got a lot of jobs already,” White said at the post-fight news conference for Saturday’s Zuffa Boxing 12 event. “We have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that.”

White also posted an image of himself at the White House press briefing podium on his Instagram story with the comment, “On to the next chapter.”

CNN reported before White’s press conference that he would decline the president’s offer.

Trump was at his golf club in Florida on Saturday when he posted his offer for the position, which has been vacant since Katie Zacharia was removed in October after only five days on the job.

“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

“I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris,” Trump added, referring to UFC bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison. “We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job! President DONALD J. TRUMP”

Karoline Leavitt was press secretary until leaving the role in August after the birth of her second child.

Trump has been a regular attendee of UFC events, including bringing a fight card to the White House’s South Lawn in June. UFC Freedom 250 celebrated the country’s 250th anniversary as well as Trump’s 80th birthday.

Trump has worked with White since the Trump Taj Mahal casino hosted a UFC event in 2001. White has spoken in support of Trump, including speeches at the Republican National Convention in 2016, 2020 and 2024. – Rappler.com

World.title: Strawberry cansi? Art meets food at Mt. Camisong for Ibagiw 2026
World.content:
TWIST. Chef Suva gives the familiar cansi a Benguet twist with strawberries, adding sweetness to the soupu2019s characteristic tang.

For Ibagiw 2026, chef Stanley Suva and artist Amparo Moldero-Magallanes bring together food, memory, and Cordillera creativity in a collaboration that gives familiar ingredients and old materials new life

BENGUET, Philippines — It began with a painting of a paper boat caught in a fishing net, surrounded by fish and swirling waves. Chef Stanley “Stan” Suva saw it and he immediately remembered a kilawin dish he had created years earlier.

Artist Amparo Moldero-Magallanes had not painted Of Dreams Cast at Sea with Suva’s dish in mind. But the resemblance was striking enough that he pulled out his phone to show her.

It was one of the happy coincidences that made their collaboration for the ninth Ibagiw Creative Festival feel special.

At Alapaap Dining in Mt. Camisong Forest Park, art has returned to the dinner table for another year of Gastro X Art, pairing chefs and visual artists to explore the relationship between food and creative expression.

This year, Suva, Mt. Camisong’s vice president for food and beverage, is paired with Moldero-Magallanes, a Baguio artist and apothecary whose paintings are playful and personal.

Their project, Roots in Transformation, is part of Ibagiw 2026’s theme, RIKUS: A Creative Circular Baguio, which explores sustainability, renewal, and the creative reuse of materials.

But this collaboration goes beyond matching paintings with beautifully plated food.

MATCH. Chef Stanley Suva and artist Amparo Moldero-Magallanes present their kilawin alongside Of Dreams Cast at Sea. Photo by Mia Magdalena Fokno/Rappler

A little sweetness in the unexpected

The first surprise came with the kilawin.

The familiar Filipino dish had a welcome addition: camote. Its sweetness and texture worked remarkably well with the acidity of the kilawin, making an already enjoyable dish more interesting.

The kilawin was paired with Moldero-Magallanes’ Of Dreams Cast at Sea, a watercolor-and-ink illustration of fish, waves, and a fishing net carrying a paper boat.

The pairing was meaningful because neither artist nor chef had created their work for the other.

Another dish, Pinoy Chicken BBQ with Smoked Pineapple Salsa, came with a clever take on rice.

The familiar tutong, the browned rice that forms at the bottom of a cooking pot, was reimagined as Pinoy ampaw, a crispy rice cake made with Unoy heirloom rice from Pasil, Kalinga. Its crunch complemented the chicken barbecue and smoked pineapple salsa.

The dish was inspired by Moldero-Magallanes’ Of Crispy Steps and Borrowed Flight, a playful illustration of children, a paper boat, and a chicken against swirling colors and mountain forms.

Then came the strawberry cansi.

Cansi, a beef soup traditionally associated with Western Visayas, gets its sourness from batwan. Suva’s version introduces Benguet strawberries, bringing a distinctly local ingredient into the broth.

The result was addictive: the soup’s tang and the strawberries’ sweetness made for an unusual combination that worked.

Suva has explained that the restaurant uses underripe strawberries, less suited for desserts, in its cansi. It is one way the kitchen makes use of ingredients that might otherwise go to waste.

The accompanying artwork, Of a Strawberry and a Floating Cow, features a strawberry hanging beneath a fanciful scene of clouds, mountains, and a floating cow.

Dessert brought another surprise.

The chocolate mousse came with a rose element that added freshness to the rich chocolate. Inspired by Of Leather Towers and Sweet Rivers, the dish played with layered textures, with the fruit leather and mousse echoing the painting’s towers and flowing forms.

It was a lovely end to a meal that kept us curious about what would arrive next.

ART. Moldero-Magallanes’ paintings adorn the walls of Alapaap Dining at Mt. Camisong, bringing her imaginative landscapes, colors, and storytelling into the restaurant. Photo by Mia Magdalena Fokno/Rappler

Returning to the easel

There is a personal story behind the paintings.

Moldero-Magallanes grew up with artist parents and began painting as a child. As life and work took over, however, her creative pursuits gradually moved into the background.

For years, her artwork appeared on the packaging of products from her small business. Upon reaching her golden years, she decided it was time to return to painting and share her work more widely.

She describes her style as whimsical and dreamlike, shaped by her parents’ influence and her desire to bring viewers back to simpler, happier memories.

For this year’s collaboration, she also experimented with materials that might otherwise have been discarded.

Expired Abra dyes became watercolor palettes, while rejected materials from soap production were turned into paint. Old glitter dyes were incorporated into acrylics, and existing canvases were given new life.

Her background in medical technology, she explained, helped shape her resourcefulness and willingness to experiment.

Moldero-Magallanes also spoke warmly about the chefs she and her husband have befriended over the years.

She has long believed that chefs are artists in their own right, not only because of how food looks, but also because they create experiences through taste, texture, and memory.

A dish, she observed, can remind someone of a mother’s cooking or a particular moment in life.

Watching Suva connect his earlier kilawin with her painting gave that belief a personal meaning.

FUSION. Pinoy Chicken BBQ with Smoked Pineapple Salsa is served with ampaw, made from Unoy heirloom rice from Pasil, Kalinga, and inspired by the familiar tutong. The dish is paired with Moldero-Magallanes’ Of Crispy Steps and Borrowed Flight, an illustration featuring children, a chicken, and a paper boat. Photo by Mia Magdalena Fokno/Rappler

More than a beautiful plate

Suva shares her view of cooking. As a chef, he sees food as a form of artistic expression, with ingredients and cooking techniques serving much the same purpose as an artist’s materials and tools.

His interest in Moldero-Magallanes’ work deepened when he learned how she incorporated recycled materials into her paintings.

At Alapaap, his kitchen has been working to reduce food waste and find more uses for available ingredients.

Their collaboration offered a chance to bring these approaches together.

Mt. Camisong board chairperson Ludette Querubin acknowledged that sustainability remains a work in progress.

The organization, she said, continues to learn and improve its practices through partnerships with artists, chefs, and the surrounding community.

For Querubin, sustainability extends beyond environmental concerns to food, culture, livelihoods, and the people who make these initiatives possible.

That broader perspective is relevant in the Cordillera, where resourcefulness and making use of available materials have long been part of everyday life.

The collaboration also points to a possible direction for Baguio’s creative economy. Artists can reach new audiences through dining, while chefs introduce guests to local ingredients, cultural stories, and the work of other creatives.

Such collaborations could benefit both, provided they give participating artists meaningful recognition and support.

SWEET. A rose adds an unexpected floral touch to Chef Suva’s chocolate mousse, paired with Moldero-Magallanes’ Of Leather Towers and Sweet Rivers. Photo by Mia Magdalena Fokno/Rappler

A meal worth remembering

Gastro X Art has returned to Ibagiw, and this year’s pairing at Mt. Camisong shows why the collaboration deserves to continue.

The dishes were enjoyable on their own. What made the meal memorable was discovering the stories behind them, then looking at the paintings again and noticing details we had missed earlier.

The art did not feel like decoration added to a restaurant. Nor did the food seem like an afterthought to an exhibition.

Suva and Moldero-Magallanes found a way to let their individual works speak to each other, sometimes by design and, as with the kilawin, through coincidence.

Roots in Transformation runs from November 8 to 30, 2026, at Alapaap Dining in Mt. Camisong Forest Park, Sitio Peday, Barangay Loacan, Itogon, Benguet, as part of the Ibagiw Gastro X Art + Live Music Creative Crawl.

If you happen to visit, don’t rush through the meal. Look at the paintings, listen to the stories, and give the food your full attention.

Especially the strawberry cansi. I’d happily have another bowl. – Rappler.com

World.title: For ‘Sway’ singer Bic Runga, being a musician is the greatest job on earth
World.content:
Time and time again, music is what Bic has fallen back on for the past three decades — so much so that if it were to be taken away from her for whatever reason, she wouldn’t quite know what to do

Whenever kids are asked what they want to be when they grow up, it isn’t out of the ordinary to be told that they dream of becoming magicians, princesses, astronauts, or superheroes. And it’s just as normal when they end up pursuing something entirely different when they enter adulthood.

Not for Bic Runga, though.

Hailing from New Zealand, the acclaimed singer-songwriter has always known that being a musician was in the cards for her — a realization she’d made as early as 11 years old. What’s more, her mother was a singer, so car rides would usually turn into impromptu karaoke sessions of the top 40 songs on the radio at that time.

American and British music from the ’60s and ’70s continue to shape Bic’s sound as we know it. When she went on to write her first song on a whim at just 14 years old, she would never look back.

“It was just something I decided to do. It’s like a commitment. There are so many times where it wasn’t going well, but you just have to keep going because you decided to years ago,” Bic said.

And 30 years later, she’s still here.

Timelessness as a philosophy

Music is something that has become intertwined with the 50-year-old artist and everything she does. Time and time again, it’s what she’s fallen back on for the past three decades — so much so that if it were to be taken away from her for whatever reason, she wouldn’t quite know what to do.

“If you’re a really committed musician, it’s almost like if you don’t do it, you don’t feel right. I’ve been doing it for over 30 years, but I realize it makes me feel normal. If I’m not singing or making music, I always feel kind of stressed out,” the singer-songwriter explained.

Bic had just been a naive teenager on the cusp of her 20s when it came time for her to work on her debut studio album Drive.

It had been a rather chaotic time in her life, where everything had just seemed to be happening all at once. She had just been signed to a record label. She had just packed up her things to move from Christchurch to Auckland. Overwhelming as it was, she had surpassed it all by fully throwing herself into her craft.

“I was such a young, determined person,” Bic said, describing the state she was in while writing Drive. “I wasn’t thinking about the outcome. I was just thinking about doing a good job at the time.”

Since then, Bic has called several other places home. Outside of New Zealand, she has lived in London, New York, and most notably, Paris, where much of her latest record Red Sunset was made.

She was just in her mid-20s when she relocated to the city of love. Coming back to the French capital 25 years later, it almost seems as if everything has changed.

“There’s all these apocalyptic things happening, so there was lots to reflect on and write about because so much time has passed and I’ve been going for such a long time that I wanted to connect again with how I felt about things when I was younger,” she said about the album.

But all these years later, Bic’s core has pretty much remained the same. She attests that she still has the same objectives and values, and still can’t quite even believe she’s here. Perhaps it’s why timelessness seems to be the great big quality her music has always taken on.

“I’m always trying to [make something timeless] because I’m sort of old,” Bic quipped.

“I don’t think I can try to chase the trends and I don’t think it’s a good idea to do that. Even if you’re young, actually, because usually if you’re trying to copy something that’s happening right at the same time as you, it’s too late by the time it comes out. So I’m always looking for that thing that makes any artwork timeless.”

Keeping human creativity alive

Obsession seems to be the habit the “Sway” singer hasn’t been able to separate herself from. It’s not something she’s looking to unlearn, though. In fact, it’s an essential part of her creative process as an artist. You’d often find her awake at odd hours just to finish recording, and it’s something she says she genuinely enjoys.

Bic is also a self-proclaimed perfectionist. She was the type to stop at nothing until the song sounded as good as it could be. But these days, things have changed.

BIC RUNGA. Photo by Tom Grut

These little flaws that used to send musicians like Bic over the edge are now thought of as treasures — and it’s all thanks (or no thanks) to the rise of generative artificial intelligence in creative spaces.

And if it’s traces of minor mistakes that allow humanity to shine through, even just a little bit, then Bic is all for it.

“I just still believe in human creativity. It’s kind of exciting that we have all these other digital tools and AI tools. But human expression is still the most important part of art. Wanting to express yourself and say something is kind of the essence of it, really. Even though it seems like a really hard time to go into art of any kind. But it’s still really important because in a way, nobody quite knows what’s real anymore. But art still is quite real. Because it’s just human expression.”

There are a lot of things Bic wishes she knew back then, like knowing how to read a contract, knowing how to preserve her energy better, and knowing how to nurture friendships and understand the people around her better.

All this wisdom eventually comes with age, though. But there’s one thing that doesn’t seem to get easier: navigating life in the spotlight.

BIC RUNGA. Photo by Tom Grut

“It always is a bit uncomfortable,” Bic confessed. “I just want to have a real life. I want to have real relationships. A lot of it can feel like you’re playing a role.”

In this day and age, privacy has become a novelty. It’s why the singer has learned to be okay with separating her musical identity from her private self, much as she loves her craft.

“Everyone is wearing their life in public, and not all of it is real. Hardly any of it’s real, actually. Everyone’s going through that same weirdness, I suppose.”

Still, Bic believes she’s the same person wherever she goes — her music serving as a reflection of that.

“I still like singing my old songs, and finding who I used to be in those old songs. I still think of that as the same person. It’s quite fun to sing something that you wrote when you were so much younger. You realize that that was always you,” she mused.

Thirty years down the line, it’s why Bic thinks being a musician is the greatest job on earth. While she admits the industry side of things can get difficult to navigate, music, for Bic, is the purest pastime out there. That’s what’s kept her going all these years — and that’s why she’s here to stay. – Rappler.com

World.title: Niño Alcantara, the ‘kuya’ of Philippine tennis, still enjoys the grind
World.content:
Filipino tennis veteran Niño Alcantara reflects on two decades of sacrifice, a historic junior Grand Slam triumph, and the life-changing perspective of fatherhood

Three days after becoming a father, Francis Casey “Niño” Alcantara had to leave his newborn son behind.

His wife, Meanne, gave birth on a Tuesday, and by Friday, Alcantara was already leaving for the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.

Though his wife approved of the trip, leaving was still difficult.

“I didn’t want to leave the baby,” Alcantara said, “But at the same time, I wanted to go play in the Asian Games.”

Yet, fatherhood ignited a fresh spark within him.

“I was playing for him every match,” Alcantara said. “It was all dedicated to my baby and my wife.”

Alcantara and his wife Meanne hold their baby’s ultrasound scans (top), and months later, they welcome their newborn son (right). All photos courtesy of Niño Alcantara

In Japan, his mixed-doubles run with Shaira Hope Rivera ultimately ended in the round of 16. Despite winning no medal, representing the country meant everything to him.

“It feels different playing for the flag,” the 34-year-old Alcantara said.

As the only veteran male athlete alongside four women in the Philippine tennis delegation, he also naturally embraced the role of a kuya (big brother).

“I am the kuya/bodyguard,” he said, laughing.

The Philippine tennis delegation at the 2026 Asian Games.

Long before the international rankings, the grueling travel schedules, and the responsibilities of fatherhood, Alcantara’s young life revolved around a wide variety of sports.

He was only four or five years old when he first picked up a tennis racket in Cagayan de Oro, but basketball, badminton, table tennis, and billiards were also among the regular sports he played.

“I was very athletic so I played most sports,” he said.

Alcantara even earned basketball MVP honors and maintained school honors from first to fifth grade. His father, however, saw a different path forward — seeing tennis as his son’s ultimate ticket to securing scholarships in Manila.

Alcantara, holding a ball, with the Xavier-Ateneo basketball team.

Tragedy struck when his father passed away when Alcantara was just in elementary.

“It was tough at first,” he recalled. “Like you know, not having a dad from 10 years old.”

Yet, the blueprint his father left behind kept him moving forward.

“I think overall if he was still alive, he’ll be very happy and proud of us,” he said.

Alcantara’s dad hands his medal Alcantara’s baby photos with his parents.

By his early teens, Alcantara left regular schooling behind for homeschooling through Xavier University-Ateneo de Cagayan so he could train full-time in Manila.

“I really had to sacrifice time, family, and friends,” he said. “So, that’s what I did. And yeah, I think it really paid off.”

From junior glory to professional grind

Those sacrifices bore historic fruit in 2009 when Alcantara captured the Australian Open junior boys’ doubles title alongside Taiwanese partner Hsieh Cheng-peng, with his mother proudly watching from the stands.

“Uy, first Filipino ka pala na nanalo and all (Hey, so you’re the first Filipino to win and all that),” Alcantara recalled people telling him. “It was a special moment. I didn’t know it was that big at first.”

Alcantara (right) and Hsieh Cheng-peng with their 2009 Australian Open juniors trophy.

The historic Grand Slam triumph skyrocketed him to No. 14 in the world junior rankings and opened the doors to numerous US college scholarship offers.

“Instead of begging the coaches, I had to pick a school na lang kung saan ako pupunta (I just had to pick a school to go to),” shared Alcantara, who went on to see action in the US NCAA, playing for Fresno State University (2011-2012) before transferring to Pepperdine University (2012-2014).

However, transitioning to the professional circuit in 2016 proved to be an entirely different beast.

“Tennis is super tough,” he said. “And it’s very hard to transition from juniors to pros.”

Alcantara poses with Alex Eala and her bronze medal during the 2026 Asian Games.

Alcantara had to grind through low-level tournaments just to qualify for bigger brackets. Yet, over a decade of relentless effort, he kept pushing — learning from every victory and setback alike.

Whether battling on the pro circuit or proudly representing the Philippines in international play — where he has won a mixed doubles bronze in the 2022 Asian Games and all medal colors in six Southeast Asian Games editions — his passion never wavered.

“I’m still here. I’m still grinding, I’m still ready to compete,” he said.

The final sets

Now a veteran of the sport, Alcantara estimates he has two or three years left in his competitive career, depending on how his body holds up.

Retirement, when it eventually comes, will mean less traveling and more time to consider what comes next.

For now, he is taking a well-deserved five- to six-week break to enjoy fatherhood before gearing up for a heavy 2027 schedule of 25 to 30 tournament weeks.

While leaving his newborn son again may be difficult, it gave Alcantara a new perspective on why he continues to compete.

“The fire and the love of the game is still there,” said Alcantara. “It’s still the same.” – Rappler.com

Jade Tan is a Rappler intern studying AB Journalism at University of Santo Tomas, Manila.

World.title: ‘Ayo Ayo sa Nangayo’ puts Bohol’s environmental struggle into perspective
World.content:
FOLKLORISH. 'Ayo Ayo sa Nangayo' follows the story of a school principal played by Marvin Ablao (left) and a tree-dwelling spirit portrayed by Angelo Vidal (right).

Through local folklore and the story of a century-old narra tree, the award-winning Bohol film asks how much of the environment humanity is willing to lose in the name of change

CEBU, Philippines – For generations at Jagna Central School in Bohol, a century-old narra tree stood as part of every student’s childhood.

More than a decade ago, the same tree was cut down over fear that it would fall on nearby buildings during typhoons. Students and alumni protested, even bringing their concerns to the municipality.

For most Boholanos, losing that tree meant losing a piece of their childhood.

This incident became the inspiration for Ayo Ayo sa Nangayo, a film by Boholano director Gerard Jamora, executive producer Pia Piquero, and writers Leon Junel Garsuta and Anne Paradiang.

The film took home the awards for Best Short Film, Best Director, Best Screenplay, and other major awards at the SINEBOHOL Film Festival 2026.

Developed during a SINEBOHOL filmmaking workshop in partnership with United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), the film explores environmental preservation and the cost of development through a story inspired by elements of Boholano folklore.

What began as an assigned theme, “Dili Ingon Ato (not like us),” eventually led Jamora back to the Jagna tree cutting incident. He saw in it an opportunity to tell a bigger story about how nature often “falls prey” to proposed developments that promise progress in communities.

At the center of the film is an Agta or a tree-dwelling spirit portrayed by Angelo Vidal whose home is cut down for the construction of a new classroom. The spirit then seeks help from the same principal, played by Marvin Ablao, who ordered its removal to find a new place to call home.

For Jamora, the story goes beyond the conflict between two characters. It is about people’s growing tendency to think only of themselves.

One line he hopes audiences remember is the Agta’s “Ija-ija, aho-aho” — a familiar Boholano expression that the film uses to describe how people prioritize what is theirs while overlooking what happens to everything around them.

“That’s the reality of human beings. It’s up to us on how we must find a solution to this,” Jamora said.

The cost of development

In May 2023, Bohol became the Philippines’ first UNESCO Global Geopark, recognizing its geological heritage and the importance of conserving its natural landscapes. Yet, the province continues to face environmental concerns, from tree-cutting applications in upland areas to controversies involving infrastructure projects.

One of the latest is the P3.5-billion Loboc River Protection Project, which has drawn scrutiny from provincial lawmakers, residents, and tourism stakeholders.

Critics have raised concerns over the installation of steel sheet piles and the removal of natural riverbank vegetation, warning of possible consequences for biodiversity, firefly habitats, and the river’s tourism appeal.

The controversy surrounding the Captain’s Peak Resort in March 2024, which was built on the foot of Chocolate Hills in Sagbayan town, Bohol, also raised questions about environmental regulation.

YONDER. “The film balances humor with genuine stakes, giving the Agta (tree spirit) dignity while modernizing the oral fable into an accessible, short film,” Dennis Judilla, an official juror of the 2026 Sine Bohol Film Festival, said in his review of the film. Photo from Gerard Jamora

Piquero shared her frustration over the increasing number of private developers seeking permission to cut trees in upland areas, noting that while some applications are questioned or deferred, others are approved without delay.

“[Just] because you don’t feel the impact of environmental danger doesn’t mean that it does not happen,” she said.

In the film, the Agta’s displacement from its home — the ancestral tree — despite not being directly visible to human characters, reminds audiences that environmental destruction affects more than what people can immediately see. For Piquero, this was also what made the story personal.

“When I write stories, I want it to be human or connect it to humans, and after pitching the story, I got so invested in it,” she shared.

There is still time

For Jamora, he hopes that Ayo Ayo sa Nangayo reaches audiences beyond Bohol and encourages them to become more critical of the environmental changes happening around them.

While the film draws from an incident in Jagna, the filmmaker believes its message remains relevant to the wider realities of environmental development and preservation.

“We hope our message resonates with the audience, because that is the goal, to let people know that this tree-cutting issue is still very much relevant,” Jamora highlighted.

He also hopes the film reminds viewers that there is still time to protect the environment.

“The film is about how we want to tell the audience that it’s not too late as human beings. We need to preserve what was given to us by nature,” Jamora said. – Rappler.com

Joshua Eli Narajos is a Cebu-based Mover and a communication student from the University of the Philippines in Cebu.

World.title: [Two Pronged] My husband’s porn consumption seems extreme
World.content:
'Is it normal — as my husband says and that I should just accept — that he watches pornography all the time?'

Rappler’s People section runs an advice column by couple Jeremy Baer and clinical psychologist Dr. Margarita Holmes.

Jeremy has a master’s degree in law from Oxford University. A banker of 37 years who worked in three continents, he has been training with Dr. Holmes for the last 10 years as co-lecturer and, occasionally, as co-therapist, especially with clients whose financial concerns intrude into their daily lives.

Together, they have written two books: Love Triangles: Understanding the Macho-Mistress Mentality and Imported Love: Filipino-Foreign Liaisons.

Dear Dr Holmes and Mr Baer,

I don’t know if you remember me, but five years ago, we had three video calls. I am Maria, from Turkey. I had a French partner and you helped me deal with him better.

I left my French boyfriend. I now have a husband. He is also French. I also need help with him.

Is it normal — as my husband says and that I should just accept — that he watches pornography all the time? He finishes work at lunchtime and when he comes home and I am cooking, he is watching porn. When he finishes his lunch and I am washing our dishes, he watches porn.

My husband leaves the house before 5 am so he is not late for his work. It starts before 6 am. This is why he is tired so right after lunch, he takes a nap. Before he takes a nap, he watches porn because he says it helps him relax. He even saves many of the pictures he sees. Many of these girls are nude, and some of them are so extreme, with their legs wide open, and their tongues always licking their lips or something that looks like a penis.

I do not like it. But if it is normal, I have to accept it. What should I do? Please help.

– Maria

Dear Maria,

Thank you for your message.

Now that almost anybody can access the internet, pornography is freely available, ubiquitous, and can be viewed anonymously. This has radically altered attitudes towards porn and in many circles it is no longer viewed as negatively as previously.

This is not to say that porn consumption is necessarily harmless. Although in some cases it can satisfy sexual curiosity, alleviate stress or boredom, combat loneliness, heavy usage can on the other hand influence sexual preferences, undermine trust and reduce intimacy in relationships, leading to feelings of inadequacy and even emotional abandonment.

Secrecy surrounding usage is also problematic, though this is not apparently an issue in your case, Maria.

It seems that your husband is quite open about his use of porn. He claims it helps him relax and sleep. Why he saves all those pictures however is perhaps less clear. The question then is: what is your objection to it?

For example, is it a matter of principle for you; do you believe all porn use is by definition bad? Is it that it has altered his sexual habits e.g. he wants to copy what he sees in videos? Is it perhaps that porn has reduced his ardor or increased his desire for novelty?

How has it affected your relationship? Has it changed his attitude towards you and if so, in what way? Has it reduced the intimacy between you? How else does it manifest?

Once you have a clearer idea of the answers to these and any related questions, then you will have a basic framework for another conversation with him about how his use of porn impacts both you individually and you as a couple.

This conversation should be non-judgmental and avoid blame, with each listening to the other’s point of view so as to understand and discern where future boundaries might be established. You might even consider counseling.

If this does not yield a compromise that you find comfortable and acceptable, you will need to weigh the pros and cons. Should he be unwilling to change significantly, are the negatives of his porn use something you can just live with? Alternatively, do they undermine your marriage to the extent that you want to take action?

An open and frank conversation aimed at improving mutual understanding and exploring options can hopefully bring greater intimacy and deepen your relationship.

Best wishes,

– JAF Baer

Dear Maria,

Thank you very much for your letter, and yes, I remember you with great fondness. I am glad you decided to write Two Pronged. This way, Mr Baer’s insights will also be included.

I agree with what he says about trying to understand what porn truly means to you. This would include not only your present — something totally unacceptable, his insisting you both try things he’s seen and insisting you try together things you do not want to? — but also your past — what you observed while growing up, what you were taught, etc.

I feel how I can help you most is to encourage what Mr Baer suggested, which is to explore more deeply “how (his porn watching) affected your relationship? And also “has it reduced the intimacy between you?”

At present, your relationship is unequal; where your husband (let’s call him Nathan) gets to say what normal is, with your having to accept it as normal and therefore, acceptable, because of nothing more than his opinion.

Your writing to Two Pronged shows a step in the right direction: wanting an outside resource to verify your “suspicions” vis-à-vis Nathan’s pronouncement that porn is normal.

For the avoidance of doubt it need not be Two Pronged per se that makes it the correct step, but any other resource that is both evidence-based and clearly distinguishes between science and mere opinion.

Perhaps, a realistically accessible guide for any person to gauge their partner’s “normality” would be the 5-D’s framework professors in Abnormal Psychology share with their undergrad students.

These include:

Deviance: Is Nathan’s porn watching significantly different from societal, cultural, or statistical norms? Not that being deviant is enough to label something as inherently a disorder. For example, possessing not just Patis Tesoro’s unsurpassed creativity but the grit and hard work to make such designs a reality is “deviant” (but not a disorder). That is the reason she is a national artist and we are not. This does NOT seem a relevant issue in your case.

Danger: Behaviors that pose a risk of harm to either Nathan or to others (like yourself) e.g. suicide ideation, aggressive violence etc. which would require immediate attention. This does NOT seem a relevant issue in your case (at the moment).

Dysfunction: resulting in a person’s inability to handle daily life e.g. working or maintaining relationships. This is a relevant issue in your case, as it is affecting the quality of your marriage.

Distress: The emotional pain, suffering, or anguish the behavior or condition causes the individual. This does NOT seem a relevant issue in your case, because the distress mentioned here refers only to Nathan. One might even comment that distress seems the very opposite of what Nathan feels when he watches porn.

Duration: How long the symptoms or behaviors have lasted. Temporary emotional reactions to a stressful life event are normal, whereas porn watching that persists continuously over an extended period points toward a clinical disorder. This does NOT seem a relevant issue here since this only focuses on how long your husband has been watching porn, not you.

If you can move beyond asking a credible resource what normal is, and have the confidence to ask yourself what you would consider normal in a marriage, then that would be a bigger/better step towards achieving even better mental health!

That saying, “What is normal for the spider is chaos for the fly,” fits your situation perfectly!

You do not have to have an evidence-based, ultra logical reason for not wanting to experience your Nathan’s constant porn watching. Everyone in your barkada (friend group) may think it ok, but the fact that you do not, that it causes you distress, is enough reason to talk about it with Nathan and find a solution acceptable to both of you.

In my clinical experience, a marriage where both partners feel safe because they feel loved is a relationship that does not insist on outside experts to convince the other an issue is worth focusing on.

If it distresses one’s partner, that alone is sufficient reason to try and find solutions that work for you both. All you need to say is “This makes me sad/angry/feel humiliated, please stop” to the partner. Because he loves and respects his wife, he will at the very least try. Nathan is definitely not at that stage yet.

How long you want to wait until he does…IF he does…depends entirely on you. That decision can be difficult. Please remember, dearest Maria, that we are right here to help you make it should you want us to.

Wishing you the clarity and courage to decide what is best for you.

– MG Holmes

Life got complicated? Write to our Two Pronged duo at twopronged@rappler.com.

World.title: Gifting with a purpose: Filipino brands doing more than just selling
World.content:
Every holiday season, we remember that the most important thing about gifts is making our recipients feel seen and special. There’s nothing quite like watching joy bloom on someone’s face as you hand them something they’ve always wanted or that makes their life easier. There’s also nothing quite like using your gift to support others along the way. What if your gift could help the sick, or stop rivers from being clogged? What if your gift could give back to a community in need?



Apparel and fabric from Anthill

Standing for “Alternative Nest and Trading/Training Hub for Indigenous or Ingenious Little Livelihood seekers”, true to their name, they help our indigenous groups have a space and name in the market. This is the place if you’re looking to gift stylish woven apparel, accessories, home decor, or even whole fabric by the meter, along with custom orders and alterations. Moreover, Anthill has sustainable zero-waste programs: bringing life back into scrap fabric via their reweave project, accepting unwanted fabric in their circulatory hub, and offering lifetime repairs and consults. So in a world of fast fashion, rest assured any gift you buy from them will reduce fabric waste and last long-term.

Get them here:

https://anthillmarkets.com/

https://anthillfabrics.com/

Lifesaver Watches by LoveHopeFaith Group

For over a decade, LoveHopeFaith Group has been helping people fight the Big C— cancer— with charities and donations. Their Lifesaver watches are not only affordable, classic, and stylish, but 50% of their proceeds go to their sponsored cancer patients.

Get them here:

https://lovehopefaithgroup.com

Creative works from Kâtha Pilipinas

As cheesy as it sounds, art brings us together. And we wouldn’t have art without the people behind it who trained their craft to show their hearts. Kâtha is one such place that supports local artists. If you’re looking for everything about art, from illustration to artisanal works and fashion, you can find it at Kâtha, and it goes beyond putting their work on the market: Kâtha also does training, workshops, advocacy campaigns, and brings their artists’ voices to policy reworks.

Visit their instagram page here.

Cara Welfare is an animal welfare organization that cares for stray cats and dogs. While we don’t recommend gifting pets, we definitely recommend sponsoring care for a furry friend or two in the giftee’s name. And hey, in the future, your giftee can foster on their own terms, or adopt them into a fur-ever home.

Visit their website here.

Leatherworks from Jacinto and Lirio

The water hyacinth is a non-endangered aquatic plant notable for its rapid reproduction… and the invasive effects of its proliferation on the ecosystem and living communities. To help keep its population in check, Jacinto and Lirio source their plant-based leather from the water hyacinth and turn it into a variety of leatherworks, like accessories, bags, and stationery. They also provide custom orders.

A shameless plug. There’s no shame in supporting the press, so why not gift a subscription to independent investigative journalism? It also comes with audio articles, exclusive articles, and, depending on your plan, discounts on other Rappler media and exclusive events. You can also gift one-time donations in your giftee’s name.

https://www.rappler.com/plus/

https://support.rappler.com

Whichever gift you choose from this list, you’ll know it’s a gift that gives back in the Filipino spirit. – Rappler.com

This piece was written by Rappler intern Czarina Yasmin Sia. Czarina is an earnest creator whose works focuses on the little things and helping others. She enjoys engaging with unconventional ways to tells stories and is eager to write about life’s overlooked aspects. A graduating Communication Arts student from De La Salle University Manila, she aims to inspire people to find wonder.

World.title: Act on environmental woes, learn from Yolanda catastrophe, says church
World.content:
Tacloban City Mayor Alfred Romualdez leads the 13th year commemoration of the onslaught of Super Typhoon Yolanda on Sunday, Nov. 8, as he urges residents to never forget the lessons of the monster typhoon that killed over 2,200 people in the city. (INQUIRER / Joey A. Gabieta)

TACLOBAN CITY — The Roman Catholic Diocese of Borongan called on communities to take concrete action against environmental destruction and protect vulnerable populations, saying the lessons of Super Typhoon Yolanda (international name: Haiyan) should result in greater responsibility toward the environment.

In a pastoral message issued on Sunday, coinciding with the 13th anniversary of Yolanda’s onslaught, the diocese urged the faithful to adopt the Church’s approach of “see, judge, and act” in responding to what it described as an increasingly urgent environmental emergency.

“Remembering is not enough. Yolanda asks something of us today, in the midst of an environmental emergency that grows more urgent each year,” said the message signed by Rev. Fr. Jan Michael Gadicho, diocesan administrator.

Article continues after this 

The diocese said the devastation caused by Yolanda in 2013 should not only remind people of the suffering and fear experienced during the disaster but also of the resilience, solidarity and generosity that helped communities rebuild.

It also expressed gratitude to individuals, communities, institutions and organizations that extended assistance to survivors, while entrusting the souls of the victims to God and offering prayers for their grieving families.

Confront, act on eco woes

However, the message stressed that the anniversary should also prompt people to confront continuing environmental problems, including destructive mining, stronger storms, rising sea levels, coastal erosion and the destruction of livelihoods.

Citing Pope Francis’ encyclical Laudato Si’, the diocese said the suffering of the environment is closely linked to the suffering of poor communities, who are often the first and most severely affected by environmental destruction despite contributing least to the crisis.

Article continues after this 

Under the call to “judge,” the Church urged the faithful to view environmental protection as a moral responsibility, emphasizing that the Earth is a gift entrusted by the Creator and not a resource to be exploited.

It also cited the biblical passage in Genesis 2:15, which calls on people to cultivate and care for the Earth.

Article continues after this 

The diocese further called for concrete actions, including opposing destructive mining, planting and protecting trees and mangroves, reducing waste, preparing families and parishes for disasters, and supporting vulnerable communities.

It also encouraged residents to make their voices heard in support of just and responsible environmental policies, beginning with initiatives in their homes, schools, parishes and communities.

“Learning from the impact of Yolanda, we may be compelled to see, to judge, and to act,” the message said.

Yolanda in Tacloban City

Tacloban City Mayor Alfred Romualdez also led a commemoration rite on Sunday.

He urged residents to remember the lessons of Super Typhoon Yolanda, particularly the importance of preparedness and early evacuation,

Speaking at a commemoration at Holy Cross Memorial Garden, where about 2,200 victims were buried in a mass grave, he also expressed gratitude to the international community and the national government for helping the city recover.

Super Typhoon Yolanda struck Eastern Visayas on Nov. 8, 2013, unleashing powerful winds and massive storm surges that devastated coastal communities, particularly in Eastern Samar, Leyte and Tacloban City.

World.title: Clans in Lanao del Sur rido to face frustrated murder raps
World.content:
Security forces halt vehicular traffic at the national highway after warring families clashed in Picong, Lanao del Sur on Saturday, Nov. 7. (Photo by 64th Infantry Battalion)

CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY – Authorities will file criminal charges against two warring families that clashed on Saturday in Picong, Lanao del Sur, which stranded hundreds of motorists for several hours along the national highway connecting the cities of Pagadian and Cotabato.

Col. Caezar Cabuhat, Lanao del Sur Provincial Police Office director, said that frustrated murder charges are being prepared for filing on Monday, after three responding soldiers were injured in the rido or clan war.

In a statement, the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (PRO-BAR) said the skirmishes erupted between the rival Labao and Gaosil families, both from Barangay Biosong, Picong.

Article continues after this 

Cabuhat said police and military forces under the 64th Infantry Battalion (IB) responded to the gunfight between the two warring families but was met with heavy gunfire.

Maj. Noelio Brigole Jr., spokesperson for the Philippine Army’s 1st Infantry “Tabak” Division, said that three soldiers were wounded after gunmen positioned on the mountainous terrain surrounding Picong Tunnel fired at them.

The 40-meter road tunnel built by the Americans during World War II in Barangay Manabilang, Picong town, is a major link connecting Pagadian and Cotabato cities.

“We had to halt vehicular traffic when the fighting intensified last Saturday afternoon for the safety of the motorists,” Cabuhat said.

Brigole said a joint team of soldiers from the 64IB and police officers from the Picong Municipal Police Station responded to pacify the warring families after residents reported the clash at around 3:00 p.m. Saturday.

Article continues after this 

He said the responding soldiers and police officers were met with heavy gunfire, which included rounds from .50-caliber machine guns.

“We deployed more troops to secure the Picong Tunnel, and by 8:00 p.m., the highway was cleared and vehicles were allowed to pass through,” Brigole told the Inquirer on the phone Sunday.

Article continues after this 

The wounded were identified as Privates First Class Jude Deligero, Reymond Padawan, and Cupid Val Masibog Mosque, all belonging to the Army’s 64IB. /gsg

World.title: Hontiveros expects Sara Duterte to attend OVP budget deliberations
World.content:
Sara Duterte (left) and Risa Hontiveros —OVP PHOTO / FILE

MANILA, Philippines – Sen. Risa Hontiveros on Sunday said she expects Vice President Sara Duterte to attend the budget deliberations of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) just like the heads of other government agencies do.

“I expect her to appear, that was explicitly mentioned by Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian during the committee hearing of the OVP budget. We expect heads of agencies to be present during committee hearings up to the plenary,” Hontiveros said in an interview on radio dzBB.

“When they’re absent, we take note of that and we tell them we expect them at least during the plenary. I also said that to other attached agencies of the [Department of Social Welfare and Development] during our budget hearing recently. VP Duterte is not being singled out,” she added.

Article continues after this 

READ: Sara Duterte snubs Senate hearing on OVP budget

Last Oct. 20, the Senate Finance Subcommittee, citing parliamentary courtesy, swiftly approved on committee level the OVP’s proposed budget amounting to P785.2 million.

Duterte was a no-show at the budget briefing, but she was represented by her chief of staff, lawyer Zuleika Lopez, who said that the vice president was representing his father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, at the inurnment of a long-serving city planner in Davao City.

In response, Gatchalian said he hoped to see Duterte once the OVP’s budget is being debated upon in session, saying agency heads are normally expected to defend their own funding requests.

If Duterte decides not to attend, Hontiveros said, “I’m sure we will take note of that because that is not the proper conduct of any head of agency even if, or especially if, it’s the VP.”

Article continues after this 

The senator explained that since Congress holds the power of the purse, it also has the privilege and the obligation to scrutinize the proposed budget of government agencies because these funds come from taxpayers’ money.

Hontiveros said she also sees no conflict with Duterte’s attendance at the OVP budget deliberations and the Senate impeachment court’s subjudice rule, saying the trial is a separate legislative proceedings from the budget-making process. /ms

World.title: PNP chief orders cybercrime probe into socmed account impersonating him
World.content:
The Philippine National Police (PNP) has launched a cybercrime probe into a fraudulent Facebook account posing as its chief, while cautioning the public against fake social media profiles impersonating police officials. —Photo from PNP

Article continues after this 

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) ordered a cybercrime investigation into a fake Facebook account using its chief’s identity and warned the public against fraudulent social media accounts impersonating police officials.

The warning followed the discovery of a fake Facebook account bearing the name “Jose Melencio Corpus” and using the photograph of PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr.

In a statement on Sunday, Nartatez condemned the unauthorized use of his identity and directed the Anti-Cybercrime Group (ACG) to immediately investigate and identify the individual or group behind the impersonation account.

Article continues after this 

“This is a deliberate attempt to misuse my identity and exploit the public’s trust in the Philippine National Police,” he said.

“We will not allow anyone to use the name of the PNP or its officials to deceive, intimidate, or take advantage of any of our kababayan (fellow citizens),” he added.

Article continues after this 

Nartatez also instructed the PNP-ACG to coordinate with Meta for account verification, preservation of digital evidence, and the prompt takedown of the fraudulent profile.

The PNP urged the public not to accept friend requests, engage in conversations, or respond to requests involving money, personal data, or favors coming from unverified accounts claiming to represent police officials.

Furthermore, they advised citizens who encounter suspicious accounts posing as police officials to preserve screenshots and other relevant information as evidence.

Police regional offices and local police units were likewise instructed to strengthen monitoring efforts against fake social media accounts impersonating police officials. /ms

World.title: Storm Cempaka retains strength ahead of PAR entry
World.content:
Image from the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration

MANILA, Philippines — Severe Tropical Storm Cempaka maintained its strength on Sunday morning ahead of its expected entry into the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR), when it will be given the local name Samuel, according to the weather bureau.

In its 11 a.m. bulletin, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said Cempaka was last estimated 1,720 kilometers east of extreme northern Luzon as of 10 a.m.

READ: Severe tropical storm may enter PAR Sunday night or early Monday

Article continues after this 

It was carrying maximum sustained winds of 110 kilometers per hour (kph) and gusts of up to 135 kph. It was moving westward at 25 kph.

Pagasa said Cempaka “will continue moving generally west-northwestward until it enters the PAR between this evening and Monday early morning.”

Once inside the PAR, it will be given the local name Samuel, becoming the country’s 19th tropical cyclone this year.

“The TC [tropical cyclone] will briefly stay inside the PAR, as it is forecast to begin to turn north-northeastward by Monday afternoon or evening and exit through the northeastern boundary of the PAR,” it added.

READ: ‘Very strong’ El Niño now active in tropical Pacific, says Pagasa

Article continues after this 

Pagasa said Cempaka is forecast to intensify into a typhoon on Sunday but weaken by Tuesday.

Although it is not directly affecting the country, the northeast monsoon will cause moderate to rough sea conditions over the seaboards of Northern and Central Luzon within the next 24 hours. /mcm

World.title: Sara Duterte conviction unlikely to spark mass protests – Ridon
World.content:
Vice President Sara Duterte. Photo from Inday Sara Duterte Facebook page.

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte’s conviction is unlikely to spark massive protests, with a survey showing that half of Filipinos would accept the Senate Impeachment Court’s ruling, according to Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon.

Ridon, one of the prosecutors in Duterte’s trial, said the vice president’s supporters may instead rally support online rather than stage protests.

“There will likely be a gathering on social media for this, but I cannot say for certain if there will be physical rallies or gatherings across different parts of the Philippines,” he said in Filipino at the Saturday News Forum.

Article continues after this 

A Social Weather Stations survey released last month showed that 51 percent of Filipinos believe the Senate’s decision should be accepted.

READ: First of 25 witnesses for VP Sara Duterte defense backs out

“So if that’s the case, the slim majority view, I would expect there to be no public support for any protest actions in favor of the vice president if she gets convicted,” Ridon said.

Duterte’s trial will resume on Monday, Nov. 9.

Her defense team is set to present evidence rebutting the prosecution’s charge that the vice president amassed unexplained wealth and failed to truthfully disclose her assets while in office. /mcm

World.title: PCG recovers 1.66 kgs of oil-contaminated waste in Bataan oil spill
World.content:
The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) has transitioned to monitoring operations in Barangay Ipag, Mariveles, Bataan, after its active response efforts recovered 1,660 kilograms of oil-contaminated waste as of Nov. 7. —Photo from PCG

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) has shifted to monitoring operations in Barangay Ipag, Mariveles, Bataan, after recovering 1,660 kilograms of oil-contaminated materials from the affected area as of Saturday, Nov. 7, following an active oil spill response.

Article continues after this 

In an update on Saturday, the PCG said the 83 sacks of recovered waste had been transported to a local transfer station in Mariveles for temporary storage.

The recovered materials will later be turned over to an accredited oily waste collector and a treatment, storage, and disposal facility.

About 2 p.m. on Saturday, the PCG and the Mariveles Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office jointly inspected the waters surrounding the affected area and found no visible traces of oil on the water’s surface.

Fishermen on Wednesday, Nov. 4, discovered approximately 25 liters of crude or used oil and alerted the PCG Station in Bataan.

Following the alert, the PCG deployed an oil boom to stop the oil from spreading to nearby coastal communities.

Article continues after this 

The PCG, together with the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, deployed seven absorbent booms and 2,200 absorbent pads for the cleanup.

Read: Mariveles investigates oil spill report

Article continues after this 

Guillermo Mangayao, a staff member of the Mariveles Municipal Agriculture Office, said the source of the oil slick remains unknown.

Earlier, the PCG said initial findings suggested that the substance came from washing activities, but its exact source has yet to be confirmed. /ms

World.title: 13 years after Yolanda, Borongan diocese warns vs destructive mining
World.content:
DEVASTATION Residents of Tacloban City sift through debris after Supertyphoon “Yolanda” hit Leyte province in November 2013. —RICHARD REYES

MANILA, Philippines — Thirteen years after Super Typhoon Yolanda (international name: Haiyan) wreaked havoc in parts of Visayas, the Diocese of Borongan has called on the faithful to reject destructive mining, emphasizing that remembering the tragedy is not enough.

In its message on Sunday, the Diocese of Borongan remembered the tragic incident that killed people, damaged communities, and left scars among families. It then thanked the Lord and the people who extended their generosity for the victims to rebuild their lives.

“But remembering is not enough. Yolanda asks something of us today, in the midst of an environmental emergency that grows more urgent each year. The Church gives us a way to respond: see, judge, and act,” the diocese said.

Article continues after this 

READ: Why ‘Yolanda’ was so deadly

Yolanda, one of the most powerful storms to ever hit the Philippines, left 6,300 dead and 1,061 missing.

The country lost more than P95 billion in damage to infrastructure and agriculture in its devastation in November 2013.

The diocese urged the faithful to see the suffering of our nation, noting how our islands are “exploited by mining, stronger storms, rising seas, eroded coasts, destroyed livelihoods and families who must rebuild again and again.”

With this, it said that the earth is a gift of God entrusted to mankind that should be cherished and not exploited. It also emphasized that the cry of the earth is a “cry for justice and stewardship.”

Article continues after this 

READ: This Taclobanion lived to tell the story of Yolanda

It called on Filipino Catholics to care more for the environment, and rally for the cause of those who are most affected by natural calamities and man-made disasters.

Article continues after this 

“Let us act with care for our common home: reject destructive mining, plant and protect trees and mangroves, reduce waste, prepare our families and parishes for disasters, support those most vulnerable, and make our voices be heard for just and responsible policies,” the diocese said.

“Let us begin in our homes, parishes, schools, and communities,” it added. /ms

World.title: Myanmar Regime Plans April Vote in 55 Constituencies Despite Continued Clashes
World.content:
Myanmar’s regime plans to hold elections in 55 constituencies across 37 townships on April 4, 2027, including 12 townships where it has regained at least partial control from resistance forces in recent years. Voting was not held in those 12 townships during the regime’s general election in December 2025 and January 2026, which was widely dismissed as a sham.

In an announcement Thursday, the regime said it would hold voting in 34 Lower House constituencies, using the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system; five Upper House constituencies; and 16 regional/state parliament constituencies across the country.

The townships include Tonzang and Falam in northern Chin State and Tigyaing, Banmauk and Indaw in Sagaing Region, all recaptured by the regime this year, as well as Singu and Mogoke in Mandalay Region, which it recaptured in 2025.

Also included on the regime’s list of townships scheduled to vote in April are Sagaing’s Kawlin, which the Myanmar military recaptured in 2024, and the Sagaing resistance strongholds of Pale, Yinmarbin, Shwebo and Taze.

A military analyst pointed out that the regime only controls the towns in Pale, Yinmarbin, Shwebo, Taze, Tigyaing, Banmauk and especially Indaw.

“The regime wants to show it is able to control the whole country, and that its administration is operating,” said Zin Yaw, a military defector who has monitored Myanmar’s conflicts since defecting after the coup.

The absence from the list of southern Chin State towns that the regime has been trying to retake since May 2026, as well as Arakan Army-controlled towns in Rakhine State, amounts to an admission by the regime that it hasn’t been able to restore its authority in these areas, he said.

The regime announced Lower House elections in Myeik, Tanintharyi Region; Nyaunglebin, Pauk Khaung and Padaung in Bago Region; Chauk and Minbu in Magwe Region; Pyin Oo Lwin, Meiktila, Natogyi, Singu and Mogoke in Mandalay Region; Kyaikmayaw in Mon State; Mayangone, Shwepyithar, Hlegu, Tamwe, Cocokyun and Hlaing Tharyar in Yangon Region; Kyaukme, Monghpyak, and Mong Pan in Shan State; Maubin in Ayeyarwady Region; and Zabuthiri, Dekkhinathiri and Ottarathiri in Naypyitaw.

The Upper House constituencies on the list are in Kachin State, Chin State, Magwe Region, Bago Region and Mandalay Region.

The list also includes state/regional parliament constituencies in Tonzang and Falam in Chin State; Tigyaing, Banmauk, Indaw, Kawlin, Pale, Yinmarbin, Taze and Shwebo in Sagaing Region; Zigon and Thegon in Bago Region; Natogyi, Singu and Mogoke in Mandalay Region; and Yegyi in Ayeyarwady Region.

The Myanmar military recently suffered heavy losses to resistance ambushes in Indaw Township. Clashes continue there and in upper Sagaing.

Despite the ongoing armed conflicts in many areas, political parties cooperating with the regime’s electoral process said they are making preparations for the vote.

Saw Than Myint, joint secretary of the Shan and Ethnic Democratic Party (SNDP), which secured 37 seats in the regime-backed general election, said the party plans to compete in the upcoming by-election but is still discussing details.

People’s Pioneer Party (PPP) chair Saw Han Aye said the party hopes to field candidates in at least one-third of the 55 constituencies, as required under the Political Parties Registration Law for parties competing at the national level.

He acknowledged that security concerns remain in some areas, adding that participation would ultimately depend on individual candidates’ willingness.

The PPP was founded by Thet Thet Khine, a former regime minister who was barred in October 2025 from running in the general election on grounds of violating rules on personal debts.

The Irrawaddy contacted People’s Party chair Ko Ko Gyi, a former 88 Generation student protest leader, about the party’s plans but received no response.

Coup leader Min Aung Hlaing’s regime organized the nationwide election in three phases in December 2025 and January 2026, with voting in 263 out of 330 townships. Civilian leaders, including Aung San Suu Kyi, remained imprisoned, while major opposition parties had been dissolved.

With only nine parties participating at the national level, the election was dominated by the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party (USDP) and allied parties, allowing the USDP to secure a majority of the seats.

Since installing himself as president in April, Min Aung Hlaing has launched a diplomatic campaign in an effort to gain legitimacy for his regime, visiting China, Russia, Belarus, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia and India, while his military forces continue targeting civilians in attacks and atrocities. The absence of elections in the 55 constituencies has underlined his regime’s lack of legitimacy, observers say.

World.title: Over 2m Myanmar Migrants in Thailand Reject Regime’s Identity Document
World.content:
Over 2 million Myanmar migrant workers in Thailand have participated in a poll calling on the parallel National Unity Government (NUG) to issue identity documents amid a mass boycott of the regime’s new Certificate of Identity (CI) process.

The poll also aims to demonstrate to the Thai government that they recognize the NUG as their legitimate government, not the military regime.

Thailand hosts an estimated 4 million Myanmar workers, both documented and undocumented. Migrant worker groups estimate that at least 600,000 are required to apply for CIs in this round. However, most are staying away from the regime’s newly opened Thai CI centers in protest against new tax and remittance rules that critics condemn as extortion. To apply, workers must prove they have remitted 25 percent of their wages through official regime channels and paid 2 percent annual income tax. The vast majority are refusing, fearing payment would help fund the regime’s war on civilians while lending it political legitimacy.

Meanwhile, Thai opposition lawmakers and labor rights groups have urged the government to review or scrap the centers, branding them a threat to national security and sovereignty.

The workers themselves made their overwhelming opposition clear in a weeklong online poll launched Sunday by the Myanmar Migrant Workers’ Representative Coordinating Committee in Thailand (MMWRCCT). Many appealed to Thai authorities to grant them work and residency permits without the CI document.

The poll result reflected resounding support among migrant workers for an alternative identification process managed by the NUG, Khin Soe of the MMWRCCT told The Irrawaddy.

“The regime CI process is a trap to extract foreign currency and information for military conscription,” he said. “The workers know this, so they don’t want to apply.”

He said the poll result would be sent to the NUG’s Labour Department to push for worker ID issuance, while a separate workers’ online petition would be delivered to the Thai government.

“The Thai government may argue it has to cooperate with the regime on the CI process to ensure national security, but we are appealing to them on humanitarian grounds. If they need an alternative authority to issue identity documents, this poll shows that millions of workers want the NUG to do it. As guests living under Thai law, we are not making demands, we are simply presenting these results as a respectful request,” Khine Soe said.

Launched on October 18, the campaign and petition contain four requests, including the right to stay and work legally without a CI, and has drawn support from Thai labour rights groups and politicians.

Among them is MP Anuson Tamajai, a prominent economist who urged the government to review or cancel the CI centers, arguing their unchecked operations compromise national security and sovereignty.

Highlighting migrant workers’ indispensable role in Thailand’s economy, he also called for an investigation into whether demanding remittance and tax payments in exchange for ID certificates violates Thai law.

The Thailand Migration Reform group recently warned that allowing Naypyitaw to control migrant registration “undermines Thai sovereignty and fuels corruption.” It urged Thai authorities to revert to the Pink Card system for migrant workers.

On Friday, Thai Labor Minister Julapun Amornvivat told media after a meeting of the Foreign Workers Management Policy Committee that CIs are required by migrants’ countries of origin for identity verification, but the process operates entirely within Thai territory.

He said his ministry will send a formal letter to its regime counterpart expressing opposition to the mandatory remittance policy, arguing it undermines migrant worker rights and fails to align with international standards.

Dismissing the backlash, the cash-strapped regime has doubled down on its push to skim foreign currency from low-paid overseas workers. Newly appointed Labor Minister Maung Myint has threatened workers with legal action and a ban on returning home if they don’t make tax and remittance payments.

However, the boycott shows no sign of weakening, with only a trickle of applicants reported at the five CI centres across Thailand since they opened on October 14.

World.title: China Wields Carrot and Stick at Beijing Meet, Regime Seeks Elections in Shan, and More
World.content:
We’ll always hold your hand, Beijing promises Myanmar regime

“China will always be a strategic partner that Myanmar can rely on,” Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Myanmar investment minister Aung Kyaw Hoe on the sidelines of the 11th Lancang–Mekong Cooperation Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on Tuesday.

The reassurance came as part of a carrot-and-stick package amid alarm in Beijing over recent meetings between U.S. and Myanmar officials that seemed to augur the start of re-engagement.

The U.S. has released an Integrated Country Strategy for its mission in Myanmar, which identifies goals for expanding Washington’s diplomatic, economic and humanitarian influence in the country. Besides singling out scam networks, it also sets goals for boosting American exports to the impoverished war-torn country and gain access to Myanmar’s “bountiful” rare earth resources—besides aiming to “counter China’s influence.”

Myanmar is China’s most important external source of rare earth minerals and a major global source of heavy rare earth elements, particularly dysprosium and terbium, which are essential for electric cars, wind turbines, advanced electronics and military technologies. But mines are concentrated in areas beyond the reach of the regime in Kachin and Shan states.

Online scam operations have become a major point of convergence and competition in the two superpowers’ approach toward Myanmar. During the meeting with Aung Kyaw Hoe, Wang urged his regime to prevent the “resurgence of chaos” in Myawaddy, referring to the vast scam compounds that flourished there.

China grows impatient over stalled investment projects

But in the same meeting Wang applied plenty of stick, urging Myanmar’s regime to get a move on in realizing long-stalled projects that form part of the planned China–Myanmar Economic Corridor (CMEC) that would provide Beijing with overland access to the Indian Ocean. Wang told Aung Kyaw Hoe the two sides must “coordinate development and security” so they can “steadily advance” key CMEC projects.

Wang’s message echoed remarks made by his President Xi Jinping during regime leader Min Aung Hlaing’s visit to Beijing in June, when Xi also called for swift implementation of CMEC projects.

The corridor’s flagship schemes include the Kyaukphyu deep-sea port and special economic zone in Rakhine State and a planned railway linking Kyaukphyu with Yunnan via Mandalay and Muse. On China side, the railroad is already entering its final phase but on the Myanmar side fighting continues across many parts of the route.

Aung Kyaw Hoe promised the regime is doing all it can but, true to form, also used the occasion to beg for even more Chinese investment.

Border trade gates reopen as armed groups consolidate control

China has significantly eased restrictions on trade through several Myanmar border crossings controlled by Beijing-linked ethnic armed organizations, allowing fuel, medicines, construction materials and other previously banned goods to enter northern Shan and Kachin.

The move suggests China is adjusting its border policy to accommodate new realities on the ground, where it appears the military regime in Naypyitaw has permanently lost control. With Operation 1027, key border trade gates and routes in northern Shan fell into the hands of the ethnic Chinese Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA), and its erstwhile partner in the Brotherhood Alliance, the Ta’ang National Liberation Army (TNLA).

Beijing initially closed the crossings to pressure them into making peace with the generals, but trade has long resumed and is now growing exponentially.

According to Chinese Customs at the Mengding crossing with MNDAA-controlled Chinshwehaw, the total value of trade there and at nearby Mangka eached 4.92 billion yuan in the first eight months of this year, up 49.3 percent on-year.

Customs figures also show increased trade through Namhkam crossing controlled by the Ta’ang National Liberation Army, as well as through the Kyin San Kyawt gate controlled jointly by the Brotherhood Alliance in Muse Township, which once accounted for some 70 percent of cross-border trade. The regime still controls a couple of crossings in Muse, where it bans the import of fuel from China.
